cfad500210b7c17496294607654377aa346559f6.title: Light-Cell Polynomial Rate
cfad500210b7c17496294607654377aa346559f6.body:
Fix an overlap constant \(\epsilon\) with \(0<\epsilon\le 1/2\). The hybrid estimator is computable in the real-arithmetic model: there is a universal operation-count constant \(K>0\) such that, for every \(n\) and \(d\), a real-arithmetic program reading the hybrid count vector returns \(\widehat\tau_n^{\mathrm{hyb}}\) exactly and uses at most \(K d M(n)^4\) arithmetic and comparison operations.

Moreover, there exist constants \(C_\epsilon,c_\epsilon>0\), depending only on \(\epsilon\), such that for every sample size \(n\), alphabet size \(d\), law \(P\) on \(\{1,\ldots,d\}\times\{0,1\}\times\{0,1\}\), and sample law \(P^{\otimes n}\in\mathcal E_{n,d,\epsilon}\) as in Definition~\ref{obj:def:experiment-class}, if
\[
d\le c_\epsilon n\log n,
\]
then the light-cell contribution satisfies
\[
E_{P^{\otimes n}}\left[\left\{\widehat T_{\mathcal L}-\sum_{k\in\widehat{\mathcal L}_n}\phi(q_k)\right\}^2\right]
\le
C_\epsilon\left\{\frac{1}{n}+\frac{d^2}{n^2(\log n)^2}\right\}.
\]

a1e2b7df6dc136b12e8a9e2545126a65f242811c.title: Pilot Sandwich Bound
a1e2b7df6dc136b12e8a9e2545126a65f242811c.body:
Let \(L=\log(en)\). For a sample satisfying Assumption~\ref{obj:ass:iid-sampling} with single-observation law \(P\), let \(\widehat{\mathcal H}\) be the pilot heavy set at threshold \(t\), let \(\widehat{\mathcal L}=\widehat{\mathcal H}^{c}\), and write \(m_0=|I_0|\), \(B_-=tL/(2m_0)\), and \(B_+=2tL/m_0\).

For every \(K>0\) and \(c>0\), there exist constants \(t_0>0\), \(C>0\), and an integer cutoff \(N\) such that, for every \(t\ge t_0\), every \(n\ge N\), every dimension \(d\), every law \(P\) on the finite observation alphabet, and every iid sample law satisfying Assumption~\ref{obj:ass:iid-sampling}, if
\[
d\le c\,n\,L,
\]
then
\[
\Pr\!\left(\widehat{\mathcal H}\not\subseteq\{k:p_k\ge B_-\}\ \text{or}\ \widehat{\mathcal L}\not\subseteq\{k:p_k\le B_+\}\right)
\le C n^{-K}.
\]
Moreover, for every \(c>0\), there exist \(C>0\) and an integer cutoff \(N\) such that the same conclusion holds for all \(n\ge N\), \(d\le c\,n\,L\), laws \(P\), and iid sample laws satisfying Assumption~\ref{obj:ass:iid-sampling}, with \(t=256\) and \(K=4\):
\[
\Pr\!\left(\widehat{\mathcal H}\not\subseteq\{k:p_k\ge 256L/(2m_0)\}\ \text{or}\ \widehat{\mathcal L}\not\subseteq\{k:p_k\le 512L/m_0\}\right)
\le C n^{-4}.
\]

1fe65ba80877b00c59e33c3d95ed1400a51a706a.title: Heavy Cell Rate
1fe65ba80877b00c59e33c3d95ed1400a51a706a.body:
For every \(0<\epsilon<1/2\), there exist constants \(C_\epsilon,\rho_\epsilon>0\) and an integer \(N_\epsilon<\infty\) such that the following holds.  For every \(n,d\in\mathbb N\), every single-observation law \(P\) on \(\{1,\ldots,d\}\times\{0,1\}\times\{0,1\}\), and every sample law \(\mu_n\), assume:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Sample size.)} \(n\ge N_\epsilon\).
\item \textbf{(Dimension growth.)} \(d\le \rho_\epsilon n\log n\).
\item \textbf{(Experiment class.)} \(\mu_n=P^{\otimes n}\) belongs to \(\mathcal E_{n,d,\epsilon}\) in the sense of Definition~\ref{obj:def:experiment-class}.
\end{itemize}
Then
\[
\int \left(\widehat T_{\mathcal H}-\sum_{k\in\widehat{\mathcal H}_n}\phi(q_k)\right)^2\,d\mu_n
\le
C_\epsilon\left\{\frac1n+\frac{d^2}{n^2(\log n)^2}\right\}.
\]

153592f6818e5a6b83530069ff7a7260855d7c5b.title: Two-Category Witness
153592f6818e5a6b83530069ff7a7260855d7c5b.body:
For every \(\epsilon\in\mathbb R\) such that \(0<\epsilon\) and \(\epsilon\le 1/2\), let \(Q\) be the full-data law constructed in Definition~\ref{obj:def:two-category-witness}, and let \(P\) be its observed marginal law. Then \(Q\) satisfies Assumption~\ref{obj:ass:consistency} and Assumption~\ref{obj:ass:conditional-exchangeability}, the observed law \(P\) satisfies Assumption~\ref{obj:ass:overlap} with overlap constant \(\epsilon\), and the ATE functional of Definition~\ref{obj:def:ate-functional} obeys
\[
\tau(P)=\frac12,
\qquad
E_P[Y\mid A=1]-E_P[Y\mid A=0]=\epsilon .
\]

4b9d426114194932321289794334941234d5ec64.title: Bernoulli Randomization Lower Bound
4b9d426114194932321289794334941234d5ec64.body:
For every \(n,d\in\mathbb N\) with \(n>0\) and \(d>0\), the minimax mean-squared-error risk \(\mathsf R_{n,d,1/2}\) of Definition~\ref{obj:def:minimax-risk} satisfies
\[
\mathsf R_{n,d,1/2}\ge \frac{1}{100n}.
\]

433e41d4fd9a3a9d7c1a71a204125e827cce7719.title: Randomized Endpoint Minimax Risk
433e41d4fd9a3a9d7c1a71a204125e827cce7719.body:
For every \(n,d\in\mathbb N\) with \(n>0\) and \(d>0\), the minimax mean-squared-error risk of Definition~\ref{obj:def:minimax-risk} at exact randomization satisfies
\[
\frac{1}{100n}\le \mathsf R_{n,d,1/2}\le \frac{1}{n}.
\]

67b2bfaa03a1f06ab2b2a4f6da70aa8c90380fe7.title: ATE Minimax Lower Bound
67b2bfaa03a1f06ab2b2a4f6da70aa8c90380fe7.body:
For any \(0<\epsilon<1/2\), let \(\mathsf R_{n,d,\epsilon}\) denote the minimax mean-squared-error risk of Definition~\ref{obj:def:minimax-risk}. There exist constants \(a_\epsilon,b_\epsilon\in\mathbb R\) and a natural-number cutoff \(N_\epsilon\) such that \(a_\epsilon>0\), \(b_\epsilon>0\), and for every \(n,d\in\mathbb N\) with \(d>0\), \(n\ge N_\epsilon\), and
\[
d\le b_\epsilon n\log n,
\]
one has
\[
\mathsf R_{n,d,\epsilon}
\ge
a_\epsilon\left\{\frac{1}{n}+\frac{d^2}{n^2(\log n)^2}\right\}.
\]

1679ddb2202d05acc32fd02d1a63126725df5240.title: Centered Linear MSE Bound
1679ddb2202d05acc32fd02d1a63126725df5240.body:
For any \(n,d\in\mathbb N\), any \(\epsilon\in\mathbb R\), any single-observation law \(P\), and any sample law \(\mu_n\), suppose that
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Sample size.)} \(n>0\).
\item \textbf{(Experiment class.)} \(\mu_n\) belongs to the experiment class \(\mathcal E_{n,d,\epsilon}\) generated by \(P\), as in Definition~\ref{obj:def:experiment-class}.
\end{itemize}
Define
\[
\widehat\tau_{\mathrm{ctr}}
=
\frac1n\sum_{i=1}^n
2(2A_i-1)\left(Y_i-\frac12\right).
\]
Then, with \(\tau(P)\) as in Definition~\ref{obj:def:ate-functional},
\[
\mathbb E_{\mu_n}\left[\left(\widehat\tau_{\mathrm{ctr}}-\tau(P)\right)^2\right]
\le
\frac1n+4\left(\frac12-\epsilon\right)^2.
\]

70f1bb60095fe3d35d224fe517589e3ea5cfcaba.title: Combined Upper Envelope
70f1bb60095fe3d35d224fe517589e3ea5cfcaba.body:
Fix constants \(\epsilon,C_\epsilon,\rho_\epsilon\in\mathbb R\) and \(N_\epsilon\in\mathbb N\). Assume:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Interior overlap.)} \(0<\epsilon<1/2\).
\item \textbf{(Positive constants.)} \(C_\epsilon>0\) and \(\rho_\epsilon>0\).
\item \textbf{(Hybrid bound.)} For every \(n,d\in\mathbb N\), if \(0<n\), \(N_\epsilon\le n\), and \(d\le \rho_\epsilon n\log n\), then the hybrid estimator \(\widehat\tau_n^{\mathrm{hyb}}\) of Definition~\ref{obj:def:hybrid-estimator-handle} satisfies
\[
\sup_{P^{\otimes n}\in\mathcal E_{n,d,\epsilon}}
\mathbb E_{P^{\otimes n}}\!\left[\left(\widehat\tau_n^{\mathrm{hyb}}-\tau(P)\right)^2\right]
\le
C_\epsilon\left\{\frac1n+\frac{d^2}{n^2(\log n)^2}\right\}.
\]
\end{itemize}
For every \(n,d\in\mathbb N\) with \(0<n\), \(N_\epsilon\le n\), and \(d\le \rho_\epsilon n\log n\), let \(K_\epsilon=\max\{C_\epsilon,4\}\), and define the selected estimator \(\widehat\tau_n^{\mathrm{sel}}\) to be \(\widehat\tau_n^{\mathrm{hyb}}\) when
\[
C_\epsilon\left\{\frac1n+\frac{d^2}{n^2(\log n)^2}\right\}
\le
\frac1n+4(1/2-\epsilon)^2
\]
and to be \(\widehat\tau_{\mathrm{ctr}}\) otherwise. Then, with \(\mathsf R_{n,d,\epsilon}\) as in Definition~\ref{obj:def:minimax-risk},
\[
\mathsf R_{n,d,\epsilon}
\le
\sup_{P^{\otimes n}\in\mathcal E_{n,d,\epsilon}}
\mathbb E_{P^{\otimes n}}\!\left[\left(\widehat\tau_n^{\mathrm{sel}}-\tau(P)\right)^2\right]
\le
K_\epsilon\left[
\frac1n+
\min\left\{\frac{d^2}{n^2(\log n)^2},(1/2-\epsilon)^2\right\}
\right].
\]

aaec50055e1d29bad26cf874a9054fdac7874c9d.title: Universal Hybrid Calibration
aaec50055e1d29bad26cf874a9054fdac7874c9d.body:
The following conclusions hold for the hybrid estimator \(\widehat\tau_n^{\mathrm{hyb}}\) and centered estimator \(\widehat\tau_{\mathrm{ctr}}\) of Definition~\ref{obj:def:hybrid-estimator-handle}, with minimax risk \(\mathsf R_{n,d,\epsilon}\) as in Definition~\ref{obj:def:minimax-risk}.
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Computability.)} There is a constant \(K\in\mathbb N\), \(K>0\), such that for every \(n,d\in\mathbb N\) there is a real-arithmetic program which, on the hybrid count input, returns exactly \(\widehat\tau_n^{\mathrm{hyb}}\) for every sample \(O_1,\ldots,O_n\), and whose arithmetic/comparison operation count is at most \(K\,d\,M(n)^4\).

\item \textbf{(Fixed-overlap hybrid calibration and envelope.)} For every \(0<\epsilon<1/2\), there exist constants \(C_\epsilon>0\), \(\rho_\epsilon>0\), and \(N_\epsilon\in\mathbb N\) such that, for all \(n,d\in\mathbb N\) with \(n>0\), \(d>0\), \(n\ge N_\epsilon\), and
\[
d\le \rho_\epsilon n\log n,
\]
the hybrid estimator satisfies
\[
\sup_{P^{\otimes n}\in\mathcal E_{n,d,\epsilon}}
E_P\!\left[(\widehat\tau_n^{\mathrm{hyb}}-\tau(P))^2\right]
\le
C_\epsilon\left\{\frac1n+\frac{d^2}{n^2(\log n)^2}\right\}.
\]
For the deterministic selector which chooses \(\widehat\tau_n^{\mathrm{hyb}}\) when
\[
C_\epsilon\left\{\frac1n+\frac{d^2}{n^2(\log n)^2}\right\}
\le
\frac1n+4(1/2-\epsilon)^2
\]
and otherwise chooses \(\widehat\tau_{\mathrm{ctr}}\), one also has
\[
\mathsf R_{n,d,\epsilon}
\le
\sup_{P^{\otimes n}\in\mathcal E_{n,d,\epsilon}}
E_P\!\left[(\widehat\tau_{\mathrm{sel}}-\tau(P))^2\right]
\]
and
\[
\sup_{P^{\otimes n}\in\mathcal E_{n,d,\epsilon}}
E_P\!\left[(\widehat\tau_{\mathrm{sel}}-\tau(P))^2\right]
\le
\max\{C_\epsilon,4\}
\left\{
\frac1n+
\min\left[
\frac{d^2}{n^2(\log n)^2},(1/2-\epsilon)^2
\right]
\right\}.
\]

\item \textbf{(Centered estimator.)} For every \(0<\epsilon\le 1/2\) and every \(n,d\in\mathbb N\) with \(n>0\) and \(d>0\),
\[
\sup_{P^{\otimes n}\in\mathcal E_{n,d,\epsilon}}
E_P\!\left[(\widehat\tau_{\mathrm{ctr}}-\tau(P))^2\right]
\le
\frac1n+4(1/2-\epsilon)^2 .
\]

\item \textbf{(Endpoint bracket.)} For every \(n,d\in\mathbb N\) with \(n>0\) and \(d>0\),
\[
\frac{1}{100n}\le \mathsf R_{n,d,1/2}\le \frac1n .
\]
\end{itemize}

4c3a59b595f8f68c3bed4a663249a3fbd1203f06.title: Fixed-Interior Minimax Rate
4c3a59b595f8f68c3bed4a663249a3fbd1203f06.body:
Fix \(0<\epsilon<1/2\). Then there exist constants \(a_\epsilon,\rho_\epsilon,C_\epsilon>0\) and an integer \(N_\epsilon<\infty\) such that the following hold.
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Sharp sandwich.)} For every \(n,d\), every single-observation law \(P\), and every sample law \(P^{\otimes n}\in\mathcal E_{n,d,\epsilon}\) as in Definition~\ref{obj:def:experiment-class}, if \(d>0\), \(n\ge N_\epsilon\), and
\[
d\le \rho_\epsilon n\log n,
\]
then, with \(\mathsf R_{n,d,\epsilon}\) as in Definition~\ref{obj:def:minimax-risk} and \(\widehat\tau_n^{\mathrm{hyb}}\) as in Definition~\ref{obj:def:hybrid-estimator-handle},
\[
a_\epsilon\left\{\frac1n+\frac{d^2}{n^2(\log n)^2}\right\}
\le
\mathsf R_{n,d,\epsilon}
\le
\sup_{Q^{\otimes n}\in\mathcal E_{n,d,\epsilon}}
E_Q\!\left[\left(\widehat\tau_n^{\mathrm{hyb}}-\tau(Q)\right)^2\right]
\le
C_\epsilon\left\{\frac1n+\frac{d^2}{n^2(\log n)^2}\right\}.
\]
\item \textbf{(Parametric window.)} For every \(K>0\), there exists \(C_K>0\) such that, for every \(n,d\), every single-observation law \(P\), and every sample law \(P^{\otimes n}\in\mathcal E_{n,d,\epsilon}\), if \(d>0\), \(n\ge N_\epsilon\),
\[
d\le K\sqrt n\,\log n
\qquad\text{and}\qquad
d\le \rho_\epsilon n\log n,
\]
then
\[
\frac{a_\epsilon}{n}
\le
\mathsf R_{n,d,\epsilon}
\le
\frac{C_K}{n}.
\]
\item \textbf{(Consistency threshold.)} For any sequences \(n_j,d_j\) with \(n_j\to\infty\), eventually \(d_j>0\), and eventually
\[
d_j\le \rho_\epsilon n_j\log n_j,
\]
one has
\[
\mathsf R_{n_j,d_j,\epsilon}\to0
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
\frac{d_j}{n_j\log n_j}\to0.
\]
\end{itemize}

29885fe8fe3949061912d03bbeec43c6e642320f.title: Iid sampling
29885fe8fe3949061912d03bbeec43c6e642320f.body: The observations \(O_1,\ldots,O_n\) are independent and identically distributed with single-observation law \(P\).

2fff01bdfaeb31c530e23535bbeb20dcbf9c2718.title: Consistency
2fff01bdfaeb31c530e23535bbeb20dcbf9c2718.body:
The observed outcome satisfies
\[
Y=Y(A)
\]
almost surely.

e3aa1338e1b91e9cf101ce1cd2a2b079fed32d6b.title: Conditional exchangeability
e3aa1338e1b91e9cf101ce1cd2a2b079fed32d6b.body:
The binary potential outcomes satisfy
\[
(Y(0),Y(1))\perp A\mid X .
\]

b30cc84f5d6a7e3caef6d4220234dae5b4a36379.title: Experiment class \(\mathcal E_{n,d,\epsilon}\)
b30cc84f5d6a7e3caef6d4220234dae5b4a36379.body:
Under Assumption~\ref{obj:ass:iid-sampling} and Assumption~\ref{obj:ass:overlap}, the experiment class is
\[
\mathcal E_{n,d,\epsilon}
:=
\{P^{\otimes n}: P\in\mathsf{Prob}(\{1,\ldots,d\}\times\{0,1\}^2),\ n,d\in\mathbb N,\ 0<\epsilon\le 1/2,\ P\text{ satisfies Assumption~\ref{obj:ass:overlap}}\}.
\]

2b22af863626b63ce68133eb9783b331634a064a.title: Overlap cone \(\mathcal C_\epsilon\)
2b22af863626b63ce68133eb9783b331634a064a.body:
The overlap-restricted cone of nonnegative four-cell vectors is
\[
\mathcal C_\epsilon
:=
\{u=(u_{00},u_{01},u_{10},u_{11})\in\mathbb R_+^4:
\epsilon(u_{00}+u_{01}+u_{10}+u_{11})
\le u_{10}+u_{11}
\le (1-\epsilon)(u_{00}+u_{01}+u_{10}+u_{11})\}.
\]

f306aa37c36b4f09464eaeb139df967e02a5f431.title: ATE functional \(\tau(P)\)
f306aa37c36b4f09464eaeb139df967e02a5f431.body:
The average treatment effect functional is
\[
\tau(P)
=
\sum_{k=1}^{d}p_k(\mu_{1k}-\mu_{0k})
=
\sum_{k=1}^{d}\phi(q_k).
\]

b51940b76b22d6b5cae856d3a21fdda9292409cf.title: Hybrid estimator \(\widehat\tau_n^{\mathrm{hyb}}\)
b51940b76b22d6b5cae856d3a21fdda9292409cf.body:
Set
\[
I_0=\{1,\ldots,\lfloor n/2\rfloor\},\qquad
I_1=\{\lfloor n/2\rfloor+1,\ldots,n\},\qquad
m_j=|I_j|,\qquad
L=\log(en).
\]
Let \(A=6\), and set
\[
\lambda_0=256,\qquad
b_0=4096,\qquad
D_A=8\log(9A/8)=8\log(27/4),
\]
and
\[
\alpha_0
=
\min\left\{
1,\frac1{32\log A},\frac1{256D_A}
\right\}.
\]
For \(n\ge2\), define
\[
M(n)=\max\{2,\lfloor\alpha_0L\rfloor\},
\qquad
B(n)=b_0L/m_1.
\]
Let \(N_0\) be the least numerical cutoff such that, for every \(n\ge N_0\),
\[
\alpha_0L\ge2,\qquad
4M(n)^2\le m_1,\qquad
4M(n)/m_1\le 3B(n)/4.
\]
For \(n\ge N_0\), write \(M=M(n)\) and \(B=B(n)\), and define the pilot-certified heavy and light category sets by
\[
\widehat{\mathcal H}_n
=
\left\{
k:\sum_{a,y}N^{(0)}_{aky}>\lambda_0L
\right\},
\qquad
\widehat{\mathcal L}_n=\widehat{\mathcal H}_n^c.
\]
For the second split, put
\[
N_k^{(1)}=\sum_{a,y}N^{(1)}_{aky},
\qquad
N_{ak}^{(1)}=\sum_yN^{(1)}_{aky},
\]
and define the heavy-category ratio contribution
\[
\widehat h_k
=
\frac{N_k^{(1)}}{m_1}
\left\{
\frac{N^{(1)}_{1k1}}{N^{(1)}_{1k}}\mathbf1\{N^{(1)}_{1k}>0\}
-
\frac{N^{(1)}_{0k1}}{N^{(1)}_{0k}}\mathbf1\{N^{(1)}_{0k}>0\}
\right\}.
\]
Let
\[
H_M(x)=\frac{1-T_M(1-2x)}{2M^2},
\qquad
E_M(x)=\frac{H_M(x)}{x},
\qquad
G_M(x)=\frac{1-E_M(x)}{x},
\]
where \(E_M\) and \(G_M\) are interpreted by polynomial continuation at zero. For \(u=(u_{00},u_{01},u_{10},u_{11})\), set
\[
s_a(u)=u_{a0}+u_{a1},\qquad
s(u)=s_0(u)+s_1(u),\qquad
t_1(u)=u_{11},\qquad
t_0(u)=u_{01}.
\]
Define the light-cell polynomial approximation
\[
P_{M,B}(u)
=
\frac{s(u)t_1(u)}B
G_M\!\left(\frac{s_1(u)}B\right)
-
\frac{s(u)t_0(u)}B
G_M\!\left(\frac{s_0(u)}B\right).
\]
Expanding \(P_{M,B}(u)=\sum_{|r|\le M}c_ru^r\), set
\[
\widehat P_k
=
\sum_{|r|\le M}
c_r
\frac{\prod_{a,y}(N^{(1)}_{aky})_{r_{ay}}}{(m_1)_{|r|}},
\qquad
\widehat T_{\mathcal H}
=
\sum_{k\in\widehat{\mathcal H}_n}\widehat h_k,
\qquad
\widehat T_{\mathcal L}
=
\sum_{k\in\widehat{\mathcal L}_n}\widehat P_k.
\]
The truncated balanced ratio-polynomial hybrid estimator is
\[
\widehat\tau_n^{\mathrm{hyb}}
=
\max\{-1,\min(1,\widehat T_{\mathcal H}+\widehat T_{\mathcal L})\}.
\]
For \(n<N_0\), set \(\widehat{\mathcal L}_n=\varnothing\) and use the ratio branch on every category. The estimator uses no overlap constant and is computable in \(O(dM^4)\) arithmetic operations.

4fd7bca745d387c62c990b48c8ad1416677d54f0.title: Two-category witness law
4fd7bca745d387c62c990b48c8ad1416677d54f0.body:
For \(d=2\), set
\[
p_1=p_2=\frac12,\qquad
\pi_1=\epsilon,\qquad
\pi_2=1-\epsilon,\qquad
\mu_{01}=\mu_{02}=0,\qquad
\mu_{11}=1,\qquad

Define a full-data extension by drawing
\[
(Y(0),Y(1))=(0,\mathbf 1\{X=1\}),
\]
and then drawing \(A\mid X=k\sim\mathsf{Bernoulli}(\pi_k)\).

1dc50564c7b6c49c329cce22b3727a24ce09727a.title: Two-Category Confounding Witness
1dc50564c7b6c49c329cce22b3727a24ce09727a.body:
For \(\epsilon\), suppose:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Real parameter.)} \(\epsilon\in\mathbb R\).
\item \textbf{(Positive contrast.)} \(0<\epsilon\).
\item \textbf{(Overlap range.)} \(\epsilon\le 1/2\).
\item \textbf{(Witness law.)} \(Q\) is the full-data law constructed in Definition~\ref{obj:def:two-category-witness}, and \(P\) is its observed marginal law.
\end{itemize}
Then \(Q\) satisfies Assumption~\ref{obj:ass:consistency} and Assumption~\ref{obj:ass:conditional-exchangeability}, the observed law \(P\) satisfies Assumption~\ref{obj:ass:overlap} with overlap constant \(\epsilon\), and the ATE functional of Definition~\ref{obj:def:ate-functional} obeys
\[
\tau(P)=\frac12,
\qquad
E_P[Y\mid A=1]-E_P[Y\mid A=0]=\epsilon .
\]

C_\epsilon\left\{\frac1n+\frac{d^2}{n^2(\log n)^2}\right\}.

For the deterministic estimator that chooses \(\widehat\tau_n^{\mathrm{hyb}}\) when
\[
C_\epsilon\left\{\frac1n+\frac{d^2}{n^2(\log n)^2}\right\}
\le
\frac1n+4(1/2-\epsilon)^2
\]
and otherwise chooses \(\widehat\tau_{\mathrm{ctr}}\), one also has
\[
\mathsf R_{n,d,\epsilon}
\le
\sup_{P^{\otimes n}\in\mathcal E_{n,d,\epsilon}}
E_P\!\left[(\widehat\tau_{\mathrm{sel}}-\tau(P))^2\right]
\]
and
\[
\sup_{P^{\otimes n}\in\mathcal E_{n,d,\epsilon}}
E_P\!\left[(\widehat\tau_{\mathrm{sel}}-\tau(P))^2\right]
\le
\max\{C_\epsilon,4\}
\left\{
\frac1n+
\min\left[
\frac{d^2}{n^2(\log n)^2},(1/2-\epsilon)^2
\right]
\right\}.
\]

\item \textbf{(Centered estimator.)} For every \(0<\epsilon\le 1/2\) and every \(n,d\in\mathbb N\) with \(n>0\) and \(d>0\), the centered estimator
\[
\widehat\tau_{\mathrm{ctr}}
=
\frac1n\sum_{i=1}^n
2(2A_i-1)\left(Y_i-\frac12\right)
\]
satisfies
\[
\sup_{P^{\otimes n}\in\mathcal E_{n,d,\epsilon}}
E_P\!\left[(\widehat\tau_{\mathrm{ctr}}-\tau(P))^2\right]
\le
\frac1n+4(1/2-\epsilon)^2 .
\]

\item \textbf{(Endpoint bracket.)} For every \(n,d\in\mathbb N\) with \(n>0\) and \(d>0\),
\[
\frac{1}{100n}\le \mathsf R_{n,d,1/2}\le \frac1n .
\]
\end{itemize}

55870b9b752f18d401a52ec00d9511b1b8776824.title: Universal Hybrid Envelope
55870b9b752f18d401a52ec00d9511b1b8776824.body:
For the hybrid estimator \(\widehat\tau_n^{\mathrm{hyb}}\) of Definition~\ref{obj:def:hybrid-estimator-handle} and the minimax risk \(\mathsf R_{n,d,\epsilon}\) of Definition~\ref{obj:def:minimax-risk}, the following conclusions hold.
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Computability.)} There is a constant \(K\in\mathbb N\), \(K>0\), such that for every \(n,d\in\mathbb N\) there is a real-arithmetic program which reads the hybrid count input, returns exactly \(\widehat\tau_n^{\mathrm{hyb}}\) for every sample \(O_1,\ldots,O_n\), and has arithmetic/comparison operation count at most \(K\,d\,M(n)^4\). The hybrid estimator itself does not take \(\epsilon\) as an input.

\item \textbf{(Fixed-overlap hybrid calibration and selected envelope.)} For every \(0<\epsilon<1/2\), there exist constants \(C_\epsilon>0\), \(\rho_\epsilon>0\), and \(N_\epsilon\in\mathbb N\) such that, for all \(n,d\in\mathbb N\) with \(n>0\), \(d>0\), \(n\ge N_\epsilon\), and
\[
d\le \rho_\epsilon n\log n,
\]
the hybrid estimator satisfies
\[
\sup_{P^{\otimes n}\in\mathcal E_{n,d,\epsilon}}
E_P\!\left[(\widehat\tau_n^{\mathrm{hyb}}-\tau(P))^2\right]
\le
C_\epsilon\left\{\frac1n+\frac{d^2}{n^2(\log n)^2}\right\}.
\]
Define \(\widehat\tau_n^{\mathrm{sel}}(C_\epsilon,\epsilon)\) to be the deterministic estimator that equals \(\widehat\tau_n^{\mathrm{hyb}}\) when
\[
C_\epsilon\left\{\frac1n+\frac{d^2}{n^2(\log n)^2}\right\}
\le
\frac1n+4(1/2-\epsilon)^2
\]
and equals \(\widehat\tau_{\mathrm{ctr}}\) otherwise. Then
\[
\mathsf R_{n,d,\epsilon}
\le
\sup_{P^{\otimes n}\in\mathcal E_{n,d,\epsilon}}
E_P\!\left[(\widehat\tau_n^{\mathrm{sel}}(C_\epsilon,\epsilon)-\tau(P))^2\right],
\]
and
\[
\sup_{P^{\otimes n}\in\mathcal E_{n,d,\epsilon}}
E_P\!\left[(\widehat\tau_n^{\mathrm{sel}}(C_\epsilon,\epsilon)-\tau(P))^2\right]
\le
\max\{C_\epsilon,4\}
\left\{
\frac1n+
\min\left[
\frac{d^2}{n^2(\log n)^2},(1/2-\epsilon)^2
\right]
\right\}.
\]

\item \textbf{(Centered estimator.)} For every \(0<\epsilon\le 1/2\) and every \(n,d\in\mathbb N\) with \(n>0\) and \(d>0\), the centered estimator
\[
\widehat\tau_{\mathrm{ctr}}
=
\frac1n\sum_{i=1}^n
2(2A_i-1)\left(Y_i-\frac12\right)
\]
satisfies
\[
\sup_{P^{\otimes n}\in\mathcal E_{n,d,\epsilon}}
E_P\!\left[(\widehat\tau_{\mathrm{ctr}}-\tau(P))^2\right]
\le
\frac1n+4(1/2-\epsilon)^2 .
\]

\item \textbf{(Endpoint bracket.)} For every \(n,d\in\mathbb N\) with \(n>0\) and \(d>0\),
\[
\frac{1}{100n}\le \mathsf R_{n,d,1/2}\le \frac1n .
\]
\end{itemize}

c5b92d80d3590743a6dabd0079cb95168382eaea.title: Universal Hybrid Envelope
c5b92d80d3590743a6dabd0079cb95168382eaea.body:
The following conclusions hold for the hybrid estimator \(\widehat\tau_n^{\mathrm{hyb}}\) and centered estimator \(\widehat\tau_{\mathrm{ctr}}\) of Definition~\ref{obj:def:hybrid-estimator-handle}, with minimax risk \(\mathsf R_{n,d,\epsilon}\) as in Definition~\ref{obj:def:minimax-risk}.
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Computability.)} There is a constant \(K\in\mathbb N\), \(K>0\), such that for every \(n,d\in\mathbb N\) there is a real-arithmetic program which, on the hybrid count input, returns exactly \(\widehat\tau_n^{\mathrm{hyb}}\) for every sample \(O_1,\ldots,O_n\), and whose arithmetic/comparison operation count is at most \(K\,d\,M(n)^4\).

\item \textbf{(Fixed-overlap hybrid calibration and envelope.)} For every \(0<\epsilon<1/2\), there exist constants \(C_\epsilon>0\), \(\rho_\epsilon>0\), and \(N_\epsilon\in\mathbb N\) such that, for all \(n,d\in\mathbb N\) with \(n>0\), \(d>0\), \(n\ge N_\epsilon\), and
\[
d\le \rho_\epsilon n\log n,
\]
the hybrid estimator satisfies
\[
\sup_{P^{\otimes n}\in\mathcal E_{n,d,\epsilon}}
E_P\!\left[(\widehat\tau_n^{\mathrm{hyb}}-\tau(P))^2\right]
\le
C_\epsilon\left\{\frac1n+\frac{d^2}{n^2(\log n)^2}\right\}.
\]
For the deterministic selected estimator obtained from the rule that chooses \(\widehat\tau_n^{\mathrm{hyb}}\) when
\[
C_\epsilon\left\{\frac1n+\frac{d^2}{n^2(\log n)^2}\right\}
\le
\frac1n+4(1/2-\epsilon)^2
\]
and otherwise chooses \(\widehat\tau_{\mathrm{ctr}}\), one also has
\[
\mathsf R_{n,d,\epsilon}
\le
\sup_{P^{\otimes n}\in\mathcal E_{n,d,\epsilon}}
E_P\!\left[(\widehat\tau^{\mathrm{sel}}_{C_\epsilon,\epsilon}-\tau(P))^2\right]
\]
and
\[
\sup_{P^{\otimes n}\in\mathcal E_{n,d,\epsilon}}
E_P\!\left[(\widehat\tau^{\mathrm{sel}}_{C_\epsilon,\epsilon}-\tau(P))^2\right]
\le
\max\{C_\epsilon,4\}
\left\{
\frac1n+
\min\left[
\frac{d^2}{n^2(\log n)^2},(1/2-\epsilon)^2
\right]
\right\}.
\]

\item \textbf{(Centered estimator.)} For every \(0<\epsilon\le 1/2\) and every \(n,d\in\mathbb N\) with \(n>0\) and \(d>0\),
\[
\sup_{P^{\otimes n}\in\mathcal E_{n,d,\epsilon}}
E_P\!\left[(\widehat\tau_{\mathrm{ctr}}-\tau(P))^2\right]
\le
\frac1n+4(1/2-\epsilon)^2 .
\]

\item \textbf{(Endpoint bracket.)} For every \(n,d\in\mathbb N\) with \(n>0\) and \(d>0\),
\[
\frac{1}{100n}\le \mathsf R_{n,d,1/2}\le \frac1n .
\]
\end{itemize}

b6ab064eb6f9c459153c9a8d5ca4be6e131fb10b.title: Combined Upper Envelope
b6ab064eb6f9c459153c9a8d5ca4be6e131fb10b.body:
Fix constants \(\epsilon,C_\epsilon,\rho_\epsilon\in\mathbb R\) and \(N_\epsilon\in\mathbb N\). Assume:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Interior overlap.)} \(0<\epsilon<1/2\).
\item \textbf{(Positive constants.)} \(C_\epsilon>0\) and \(\rho_\epsilon>0\).
\item \textbf{(Hybrid bound.)} For every \(n,d\in\mathbb N\), if \(0<n\), \(N_\epsilon\le n\), and \(d\le \rho_\epsilon n\log n\), then the hybrid estimator \(\widehat\tau_n^{\mathrm{hyb}}\) of Definition~\ref{obj:def:hybrid-estimator-handle} satisfies
\[
\sup_{P^{\otimes n}\in\mathcal E_{n,d,\epsilon}}
\mathbb E_{P^{\otimes n}}\!\left[\left(\widehat\tau_n^{\mathrm{hyb}}-\tau(P)\right)^2\right]
\le
C_\epsilon\left\{\frac1n+\frac{d^2}{n^2(\log n)^2}\right\}.
\]
\end{itemize}
For every \(n,d\in\mathbb N\) with \(0<n\), \(N_\epsilon\le n\), and \(d\le \rho_\epsilon n\log n\), let \(K_\epsilon=\max\{C_\epsilon,4\}\). Define \(\widehat\tau_{\mathrm{sel}}\) to be \(\widehat\tau_n^{\mathrm{hyb}}\) when
\[
C_\epsilon\left\{\frac1n+\frac{d^2}{n^2(\log n)^2}\right\}
\le
\frac1n+4(1/2-\epsilon)^2
\]
and to be \(\widehat\tau_{\mathrm{ctr}}\) otherwise. Then, with \(\mathsf R_{n,d,\epsilon}\) as in Definition~\ref{obj:def:minimax-risk},
\[
\mathsf R_{n,d,\epsilon}
\le
\sup_{P^{\otimes n}\in\mathcal E_{n,d,\epsilon}}
\mathbb E_{P^{\otimes n}}\!\left[\left(\widehat\tau_{\mathrm{sel}}-\tau(P)\right)^2\right]
\le
K_\epsilon\left[
\frac1n+
\min\left\{\frac{d^2}{n^2(\log n)^2},(1/2-\epsilon)^2\right\}
\right].
\]

f2898bd0aafdb263dfcabc29477bb463081e3c49.title: Combined Upper Envelope
f2898bd0aafdb263dfcabc29477bb463081e3c49.body:
Fix constants \(\epsilon,C_\epsilon,\rho_\epsilon\in\mathbb R\) and \(N_\epsilon\in\mathbb N\). Assume:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Interior overlap.)} \(0<\epsilon<1/2\).
\item \textbf{(Positive constants.)} \(C_\epsilon>0\) and \(\rho_\epsilon>0\).
\item \textbf{(Hybrid bound.)} For every \(n,d\in\mathbb N\), if \(0<n\), \(N_\epsilon\le n\), and \(d\le \rho_\epsilon n\log n\), then the hybrid estimator \(\widehat\tau_n^{\mathrm{hyb}}\) of Definition~\ref{obj:def:hybrid-estimator-handle} satisfies
\[
\sup_{P^{\otimes n}\in\mathcal E_{n,d,\epsilon}}
\mathbb E_{P^{\otimes n}}\!\left[\left(\widehat\tau_n^{\mathrm{hyb}}-\tau(P)\right)^2\right]
\le
C_\epsilon\left\{\frac1n+\frac{d^2}{n^2(\log n)^2}\right\}.
\]
\end{itemize}
Then for every \(n,d\in\mathbb N\) with \(0<n\), \(N_\epsilon\le n\), and \(d\le \rho_\epsilon n\log n\), let \(K_\epsilon=\max\{C_\epsilon,4\}\). Define the \(C_\epsilon,\epsilon\)-dependent selected estimator \(\widehat\tau^{\mathrm{sel}}_{C_\epsilon,\epsilon}\) to be \(\widehat\tau_n^{\mathrm{hyb}}\) when
\[
C_\epsilon\left\{\frac1n+\frac{d^2}{n^2(\log n)^2}\right\}
\le
\frac1n+4(1/2-\epsilon)^2
\]
and to be \(\widehat\tau_{\mathrm{ctr}}\) otherwise. This selected estimator satisfies
\[
\sup_{P^{\otimes n}\in\mathcal E_{n,d,\epsilon}}
\mathbb E_{P^{\otimes n}}\!\left[\left(\widehat\tau^{\mathrm{sel}}_{C_\epsilon,\epsilon}-\tau(P)\right)^2\right]
\le
K_\epsilon\left[
\frac1n+
\min\left\{\frac{d^2}{n^2(\log n)^2},(1/2-\epsilon)^2\right\}
\right].
\]

1bade2c33142628f4ff3614af5e53c22a7baad4c.title: Selected estimator \(\widehat\tau^{\mathrm{sel}}_{C_\epsilon,\epsilon}\)
1bade2c33142628f4ff3614af5e53c22a7baad4c.body:
For fixed \(0<\epsilon<1/2\) and fixed-interior upper-bound constant \(C_\epsilon\), define \(\widehat\tau^{\mathrm{sel}}_{C_\epsilon,\epsilon}\) to be \(\widehat\tau_n^{\mathrm{hyb}}\) when
\[
C_\epsilon\{1/n+d^2/(n^2\log^2 n)\}\le 1/n+4(1/2-\epsilon)^2,
\]
and to be \(\widehat\tau_{\mathrm{ctr}}\) otherwise.

158da12f3467ff587a180afe80913185705ede75.title: Heavy-cell rate bound
158da12f3467ff587a180afe80913185705ede75.body:
Fix an overlap parameter \(\epsilon\) with \(0<\epsilon<1/2\).  Then there exist constants \(C_\epsilon,\rho_\epsilon>0\) and an integer \(N_\epsilon<\infty\) such that, for every sample size \(n\), alphabet size \(d\), single-observation law \(P\) on \(\{1,\ldots,d\}\times\{0,1\}\times\{0,1\}\), and sample law \(\mu_n\), the following conditions imply the displayed bound:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Sample size.)} \(n\ge N_\epsilon\).
\item \textbf{(Dimension growth.)} \(d\le \rho_\epsilon n\log n\).
\item \textbf{(Experiment class.)} \(\mu_n=P^{\otimes n}\) belongs to the overlap-restricted iid product-law experiment class \(\mathcal E_{n,d,\epsilon}\) of \(\cref{obj:def:experiment-class}\).
\end{itemize}
For the pilot-certified heavy set \(\widehat{\mathcal H}_n\), the summed heavy-cell ratio contribution satisfies
\[
\int \left\{\widehat T_{\mathcal H}(O_1,\ldots,O_n)
-\sum_{k\in\widehat{\mathcal H}_n}\phi(q_k)\right\}^2\,d\mu_n
\le
C_\epsilon\left\{\frac{1}{n}+\frac{d^2}{n^2(\log n)^2}\right\}.
\]

ebe1583e10fea04b8233f3e976cc881f5b35a565.title: Light-cell polynomial rate
ebe1583e10fea04b8233f3e976cc881f5b35a565.body:
For every overlap parameter \(\epsilon\) with \(0<\epsilon\le 1/2\), the following hold:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Computable calibration.)} The hybrid estimator admits a real-arithmetic implementation: there is a universal integer \(K\ge 1\) such that, for every \(n\) and \(d\), a program reading the hybrid count vector returns \(\widehat\tau_n^{\mathrm{hyb}}\) exactly using at most \(K\,d\,M(n)^4\) arithmetic and comparison operations.
\item \textbf{(Rate constants.)} There exist constants \(C_\epsilon,c_\epsilon>0\), depending only on \(\epsilon\), such that the following bound holds.
\end{itemize}
For every sample size \(n\), alphabet size \(d\), single-observation law \(P\), and sample law \(P^{\otimes n}\in\mathcal E_{n,d,\epsilon}\) in the sense of \(\cref{obj:def:experiment-class}\), if
\[
d\le c_\epsilon n\log n,
\]
then the light-cell contribution \(\widehat T_{\mathcal L}\) satisfies
\[
E_{P^{\otimes n}}\!\left[
\left\{
\widehat T_{\mathcal L}
-
\sum_{k\in\widehat{\mathcal L}_n}\phi(q_k)
\right\}^2
\right]
\le
C_\epsilon\left\{
\frac{1}{n}
+
\frac{d^2}{n^2(\log n)^2}
\right\}.
\]

30c3e0d47a7b488f9267a2c4649885d29ef5b82c.title: Pilot sandwich tail bound
30c3e0d47a7b488f9267a2c4649885d29ef5b82c.body:
For a sample \(O_1,\ldots,O_n\), let \(L=\log(en)\), let \(m_0=|I_0|\), let
\[
\widehat{\mathcal H}=\{k:N_k^{(0)}>tL\},
\qquad
\widehat{\mathcal L}=\widehat{\mathcal H}^{c},
\qquad
B_-=\frac{tL}{2m_0},
\qquad
B_+=\frac{2tL}{m_0}.
\]
Then the following two assertions hold.
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Arbitrary polynomial order.)} For every \(K>0\) and every \(c>0\), there exist constants \(t_0>0\), \(C>0\), and \(N\) such that, for every \(t\ge t_0\), every \(n\ge N\), every alphabet size \(d\) satisfying
\[
d\le c\,n\log(en),
\]
every single-observation law \(P\) on \(\{1,\ldots,d\}\times\{0,1\}\times\{0,1\}\), and every sample law \(\mu_n\) satisfying \(\cref{obj:ass:iid-sampling}\),
\[
\mu_n\!\left(
\widehat{\mathcal H}\not\subseteq\{k:p_k\ge B_-\}
\ \text{or}\
\widehat{\mathcal L}\not\subseteq\{k:p_k\le B_+\}
\right)
\le C n^{-K}.
\]
\item \textbf{(Fixed calibration.)} For every \(c>0\), there exist constants \(C>0\) and \(N\) such that, for every \(n\ge N\), every alphabet size \(d\) satisfying
\[
d\le c\,n\log(en),
\]
every single-observation law \(P\) on \(\{1,\ldots,d\}\times\{0,1\}\times\{0,1\}\), and every sample law \(\mu_n\) satisfying \(\cref{obj:ass:iid-sampling}\), the same event with \(t=256\) obeys
\[
\mu_n\!\left(
\widehat{\mathcal H}\not\subseteq\{k:p_k\ge B_-\}
\ \text{or}\
\widehat{\mathcal L}\not\subseteq\{k:p_k\le B_+\}
\right)
\le C n^{-4}.
\]
\end{itemize}

d9a309b6064cbf18dc91c4c160b0b7f750cbe8a7.title: Two-category confounding witness
d9a309b6064cbf18dc91c4c160b0b7f750cbe8a7.body:
For every real \(\epsilon\) with \(0<\epsilon\le 1/2\), let \(Q\) be the full-data law constructed in \(\cref{obj:def:two-category-witness}\), and let \(P\) be its observed marginal law for \(O=(X,A,Y)\). Then:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Consistency.)} \(Q\) satisfies \(\cref{obj:ass:consistency}\).
\item \textbf{(Conditional exchangeability.)} \(Q\) satisfies \(\cref{obj:ass:conditional-exchangeability}\).
\item \textbf{(Overlap.)} \(P\) satisfies \(\epsilon\)-overlap in the sense of \(\cref{obj:ass:overlap}\).
\end{itemize}
The average treatment effect functional in \(\cref{obj:def:ate-functional}\) and the naive observed contrast under \(P\) obey
\[
\tau(P)=\frac12,
\qquad
E_P[Y\mid A=1]-E_P[Y\mid A=0]=\epsilon .
\]

2333ea3cfc9092ce16363629fe56bfdf34449b42.title: Bernoulli randomization lower bound
2333ea3cfc9092ce16363629fe56bfdf34449b42.body:
For all positive integers \(n\) and \(d\), the minimax mean-squared-error risk \(\mathsf R_{n,d,\epsilon}\) of \cref{obj:def:minimax-risk}, evaluated at \(\epsilon=1/2\), satisfies
\[
\frac{1}{100n}\le \mathsf R_{n,d,1/2}.
\]

0fc0d19667b5593e2ca53468d3f38211329d12d8.title: Randomized endpoint risk
0fc0d19667b5593e2ca53468d3f38211329d12d8.body:
For every \(n,d\in\mathbb N\) with \(0<n\) and \(0<d\), the minimax mean-squared-error risk \(\mathsf R_{n,d,\epsilon}\) defined in \(\cref{obj:def:minimax-risk}\) satisfies, at \(\epsilon=1/2\),
\[
\frac{1}{100n}\le \mathsf R_{n,d,1/2}\le \frac{1}{n}.
\]

9697198f657d2f5ade2e609b526050d55ed7a290.title: ATE lower-bound transfer
9697198f657d2f5ade2e609b526050d55ed7a290.body:
Fix an overlap parameter \(\epsilon\) with \(0<\epsilon<1/2\), and let \(\mathsf R_{n,d,\epsilon}\) be the minimax mean-squared-error risk in \(\cref{obj:def:minimax-risk}\). Then there exist constants \(a_\epsilon,b_\epsilon>0\) and \(N_\epsilon\in\mathbb N\) such that, for every \(n,d\in\mathbb N\), if \(0<d\), \(N_\epsilon\le n\), and
\[
d\le b_\epsilon n\log n,
\]
then
\[
a_\epsilon\left\{\frac{1}{n}+\frac{d^2}{n^2(\log n)^2}\right\}
\le
\mathsf R_{n,d,\epsilon}.
\]

b652a39f476d658dea0daab6169cd8e0f805d0a5.title: Centered linear upper bound
b652a39f476d658dea0daab6169cd8e0f805d0a5.body:
For every \(n,d\in\mathbb N\) with \(n>0\), every overlap parameter \(\epsilon\), every single-observation law \(P\), and every sample law \(\mu_n\) such that \(\mu_n\in\mathcal E_{n,d,\epsilon}\) for \(P\) in the sense of \cref{obj:def:experiment-class}, define
\[
\widehat\tau_{\mathrm{ctr}}
=
\frac1n\sum_{i=1}^n
2(2A_i-1)\left(Y_i-\frac12\right).
\]
Then the mean squared error of \(\widehat\tau_{\mathrm{ctr}}\) for the average treatment effect functional \(\tau(P)\) in \cref{obj:def:ate-functional} satisfies
\[
\int \bigl(\widehat\tau_{\mathrm{ctr}}(o_1,\ldots,o_n)-\tau(P)\bigr)^2\,d\mu_n(o_1,\ldots,o_n)
\le
\frac1n+4\left(\frac12-\epsilon\right)^2 .
\]

e5ea268f18dfa18a7764c1aad75274e4774b5c03.title: Sharp fixed-interior minimax rate
e5ea268f18dfa18a7764c1aad75274e4774b5c03.body:
For an overlap parameter \(\epsilon\) with \(0<\epsilon<1/2\), there exist constants \(a_\epsilon,\rho_\epsilon,C_\epsilon>0\) and an integer \(N_\epsilon<\infty\) such that the following statements hold. Let
\[
r_{n,d}=\frac{1}{n}+\frac{d^2}{n^2(\log n)^2}.
\]
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Sharp sandwich.)} For every \(n,d\), every single-observation law \(P\), and every sample law \(P^{\otimes n}\in\mathcal E_{n,d,\epsilon}\) as in \(\cref{obj:def:experiment-class}\), if \(d>0\), \(n\ge N_\epsilon\), and
\[
d\le \rho_\epsilon n\log n,
\]
then the minimax mean-squared-error risk \(\mathsf R_{n,d,\epsilon}\) from \(\cref{obj:def:minimax-risk}\) and the hybrid estimator \(\widehat\tau_n^{\mathrm{hyb}}\) from \(\cref{obj:def:hybrid-estimator-handle}\) satisfy
\[
a_\epsilon r_{n,d}
\le
\mathsf R_{n,d,\epsilon}
\le
\sup_{P^{\otimes n}\in\mathcal E_{n,d,\epsilon}}
E_P\!\left[\left(\widehat\tau_n^{\mathrm{hyb}}-\tau(P)\right)^2\right]
\le
C_\epsilon r_{n,d}.
\]

\item \textbf{(Parametric interior.)} For every \(K>0\), there exists \(C_K>0\) such that, for every \(n,d\), every single-observation law \(P\), and every sample law \(P^{\otimes n}\in\mathcal E_{n,d,\epsilon}\), if \(d>0\), \(n\ge N_\epsilon\),
\[
d\le K\sqrt n\log n,
\qquad
d\le \rho_\epsilon n\log n,
\]
then
\[
\frac{a_\epsilon}{n}
\le
\mathsf R_{n,d,\epsilon}
\le
\frac{C_K}{n}.
\]

\item \textbf{(Consistency threshold.)} For any sequences \(n_j,d_j\) with \(n_j\to\infty\), with \(d_j>0\) eventually, and with
\[
d_j\le \rho_\epsilon n_j\log n_j
\]
eventually, one has
\[
\mathsf R_{n_j,d_j,\epsilon}\to 0
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
\frac{d_j}{n_j\log n_j}\to 0.
\]
\end{itemize}

fece995567062f4a62a497fbd206a6788177d1ba.title: Universal hybrid envelope
fece995567062f4a62a497fbd206a6788177d1ba.body:
With \(\widehat\tau_n^{\mathrm{hyb}}\) as in \(\cref{obj:def:hybrid-estimator-handle}\) and \(\mathsf R_{n,d,\epsilon}\) as in \(\cref{obj:def:minimax-risk}\), the following conclusions hold.
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{Computability.} There is a constant \(K\in\mathbb N\), \(K>0\), such that for every \(n,d\in\mathbb N\) there is a finite real-arithmetic program which reads the split count vector, returns \(\widehat\tau_n^{\mathrm{hyb}}\) exactly on every sample \(O_1,\ldots,O_n\), and uses at most \(K d M(n)^4\) arithmetic and comparison operations.
\item \textbf{Fixed-interior calibration.} For every overlap parameter \(\epsilon\) with \(0<\epsilon<1/2\), there are constants \(C_\epsilon,\rho_\epsilon>0\) and \(N_\epsilon\in\mathbb N\) such that, for all \(n,d\in\mathbb N\) with \(n>0\), \(d>0\), \(N_\epsilon\le n\), and \(d\le \rho_\epsilon n\log n\),
\[
\sup_{P^{\otimes n}\in\mathcal E_{n,d,\epsilon}}
E_P\!\left[(\widehat\tau_n^{\mathrm{hyb}}-\tau(P))^2\right]
\le
C_\epsilon\left\{\frac1n+\frac{d^2}{n^2(\log n)^2}\right\}.
\]
For the deterministic estimator \(\widehat\tau^{\mathrm{sel}}_{C_\epsilon,\epsilon}\) that equals \(\widehat\tau_n^{\mathrm{hyb}}\) when
\[
C_\epsilon\left\{\frac1n+\frac{d^2}{n^2(\log n)^2}\right\}
\le
\frac1n+4(1/2-\epsilon)^2
\]
and equals \(\widehat\tau_{\mathrm{ctr}}\) otherwise, the same \(n,d,\epsilon\) satisfy
\[
\mathsf R_{n,d,\epsilon}
\le
\sup_{P^{\otimes n}\in\mathcal E_{n,d,\epsilon}}
E_P\!\left[(\widehat\tau^{\mathrm{sel}}_{C_\epsilon,\epsilon}-\tau(P))^2\right],
\]
and
\[
\sup_{P^{\otimes n}\in\mathcal E_{n,d,\epsilon}}
E_P\!\left[(\widehat\tau^{\mathrm{sel}}_{C_\epsilon,\epsilon}-\tau(P))^2\right]
\le
\max\{C_\epsilon,4\}
\left[
\frac1n+
\min\left\{\frac{d^2}{n^2(\log n)^2},(1/2-\epsilon)^2\right\}
\right].
\]
\item \textbf{Centered randomization bound.} For every overlap parameter \(\epsilon\) with \(0<\epsilon\le 1/2\) and every \(n,d\in\mathbb N\) with \(n>0\) and \(d>0\), the centered estimator
\[
\widehat\tau_{\mathrm{ctr}}
=
\frac1n\sum_{i=1}^n
2(2A_i-1)\left(Y_i-\frac12\right)
\]
satisfies
\[
\sup_{P^{\otimes n}\in\mathcal E_{n,d,\epsilon}}
E_P\!\left[(\widehat\tau_{\mathrm{ctr}}-\tau(P))^2\right]
\le
\frac1n+4(1/2-\epsilon)^2.
\]
\item \textbf{Endpoint bracket.} For every \(n,d\in\mathbb N\) with \(n>0\) and \(d>0\),
\[
\frac{1}{100n}\le \mathsf R_{n,d,1/2}\le \frac1n.
\]
\end{itemize}

6adb509f1170e85b4015e9011eaa08c68f17e3ae.title: Combined envelope selector
6adb509f1170e85b4015e9011eaa08c68f17e3ae.body:
Fix constants \(\epsilon,C_\epsilon,\rho_\epsilon\in\mathbb R\) and \(N_\epsilon\in\mathbb N\). Assume:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Interior overlap.)} \(0<\epsilon<1/2\).
\item \textbf{(Positive constants.)} \(C_\epsilon>0\) and \(\rho_\epsilon>0\).
\item \textbf{(Hybrid bound.)} For every \(n,d\in\mathbb N\), if \(0<n\), \(N_\epsilon\le n\), and \(d\le \rho_\epsilon n\log n\), then the hybrid estimator \(\widehat\tau_n^{\mathrm{hyb}}\) of \cref{obj:def:hybrid-estimator-handle} satisfies
\[
\sup_{P^{\otimes n}\in\mathcal E_{n,d,\epsilon}}
\mathbb E_{P^{\otimes n}}\!\left[\left(\widehat\tau_n^{\mathrm{hyb}}-\tau(P)\right)^2\right]
\le
C_\epsilon\left\{\frac1n+\frac{d^2}{n^2(\log n)^2}\right\}.
\]
\end{itemize}
Then for every \(n,d\in\mathbb N\) with \(0<n\), \(N_\epsilon\le n\), and \(d\le \rho_\epsilon n\log n\), let \(K_\epsilon=\max\{C_\epsilon,4\}\). Define the \(C_\epsilon,\epsilon\)-dependent selected estimator \(\widehat\tau^{\mathrm{sel}}_{C_\epsilon,\epsilon}\) to be \(\widehat\tau_n^{\mathrm{hyb}}\) when
\[
C_\epsilon\left\{\frac1n+\frac{d^2}{n^2(\log n)^2}\right\}
\le
\frac1n+4(1/2-\epsilon)^2
\]
and to be \(\widehat\tau_{\mathrm{ctr}}\) otherwise. This selected estimator satisfies
\[
\mathsf R_{n,d,\epsilon}\le
\sup_{P^{\otimes n}\in\mathcal E_{n,d,\epsilon}}
\mathbb E_{P^{\otimes n}}\!\left[\left(\widehat\tau^{\mathrm{sel}}_{C_\epsilon,\epsilon}-\tau(P)\right)^2\right]
\le
K_\epsilon\left[
\frac1n+
\min\left\{\frac{d^2}{n^2(\log n)^2},(1/2-\epsilon)^2\right\}
\right],
\]
where \(\mathsf R_{n,d,\epsilon}\) is the minimax risk of \cref{obj:def:minimax-risk}.

11adce4ace6a5e9f6b66a22d1f31674d68388ec8.title: Iid sampling
11adce4ace6a5e9f6b66a22d1f31674d68388ec8.body:
The observations \(O_1,\ldots,O_n\) are independent and identically distributed with single-observation law \(P\):
\[
O_1,\ldots,O_n \stackrel{\mathrm{iid}}{\sim} P.
\]

d599dca9aa42c491c29452a502e2d96531401546.title: Fixed overlap
d599dca9aa42c491c29452a502e2d96531401546.body:
For every category \(k\) with \(p_k>0\), the treatment probability \(\pi_k\) satisfies
\[
\epsilon \le \pi_k \le 1-\epsilon.
\]

aec9b9d35a41a1b038cb6964021b0a9e9f241e69.title: Potential-outcome consistency
aec9b9d35a41a1b038cb6964021b0a9e9f241e69.body:
The observed outcome agrees almost surely with the potential outcome realized under the observed treatment:
\[
Y=Y(A)\quad\text{almost surely}.
\]

e6aa9248be4ed56bf3fd1524ed8d7858219d5f2f.title: Conditional exchangeability
e6aa9248be4ed56bf3fd1524ed8d7858219d5f2f.body:
The binary potential outcomes are conditionally independent of treatment given covariates:
\[
(Y(0),Y(1))\perp A\mid X.
\]

694ac0cff3d6baf78b8c673290966e39807f554c.title: Overlap cone \(\mathcal C_\epsilon\)
694ac0cff3d6baf78b8c673290966e39807f554c.body:
The overlap-restricted cone of nonnegative four-cell vectors is
\[
\mathcal C_\epsilon
:=
\left\{
u=(u_{00},u_{01},u_{10},u_{11})\in\mathbb R_+^4:
\epsilon(u_{00}+u_{01}+u_{10}+u_{11})
\le
u_{10}+u_{11}
\le
(1-\epsilon)(u_{00}+u_{01}+u_{10}+u_{11})
\right\}.
\]

4dc9d8b519de435032eb6d78d4fde7023bdc8e70.title: Cell functional \(\phi(u)\)
4dc9d8b519de435032eb6d78d4fde7023bdc8e70.body:
For \(u=(u_{00},u_{01},u_{10},u_{11})\in\mathcal C_\epsilon\), with \(\mathcal C_\epsilon\) as in \(\cref{obj:def:overlap-cone}\), define
\[
\phi(u)
=
(u_{00}+u_{01}+u_{10}+u_{11})
\left\{
\frac{u_{11}}{u_{10}+u_{11}}
-
\frac{u_{01}}{u_{00}+u_{01}}
\right\}
\]
when \(u\ne(0,0,0,0)\), and set
\[
\phi(0,0,0,0)=0.
\]

f395034b4175ea74fe0eacb8c07de8fee603c125.title: Average treatment effect \(\tau(P)\)
f395034b4175ea74fe0eacb8c07de8fee603c125.body:
Define the average treatment effect functional by
\[
\tau(P)
=
\sum_{k=1}^{d} p_k(\mu_{1k}-\mu_{0k})
=
\sum_{k=1}^{d}\phi(q_k).
\]

6fe1c9625449088162283f696c1080c07290a6be.body:
For \(d=2\), set
\[
p_1=p_2=\frac12,\qquad
\pi_1=\epsilon,\qquad
\pi_2=1-\epsilon,\qquad
\mu_{01}=\mu_{02}=0,\qquad
\mu_{11}=1,\qquad
\mu_{12}=0.
\]
Define the corresponding full-data extension by drawing
\[
(Y(0),Y(1))=(0,\mathbf 1\{X=1\})
\]
and then drawing \(A\mid X=k\sim\mathsf{Bernoulli}(\pi_k)\).

92806ca0fadde5b1ca0a42ec637acd0b2bdd1743.title: Hybrid estimator \(\widehat\tau_n^{\mathrm{hyb}}\)
92806ca0fadde5b1ca0a42ec637acd0b2bdd1743.body:
Set \(I_0=\{1,\ldots,\lfloor n/2\rfloor\}\), \(I_1=\{\lfloor n/2\rfloor+1,\ldots,n\}\), \(m_j=|I_j|\), and \(L=\log(en)\). Set \(A=6\), \(\lambda_0=256\), \(b_0=4096\), and
\[
D_A=8\log(9A/8)=8\log(27/4).
\]
Define
\[
\alpha_0=\min\left\{1,\frac1{32\log A},\frac1{256D_A}\right\}.
\]
For \(n\ge2\), set
\[
M(n)=\max\{2,\lfloor\alpha_0L\rfloor\},
\qquad
B(n)=\frac{b_0L}{m_1}.
\]
Let \(N_0\) be the least numerical cutoff such that, for every \(n\ge N_0\),
\[
\alpha_0L\ge2,\qquad 4M(n)^2\le m_1,\qquad \frac{4M(n)}{m_1}\le \frac{3B(n)}4.
\]
For \(n\ge N_0\), abbreviate \(M=M(n)\) and \(B=B(n)\), and define
\[
\widehat{\mathcal H}_n=\left\{k:\sum_{a,y}N^{(0)}_{aky}>\lambda_0L\right\},
\qquad
\widehat{\mathcal L}_n=\widehat{\mathcal H}_n^c.
\]
Set
\[
N_k^{(1)}=\sum_{a,y}N^{(1)}_{aky},
\qquad
N_{ak}^{(1)}=\sum_yN^{(1)}_{aky}.
\]
For each category \(k\), define
\[
\widehat h_k=\frac{N_k^{(1)}}{m_1}\left\{\frac{N^{(1)}_{1k1}}{N^{(1)}_{1k}}\mathbf1\{N^{(1)}_{1k}>0\}-\frac{N^{(1)}_{0k1}}{N^{(1)}_{0k}}\mathbf1\{N^{(1)}_{0k}>0\}\right\}.
\]
Let
\[
H_M(x)=\frac{1-T_M(1-2x)}{2M^2},
\qquad
E_M(x)=\frac{H_M(x)}x,
\qquad
G_M(x)=\frac{1-E_M(x)}x,
\]
where \(E_M\) and \(G_M\) are defined at zero by polynomial continuation. For \(u=(u_{00},u_{01},u_{10},u_{11})\), set
\[
s_a(u)=u_{a0}+u_{a1},
\qquad
s(u)=s_0(u)+s_1(u),
\qquad
t_1(u)=u_{11},
\qquad
t_0(u)=u_{01}.
\]
Define
\[
P_{M,B}(u)=\frac{s(u)t_1(u)}B G_M\!\left(\frac{s_1(u)}B\right)-\frac{s(u)t_0(u)}B G_M\!\left(\frac{s_0(u)}B\right).
\]
Expand \(P_{M,B}\) as
\[
P_{M,B}(u)=\sum_{|r|\le M}c_ru^r.
\]
Then set
\[
\widehat P_k=\sum_{|r|\le M}c_r\frac{\prod_{a,y}(N^{(1)}_{aky})_{r_{ay}}}{(m_1)_{|r|}},
\qquad
\widehat T_{\mathcal H}=\sum_{k\in\widehat{\mathcal H}_n}\widehat h_k,
\qquad
\widehat T_{\mathcal L}=\sum_{k\in\widehat{\mathcal L}_n}\widehat P_k.
\]
The truncated balanced ratio-polynomial hybrid estimator is
\[
\widehat\tau_n^{\mathrm{hyb}}=\max\{-1,\min(1,\widehat T_{\mathcal H}+\widehat T_{\mathcal L})\}.
\]
For \(n<N_0\), set \(\widehat{\mathcal L}_n=\varnothing\) and apply the ratio branch to every category. The construction is independent of the overlap constant and is computable in \(O(dM^4)\) arithmetic operations.

52f30b0febf85e8c73f19dcdf885e4ffdc965e10.title: Experiment class \(\mathcal E_{n,d,\epsilon}\)
52f30b0febf85e8c73f19dcdf885e4ffdc965e10.body:
For a single-observation law \(P\) on \(\{1,\ldots,d\}\times\{0,1\}^2\), write
\[
p_k=P(X=k),
\qquad
\pi_k=P(A=1\mid X=k).
\]

\[
\mathcal E_{n,d,\epsilon}
:=
\left\{
P^{\otimes n}:
P\in\mathsf{Prob}(\{1,\ldots,d\}\times\{0,1\}^2),
\ P \text{ satisfies the overlap condition}
\right\}.
\]

5b75139731a3a67920eb0d625cf60140fe3c1800.title: Average treatment effect \(\tau(P)\)
5b75139731a3a67920eb0d625cf60140fe3c1800.body:
For a single-observation law \(P\), define
\[
\mu_{ak}=E_P[Y\mid A=a,X=k],
\qquad
q_{aky}=P(A=a,X=k,Y=y),
\qquad
q_k=(q_{0k0},q_{0k1},q_{1k0},q_{1k1}).
\]
The average treatment effect functional is
\[
\tau(P)
=
\sum_{k=1}^{d} p_k(\mu_{1k}-\mu_{0k})
=
\sum_{k=1}^{d}\phi(q_k).
\]

c80192cd654c51601b2584963e5daa2d649b0e0c.title: Potential-outcome consistency
c80192cd654c51601b2584963e5daa2d649b0e0c.body:

7662a2bcbbbf164f4a6eb8316a4c34090ac099bf.title: Pilot sandwich probability
7662a2bcbbbf164f4a6eb8316a4c34090ac099bf.body:
For a sample \(O_1,\ldots,O_n\), let \(L=\log(en)\), let \(m_0=|I_0|\), and, for a threshold \(t>0\), set
\[
\widehat{\mathcal H}=\{k:N_k^{(0)}>tL\},
\qquad
\widehat{\mathcal L}=\widehat{\mathcal H}^{c},
\qquad
B_-(t)=\frac{tL}{2m_0},
\qquad
B_+(t)=\frac{2tL}{m_0}.
\]
For a single-observation law \(P\), write
\[
p_k=P(X=k).
\]
Then the following assertions hold.
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Arbitrary polynomial order.)} For every \(K>0\) and every \(c>0\), there exist constants \(t_0>0\), \(C>0\), and \(N\) such that, for every \(t\ge t_0\), every \(n\ge N\), every alphabet size \(d\) satisfying
\[
d\le c\,n\log(en),
\]
every single-observation law \(P\) on \(\{1,\ldots,d\}\times\{0,1\}\times\{0,1\}\), and every sample law \(\mu_n\) satisfying \cref{obj:ass:iid-sampling},
\[
\mu_n\!\left(
\widehat{\mathcal H}\not\subseteq\{k:p_k\ge B_-(t)\}
\ \text{or}\
\widehat{\mathcal L}\not\subseteq\{k:p_k\le B_+(t)\}
\right)
\le C n^{-K}.
\]
\item \textbf{(Fixed calibration.)} For every \(c>0\), there exist constants \(C>0\) and \(N\) such that, for every \(n\ge N\), every alphabet size \(d\) satisfying
\[
d\le c\,n\log(en),
\]
every single-observation law \(P\) on \(\{1,\ldots,d\}\times\{0,1\}\times\{0,1\}\), and every sample law \(\mu_n\) satisfying \cref{obj:ass:iid-sampling},
\[
\mu_n\!\left(
\widehat{\mathcal H}\not\subseteq\{k:p_k\ge B_-(256)\}
\ \text{or}\
\widehat{\mathcal L}\not\subseteq\{k:p_k\le B_+(256)\}
\right)
\le C n^{-4}.
\]
\end{itemize}

1283afa547e47df820af6dad8a2af94a3024e9fd.title: Iid observed data
1283afa547e47df820af6dad8a2af94a3024e9fd.body:
Let \(O=(X,A,Y)\), where \(X\) is the discrete covariate coordinate taking values in \(\{1,\ldots,d\}\), \(A\in\{0,1\}\) is the treatment coordinate, and \(Y\in\{0,1\}\) is the observed outcome coordinate. The observations \(O_1,\ldots,O_n\) are independent and identically distributed with single-observation law \(P\):
\[
O_1,\ldots,O_n \stackrel{\mathrm{iid}}{\sim} P.
\]

13432d889a318a8bf1df86f1879782edbfbfb569.title: Consistency of outcomes
13432d889a318a8bf1df86f1879782edbfbfb569.body:
For each treatment value \(a\in\{0,1\}\), let \(Y(a)\) denote the potential outcome under treatment \(a\); in particular, \(Y(0)\) and \(Y(1)\) are the control and treated potential outcomes. The realized potential outcome under the observed treatment is \(Y(A)\). The observed outcome agrees almost surely with the realized potential outcome:
\[
Y=Y(A)\quad\text{almost surely}.
\]

dac2f066cb090e71b581f85b02e381463c506688.title: Experiment class \(\mathcal E_{n,d,\epsilon}\)
dac2f066cb090e71b581f85b02e381463c506688.body:
For a single-observation law \(P\) as in \(\cref{obj:ass:iid-sampling}\), define the category mass and treatment probability
\[
p_k=P(X=k),
\qquad
\pi_k=P(A=1\mid X=k),

67988ecd17977a14ad1f3e640d876f2ba3a91508.title: Hybrid estimator \(\widehat\tau_n^{\mathrm{hyb}}\)
67988ecd17977a14ad1f3e640d876f2ba3a91508.body:
Set
\[
I_0=\{1,\ldots,\lfloor n/2\rfloor\},
\qquad
I_1=\{\lfloor n/2\rfloor+1,\ldots,n\},
\qquad
m_j=|I_j|,
\qquad
L=\log(en).
\]
Set \(A=6\), \(\lambda_0=256\), \(b_0=4096\), and
\[
D_A=8\log(9A/8)=8\log(27/4).
\]
Define
\[
\alpha_0=\min\left\{1,\frac1{32\log A},\frac1{256D_A}\right\}.
\]
For \(n\ge2\), set
\[
M(n)=\max\{2,\lfloor\alpha_0L\rfloor\},
\qquad
B(n)=\frac{b_0L}{m_1}.
\]
Let \(N_0\) be the least numerical cutoff such that, for every \(n\ge N_0\),
\[
\alpha_0L\ge2,
\qquad
4M(n)^2\le m_1,
\qquad
\frac{4M(n)}{m_1}\le \frac{3B(n)}4.
\]
For \(n\ge N_0\), abbreviate \(M=M(n)\) and \(B=B(n)\), and define
\[
\widehat{\mathcal H}_n=\left\{k:\sum_{a,y}N^{(0)}_{aky}>\lambda_0L\right\},
\qquad
\widehat{\mathcal L}_n=\widehat{\mathcal H}_n^c.
\]
Set
\[
N_k^{(1)}=\sum_{a,y}N^{(1)}_{aky},
\qquad
N_{ak}^{(1)}=\sum_yN^{(1)}_{aky}.
\]
For each category \(k\), define
\[
\widehat h_k=\frac{N_k^{(1)}}{m_1}
\left\{
\frac{N^{(1)}_{1k1}}{N^{(1)}_{1k}}\mathbf1\{N^{(1)}_{1k}>0\}
-
\frac{N^{(1)}_{0k1}}{N^{(1)}_{0k}}\mathbf1\{N^{(1)}_{0k}>0\}
\right\}.
\]
Let
\[
H_M(x)=\frac{1-T_M(1-2x)}{2M^2},
\qquad
E_M(x)=\frac{H_M(x)}x,
\qquad
G_M(x)=\frac{1-E_M(x)}x,
\]
where \(E_M\) and \(G_M\) are defined at zero by polynomial continuation. For \(u=(u_{00},u_{01},u_{10},u_{11})\), set
\[
s_a(u)=u_{a0}+u_{a1},
\qquad
s(u)=s_0(u)+s_1(u),
\qquad
t_1(u)=u_{11},
\qquad
t_0(u)=u_{01}.
\]
Define
\[
P_{M,B}(u)=
\frac{s(u)t_1(u)}B G_M\!\left(\frac{s_1(u)}B\right)
-
\frac{s(u)t_0(u)}B G_M\!\left(\frac{s_0(u)}B\right).
\]
Expand \(P_{M,B}\) as
\[
P_{M,B}(u)=\sum_{|r|\le M}c_ru^r.
\]
Then set
\[
\widehat P_k
=
\sum_{|r|\le M}
c_r
\frac{\prod_{a,y}(N^{(1)}_{aky})_{r_{ay}}}{(m_1)_{|r|}},
\qquad
\widehat T_{\mathcal H}
=
\sum_{k\in\widehat{\mathcal H}_n}\widehat h_k,
\qquad
\widehat T_{\mathcal L}
=
\sum_{k\in\widehat{\mathcal L}_n}\widehat P_k.
\]

\[
\widehat\tau_n^{\mathrm{hyb}}
=
\max\{-1,\min(1,\widehat T_{\mathcal H}+\widehat T_{\mathcal L})\}.
\]

f9eb0a4d0becd8684db6bc264b013a695006f2b8.body:
The observations \(O_1,\ldots,O_n\), with \(O_i=(X_i,A_i,Y_i)\), are independent and identically distributed with single-observation law \(P\):
\[
O_1,\ldots,O_n \stackrel{\mathrm{iid}}{\sim} P.
\]

\[
p_k=P(X=k),
\qquad
\pi_k=P(A=1\mid X=k).
\]

1aeb6484b98156b8143e9d9d68d648f5d4cfeedb.body:
Let \(Y(0)\) and \(Y(1)\) denote the binary potential outcomes under control and treatment. The observed outcome agrees almost surely with the potential outcome realized under the observed treatment:
\[
Y=Y(A)\quad\text{almost surely}.
\]

H_M(x)=\frac{1-T_M(1-2x)}{2M^2},
\qquad
E_M(x)=\frac{H_M(x)}x,
\qquad
G_M(x)=\frac{1-E_M(x)}x,
\]
where \(E_M\) and \(G_M\) are defined at zero by polynomial continuation. For \(u=(u_{00},u_{01},u_{10},u_{11})\), set
\[
s_a(u)=u_{a0}+u_{a1},
\qquad
s(u)=s_0(u)+s_1(u),
\qquad
t_1(u)=u_{11},
\qquad
t_0(u)=u_{01}.
\]
Define
\[
P_{M,B}(u)=\frac{s(u)t_1(u)}B G_M\!\left(\frac{s_1(u)}B\right)-\frac{s(u)t_0(u)}B G_M\!\left(\frac{s_0(u)}B\right).
\]
Expand \(P_{M,B}\) as
\[
P_{M,B}(u)=\sum_{|r|\le M}c_ru^r.
\]
Then set
\[
\widehat P_k=\sum_{|r|\le M}c_r\frac{\prod_{a,y}(N^{(1)}_{aky})_{r_{ay}}}{(m_1)_{|r|}},
\qquad
\widehat T_{\mathcal H}=\sum_{k\in\widehat{\mathcal H}_n}\widehat h_k,
\qquad
\widehat T_{\mathcal L}=\sum_{k\in\widehat{\mathcal L}_n}\widehat P_k.
\]
The truncated balanced ratio-polynomial hybrid estimator is
\[
\widehat\tau_n^{\mathrm{hyb}}=\max\{-1,\min(1,\widehat T_{\mathcal H}+\widehat T_{\mathcal L})\}.
\]
For \(n<N_0\), set \(\widehat{\mathcal L}_n=\varnothing\) and apply the ratio branch to every category. The construction is overlap-adaptive and is computable in \(O(dM^4)\) arithmetic operations.

811034fb9200c123708fa3c5f8bb9ed324167416.title: Hybrid estimator \(\widehat\tau_n^{\mathrm{hyb}}\)
811034fb9200c123708fa3c5f8bb9ed324167416.body:
Set
\[
I_0=\{1,\ldots,\lfloor n/2\rfloor\},
\qquad
I_1=\{\lfloor n/2\rfloor+1,\ldots,n\},
\qquad
m_j=|I_j|,
\qquad
L=\log(en).
\]
For \(j\in\{0,1\}\), let \(N^{(j)}_{aky}\) be the split-\(j\) count of observations with \((A,X,Y)=(a,k,y)\). Set
\[
A=6,
\qquad
\lambda_0=256,
\qquad
b_0=4096,
\qquad
D_A=8\log(9A/8)=8\log(27/4),
\]
and
\[
\alpha_0=\min\left\{1,\frac1{32\log A},\frac1{256D_A}\right\}.
\]
For \(n\ge2\), set
\[
M(n)=\max\{2,\lfloor\alpha_0L\rfloor\},
\qquad
B(n)=\frac{b_0L}{m_1}.
\]
Let \(N_0\) be the least numerical cutoff such that, for every \(n\ge N_0\),
\[
\alpha_0L\ge2,
\qquad
4M(n)^2\le m_1,
\qquad
\frac{4M(n)}{m_1}\le\frac{3B(n)}4.
\]
For \(n\ge N_0\), abbreviate \(M=M(n)\) and \(B=B(n)\), and define
\[
\widehat{\mathcal H}_n=\left\{k:\sum_{a,y}N^{(0)}_{aky}>\lambda_0L\right\},
\qquad
\widehat{\mathcal L}_n=\widehat{\mathcal H}_n^c.
\]
Set
\[
N_k^{(1)}=\sum_{a,y}N^{(1)}_{aky},
\qquad
N_{ak}^{(1)}=\sum_yN^{(1)}_{aky},
\]
and, for each category \(k\),
\[
\widehat h_k=\frac{N_k^{(1)}}{m_1}\left\{\frac{N^{(1)}_{1k1}}{N^{(1)}_{1k}}\mathbf1\{N^{(1)}_{1k}>0\}-\frac{N^{(1)}_{0k1}}{N^{(1)}_{0k}}\mathbf1\{N^{(1)}_{0k}>0\}\right\}.
\]
Define
\[
H_M(x)=\frac{1-T_M(1-2x)}{2M^2},
\qquad
E_M(x)=\frac{H_M(x)}x,
\qquad
G_M(x)=\frac{1-E_M(x)}x,
\]
with \(E_M\) and \(G_M\) defined at zero by polynomial continuation. For \(u=(u_{00},u_{01},u_{10},u_{11})\), set
\[
s_a(u)=u_{a0}+u_{a1},
\qquad
s(u)=s_0(u)+s_1(u),
\qquad
t_1(u)=u_{11},
\qquad
t_0(u)=u_{01}.
\]
Define
\[
P_{M,B}(u)=\frac{s(u)t_1(u)}B G_M\!\left(\frac{s_1(u)}B\right)-\frac{s(u)t_0(u)}B G_M\!\left(\frac{s_0(u)}B\right),
\]
and expand
\[
P_{M,B}(u)=\sum_{|r|\le M}c_ru^r.
\]
Set
\[
\widehat P_k=\sum_{|r|\le M}c_r\frac{\prod_{a,y}(N^{(1)}_{aky})_{r_{ay}}}{(m_1)_{|r|}},
\qquad
\widehat T_{\mathcal H}=\sum_{k\in\widehat{\mathcal H}_n}\widehat h_k,
\qquad
\widehat T_{\mathcal L}=\sum_{k\in\widehat{\mathcal L}_n}\widehat P_k.
\]
The truncated balanced ratio-polynomial hybrid estimator is
\[
\widehat\tau_n^{\mathrm{hyb}}=\max\{-1,\min(1,\widehat T_{\mathcal H}+\widehat T_{\mathcal L})\}.
\]
For \(n<N_0\), set \(\widehat{\mathcal L}_n=\varnothing\) and apply the ratio branch to every category. The construction is computed from the sample and the fixed numerical constants above, and is computable in \(O(dM^4)\) arithmetic operations.

7aef41d8540a21b9dc954a4441b2b8b9e8268107.title: Iid sampling law
7aef41d8540a21b9dc954a4441b2b8b9e8268107.body:
The observations \(O_1,\ldots,O_n\) are independent and identically distributed with single-observation law \(P\), where \(O=(X,A,Y)\) and the covariate \(X\) takes values in \(\{1,\ldots,d\}\):
\[
O_1,\ldots,O_n \stackrel{\mathrm{iid}}{\sim} P.
\]
For each category \(k\in\{1,\ldots,d\}\), let
\[
p_k=P(X=k)
\]
denote the category mass, and let
\[
\pi_k=P(A=1\mid X=k)
\]
denote the treatment probability in category \(k\).

108183807d35b8e3a879364c9b67da17b59075c8.title: Potential-outcome consistency
108183807d35b8e3a879364c9b67da17b59075c8.body:
For \(a\in\{0,1\}\), \(Y(a)\) denotes the potential outcome realized under treatment \(a\). The observed outcome agrees almost surely with the potential outcome realized under the observed treatment:
\[
Y=Y(A)\quad\text{almost surely}.
\]

3e155fd3a9459ceb6b06d8a1e31d332c5207bd9c.title: Average treatment effect \(\tau(P)\)
3e155fd3a9459ceb6b06d8a1e31d332c5207bd9c.body:
For each \(a\in\{0,1\}\) and \(k\in\{1,\ldots,d\}\), define the conditional mean outcome
\[
\mu_{ak}=E_P[Y\mid A=a,X=k].
\]
For \(a,y\in\{0,1\}\) and \(k\in\{1,\ldots,d\}\), define the joint cell mass
\[
q_{aky}=P(A=a,X=k,Y=y),
\]
and write
\[
q_k=(q_{0k0},q_{0k1},q_{1k0},q_{1k1})
\]
for the corresponding four-cell vector in category \(k\). The average treatment effect functional is
\[
\tau(P)
=
\sum_{k=1}^{d} p_k(\mu_{1k}-\mu_{0k})
=
\sum_{k=1}^{d}\phi(q_k).
\]

aa58fc2eadc2a0c26789cb5ecc7939507f87f018.title: Pilot sandwich bound
aa58fc2eadc2a0c26789cb5ecc7939507f87f018.body:
For a sample \(O_1,\ldots,O_n\), let \(L=\log(en)\), let \(m_0=|I_0|\), and, for a threshold \(t\),
\[
\widehat{\mathcal H}=\{k:N_k^{(0)}>tL\},
\qquad
\widehat{\mathcal L}=\widehat{\mathcal H}^{c},
\qquad
B_-=\frac{tL}{2m_0},
\qquad
B_+=\frac{2tL}{m_0}.
\]
The following two assertions hold.
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Arbitrary polynomial order.)} For every \(K>0\) and every \(c>0\), there exist constants \(t_0>0\), \(C>0\), and \(N\) such that, for every \(t\ge t_0\), every \(n\ge N\), every alphabet size \(d\) satisfying
\[
d\le c\,n\log(en),
\]
every single-observation law \(P\) on \(\{1,\ldots,d\}\times\{0,1\}\times\{0,1\}\), and every sample law \(\mu_n\) satisfying \cref{obj:ass:iid-sampling},
\[
\mu_n\!\left(
\widehat{\mathcal H}\not\subseteq\{k:p_k\ge B_-\}
\ \text{or}\
\widehat{\mathcal L}\not\subseteq\{k:p_k\le B_+\}
\right)
\le C n^{-K}.
\]
\item \textbf{(Fixed calibration.)} For every \(c>0\), there exist constants \(C>0\) and \(N\) such that, with \(t=256\), for every \(n\ge N\), every alphabet size \(d\) satisfying
\[
d\le c\,n\log(en),
\]
every single-observation law \(P\) on \(\{1,\ldots,d\}\times\{0,1\}\times\{0,1\}\), and every sample law \(\mu_n\) satisfying \cref{obj:ass:iid-sampling},
\[
\mu_n\!\left(
\widehat{\mathcal H}\not\subseteq\{k:p_k\ge B_-\}
\ \text{or}\
\widehat{\mathcal L}\not\subseteq\{k:p_k\le B_+\}
\right)
\le C n^{-4}.
\]
\end{itemize}

2a4153cc89d8f2d2f538edfc0cda5f9385acb398.title: Pilot category count
2a4153cc89d8f2d2f538edfc0cda5f9385acb398.body:
For each \(a,y\in\{0,1\}\) and \(k\in\{1,\ldots,d\}\), let
\[
N_{aky}^{(0)}
=
\sum_{i\in I_0}\mathbf 1\{A_i=a,\ X_i=k,\ Y_i=y\}.
\]
The pilot category count is
\[
N_k^{(0)}
=
\sum_{i\in I_0}\mathbf 1\{X_i=k\}
=
\sum_{a,y\in\{0,1\}}N_{aky}^{(0)}.
\]

109793692ace455ca5962e1d78e9e18401c7059c.title: Iid observed sampling
109793692ace455ca5962e1d78e9e18401c7059c.body:
The observations \(O_1,\ldots,O_n\) are independent and identically distributed with single-observation law \(P\):
\[
O_1,\ldots,O_n \stackrel{\mathrm{iid}}{\sim} P.
\]
For \(O=(X,A,Y)\), the covariate \(X\) takes values in \(\{1,\ldots,d\}\). For each category \(k\), define
\[
p_k=P(X=k),
\qquad
\pi_k=P(A=1\mid X=k),
\qquad
\mu_{ak}=E_P[Y\mid A=a,X=k].
\]

ce7747e55e9a0e676810b43746425f49d0d3af52.title: Potential-outcome consistency
ce7747e55e9a0e676810b43746425f49d0d3af52.body:
Let \(Y(0)\) and \(Y(1)\) denote the binary potential outcomes under control and treatment, and let \(Y(A)\) denote the potential outcome realized under the observed treatment \(A\). The observed outcome satisfies
\[
Y=Y(A)\quad\text{almost surely}.
\]

9febfa12a6de35052c3ebb50977f165890098692.title: Hybrid estimator \(\widehat\tau_n^{\mathrm{hyb}}\)
9febfa12a6de35052c3ebb50977f165890098692.body:
Set
\[
I_0=\{1,\ldots,\lfloor n/2\rfloor\},
\qquad
I_1=\{\lfloor n/2\rfloor+1,\ldots,n\},
\qquad
m_j=|I_j|,
\qquad
L=\log(en).
\]
For \(j\in\{0,1\}\), \(a,y\in\{0,1\}\), and \(k\in\{1,\ldots,d\}\), define the split-cell count
\[
N_{aky}^{(j)}
=
\sum_{i\in I_j}\mathbf 1\{A_i=a,\ X_i=k,\ Y_i=y\}.
\]
Set \(A_0=6\), \(\lambda_0=256\), \(b_0=4096\), and
\[
D_{A_0}=8\log(9A_0/8)=8\log(27/4).
\]
Define
\[
\alpha_0=\min\left\{1,\frac1{32\log A_0},\frac1{256D_{A_0}}\right\}.
\]
For \(n\ge2\), set
\[
M(n)=\max\{2,\lfloor\alpha_0L\rfloor\},
\qquad
B(n)=\frac{b_0L}{m_1}.
\]
Let \(N_0\) be the least numerical cutoff such that, for every \(n\ge N_0\),
\[
\alpha_0L\ge2,
\qquad
4M(n)^2\le m_1,
\qquad
\frac{4M(n)}{m_1}\le \frac{3B(n)}4.
\]
For \(n\ge N_0\), abbreviate \(M=M(n)\) and \(B=B(n)\), and define
\[
\widehat{\mathcal H}_n
=
\left\{k:\sum_{a,y\in\{0,1\}}N_{aky}^{(0)}>\lambda_0L\right\},
\qquad
\widehat{\mathcal L}_n=\widehat{\mathcal H}_n^c.
\]
Set
\[
N_k^{(1)}=\sum_{a,y\in\{0,1\}}N_{aky}^{(1)},
\qquad
N_{ak}^{(1)}=\sum_{y\in\{0,1\}}N_{aky}^{(1)}.
\]
For each category \(k\), define
\[
\widehat h_k
=
\frac{N_k^{(1)}}{m_1}
\left\{
\frac{N_{1k1}^{(1)}}{N_{1k}^{(1)}}\mathbf1\{N_{1k}^{(1)}>0\}
-
\frac{N_{0k1}^{(1)}}{N_{0k}^{(1)}}\mathbf1\{N_{0k}^{(1)}>0\}
\right\}.
\]
Let
\[
H_M(x)=\frac{1-T_M(1-2x)}{2M^2},
\qquad
E_M(x)=\frac{H_M(x)}x,
\qquad
G_M(x)=\frac{1-E_M(x)}x,
\]
where \(E_M\) and \(G_M\) are defined at zero by polynomial continuation. For \(u=(u_{00},u_{01},u_{10},u_{11})\), set
\[
s_a(u)=u_{a0}+u_{a1},
\qquad
s(u)=s_0(u)+s_1(u),
\qquad
t_1(u)=u_{11},
\qquad
t_0(u)=u_{01}.
\]
Define
\[
P_{M,B}(u)
=
\frac{s(u)t_1(u)}B G_M\!\left(\frac{s_1(u)}B\right)
-
\frac{s(u)t_0(u)}B G_M\!\left(\frac{s_0(u)}B\right).
\]
Expand \(P_{M,B}\) as
\[
P_{M,B}(u)=\sum_{|r|\le M}c_ru^r.
\]
Then set
\[
\widehat P_k
=
\sum_{|r|\le M}
c_r
\frac{\prod_{a,y\in\{0,1\}}(N_{aky}^{(1)})_{r_{ay}}}{(m_1)_{|r|}},
\qquad
\widehat T_{\mathcal H}
=
\sum_{k\in\widehat{\mathcal H}_n}\widehat h_k,
\qquad
\widehat T_{\mathcal L}
=
\sum_{k\in\widehat{\mathcal L}_n}\widehat P_k.
\]
The truncated balanced ratio-polynomial hybrid estimator is
\[
\widehat\tau_n^{\mathrm{hyb}}
=
\max\{-1,\min(1,\widehat T_{\mathcal H}+\widehat T_{\mathcal L})\}.
\]
For \(n<N_0\), set \(\widehat{\mathcal L}_n=\varnothing\) and apply the ratio branch to every category. The construction is independent of the overlap constant and is computable in \(O(dM^4)\) arithmetic operations.

6c7fbe6f015231c852b74166c6870e0ad0a6f85e.title: Two-category confounding witness
6c7fbe6f015231c852b74166c6870e0ad0a6f85e.body:
For every real \(\epsilon\) with \(0<\epsilon\le 1/2\), let \(Q\) be the full-data law constructed in \cref{obj:def:two-category-witness}, and let \(P\) be its observed marginal law for \(O=(X,A,Y)\). Then:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Consistency.)} \(Q\) satisfies \cref{obj:ass:consistency}.
\item \textbf{(Conditional exchangeability.)} \(Q\) satisfies \cref{obj:ass:conditional-exchangeability}.
\item \textbf{(Overlap.)} \(P\) satisfies the overlap condition of \cref{obj:ass:overlap} with overlap parameter \(\epsilon\).
\end{itemize}
The average treatment effect functional in \cref{obj:def:ate-functional} and the naive observed contrast under \(P\) obey
\[
\tau(P)=\frac12,
\qquad
E_P[Y\mid A=1]-E_P[Y\mid A=0]=\epsilon .
\]

a3fa0dad2b4735b1e93b7c84c090316039b5e88b.title: Iid sampling law
a3fa0dad2b4735b1e93b7c84c090316039b5e88b.body:
The observed data are \(O_i=(X_i,A_i,Y_i)\), \(i=1,\ldots,n\), with
\[
O_1,\ldots,O_n \stackrel{\mathrm{iid}}{\sim} P.
\]
The covariate \(X\) takes values in \(\{1,\ldots,d\}\). For each \(k\in\{1,\ldots,d\}\), let
\[
p_k=P(X=k),
\qquad
\pi_k=P(A=1\mid X=k).
\]
For each admissible treatment--category cell \((a,k)\), let
\[
\mu_{ak}=E_P[Y\mid A=a,X=k].
\]

aa6165e817161b1acdc924969bff92da19656562.title: Potential-outcome consistency
aa6165e817161b1acdc924969bff92da19656562.body:
Let \(Y(0)\) and \(Y(1)\) denote the control and treated potential outcomes. The observed outcome agrees almost surely with the potential outcome realized under the observed treatment:
\[
Y=Y(A)\quad\text{almost surely}.
\]

279c9d4157544d68ec25adddd10994ea28e95e9d.title: Average treatment effect \(\tau(P)\)
279c9d4157544d68ec25adddd10994ea28e95e9d.body:
For \(a,y\in\{0,1\}\) and \(k\in\{1,\ldots,d\}\), define the joint cell mass
\[
q_{aky}=P(A=a,X=k,Y=y),
\]
and set
\[
q_k=(q_{0k0},q_{0k1},q_{1k0},q_{1k1}).
\]
The average treatment effect functional is
\[
\tau(P)
=
\sum_{k=1}^{d} p_k(\mu_{1k}-\mu_{0k})
=
\sum_{k=1}^{d}\phi(q_k).
\]

636000e56e267e092305ea0d52e5e1baab2924ae.title: Absolute coefficient envelope
636000e56e267e092305ea0d52e5e1baab2924ae.body:
Let \(M\in\mathbb N\), let \(B>0\), and let \(v\) be a nonnegative four-cell vector. Define
\[
P_{M,B}(u)
=
B^{-1}s(u)t_1(u)\sum_{j=0}^{M-2} g_{M,j}\{B^{-1}s_1(u)\}^j
-
B^{-1}s(u)t_0(u)\sum_{j=0}^{M-2} g_{M,j}\{B^{-1}s_0(u)\}^j .
\]
Writing \(P_{M,B}(u)=\sum_r c_r u^r\) in multi-index form over the four cells, the coefficients obey
\[
\sum_{r\in\operatorname{supp}(P_{M,B})}|c_r|\,v^r
\le
B\,6^M
\max\left\{
\left(\frac{s(v)}{B}\right)^2,
\left(\frac{s(v)}{B}\right)^M
\right\}.
\]

7fd53c6be8aa86cbf74c00383d4ce6d08a5a18c3.title: Factorial moment mean
7fd53c6be8aa86cbf74c00383d4ce6d08a5a18c3.body:
Let \(P\) be a single-observation law on the finite alphabet \(\{1,\ldots,d\}\times\{0,1\}^2\), let \(k\in\{1,\ldots,d\}\), and let \(n\ge N_0\), where \(N_0\) is the calibration cutoff. Set
\[
M(n)=\max\{2,\lfloor \alpha_0\log(en)\rfloor\},
\qquad
B(n)=b_0\log(en)/m_1 .
\]
For the four-cell vector \(q_k=(P(X=k,A=a,Y=y))_{a,y\in\{0,1\}}\), define
\[
P_{M,B}(u)
=
B^{-1}s(u)t_1(u)\sum_{j=0}^{M-2} g_{Mj}\{B^{-1}s_1(u)\}^j
-
B^{-1}s(u)t_0(u)\sum_{j=0}^{M-2} g_{Mj}\{B^{-1}s_0(u)\}^j .
\]
If \(O_1,O_2,\ldots\) are iid with law \(P\), then the factorial-moment polynomial contribution \(\widehat P_k\) computed from \(O_1,\ldots,O_n\) satisfies
\[
\mathbb E_{P^{\otimes\infty}}\!\left[\widehat P_k\right]
=
P_{M(n),B(n)}(q_k).
\]

60f5909592304318c379070f3cf50684369c9b3d.title: Factorial moment variance bound
60f5909592304318c379070f3cf50684369c9b3d.body:
Fix \(n,d\in\mathbb N\), a law \(P\in\mathsf{Prob}(\{1,\ldots,d\}\times\{0,1\}^2)\), and a category \(k\in\{1,\ldots,d\}\).  Let \(p_k=P(X=k)\) be the category mass, let \(m_1=|I_1|\), and abbreviate \(M=M(n)\) and \(B=B(n)\).  Write \(\bar P_k\) for the sparse factorial-polynomial mean of category \(k\), namely the difference between the sparse arm means for arms \(1\) and \(0\) at degree \(M\) and scale \(B\).

Assume that
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Split size.)} \(m_1>0\).
\item \textbf{(Degree and scale.)} \(M>0\) and \(B>0\).
\item \textbf{(Size calibration.)} \(4M^2\le m_1\).
\item \textbf{(Shifted mass.)} \(p_k+4M/m_1\le B\).
\item \textbf{(Mass bound.)} \(p_k\le B\).
\end{itemize}
Then the factorial-moment polynomial estimate \(\widehat P_k\), computed from the first \(n\) observations of an iid sequence with one-observation law \(P\), satisfies
\[
\mathbb E\!\left[\left(\widehat P_k-\bar P_k\right)^2\right]
\le
8(\mathrm e+1)\bigl(B\,6^M\bigr)^2 .
\]

aabbe843d1105ee6e5b53820aababf665a970ca4.title: Large calibration consequences
aabbe843d1105ee6e5b53820aababf665a970ca4.body:
Let \(N_0\) be the least numerical cutoff satisfying the calibration inequalities, and let \(n\) be a sample size. Set
\[
L=\log(en),\qquad \ell=\log n,\qquad M=M(n),\qquad B=B(n),\qquad m_1=|I_1|.
\]
Assume that
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Calibration range.)} \(n\ge N_0\).
\item \textbf{(Large logarithmic scale.)} \(L\ge240\).
\end{itemize}
Then
\[
0<\ell,\qquad
\ell\le L,\qquad
L\le2\ell,\qquad
0<m_1,\qquad
n\le2m_1,\qquad
M\le L,\qquad
B\le\frac{8192L}{n},\qquad
(6^{2M})^2L^6\le n.
\]

39b447cd114ba52f19fb7ad80716d012cb75e173.title: Polynomial cell approximation
39b447cd114ba52f19fb7ad80716d012cb75e173.body:
Let \(M\) be a positive integer, let \(B\in\mathbb R\), and let \(\epsilon>0\).  For a four-cell vector \(u=(u_{00},u_{01},u_{10},u_{11})\), write
\[
s_a(u)=u_{a0}+u_{a1},
\qquad
s(u)=s_0(u)+s_1(u).
\]
Assume that
\[
u_{ay}\ge 0\quad\text{for all }a,y\in\{0,1\},
\qquad
\epsilon s(u)\le s_1(u)\le (1-\epsilon)s(u),
\qquad
s(u)\le B.
\]
Let \(P_{M,B}\) be the four-cell polynomial
\[
P_{M,B}(u)
=
B^{-1}s(u)u_{11}\sum_{j=0}^{M-2}g_{M,j}\{B^{-1}s_1(u)\}^{j}
-
B^{-1}s(u)u_{01}\sum_{j=0}^{M-2}g_{M,j}\{B^{-1}s_0(u)\}^{j},
\]
with the coefficients \(g_{M,j}\) from the Chebyshev reciprocal construction, and let
\[
\phi(u)=
\begin{cases}
0, & u=0,\\
s(u)\left\{u_{11}/s_1(u)-u_{01}/s_0(u)\right\}, & u\ne 0.
\end{cases}
\]
Then
\[
\left|P_{M,B}(u)-\phi(u)\right|
\le
\frac{2B}{\epsilon M^2}.
\]

8a18ece101d56e16f9eb322b3b7206e2996af74f.title: False-light error envelope
8a18ece101d56e16f9eb322b3b7206e2996af74f.body:
Let \(P\) be a probability law on \(\{1,\ldots,d\}\times\{0,1\}^2\). Suppose that:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Overlap.)} For every category \(k\) with \(p_k>0\), the treatment probability satisfies
\[
\epsilon \le \pi_k \le 1-\epsilon .
\]
\item \textbf{(Calibration cutoff.)} The sample size satisfies \(n\ge N_0\), where \(N_0\) is the least numerical cutoff satisfying the calibration inequalities used in the estimator.
\item \textbf{(Logarithmic scale.)} With \(L=\log(en)\), one has \(L\ge 240\).
\end{itemize}
For \(S_k=\mathbf 1\{k\in\widehat{\mathcal L}_n\}\), the selected false-light error satisfies
\[
E_{P^{\otimes n}}\left[
\left\{
\sum_{k\in\widehat{\mathcal L}_n}
S_k\bigl(\widehat P_k-\phi(q_k)\bigr)
\right\}^2
\right]
\le
8(\mathrm e+1)8192^2
\left\{
\frac1n+\frac{d^2}{n^2(\log n)^2}
\right\}.
\]

d5b8564a176cf1386789e9c7346613a99bd7d7d8.title: Off-diagonal covariance bound
d5b8564a176cf1386789e9c7346613a99bd7d7d8.body:
For any \(n,d\), let \(P\in\mathsf{Prob}(\{1,\ldots,d\}\times\{0,1\}^2)\), and let \(k\) and \(l\) be distinct categories. Write \(M=M(n)\), \(B=B(n)\), \(m_1=|I_1|\), and \(p_k=P(X=k)\). Let \(\widehat P_k\) denote the factorial-moment polynomial estimate for category \(k\) computed from \(O_1,\ldots,O_n\), and let \(\bar P_k\) denote its sparse polynomial mean under \(P\) with degree \(M(n)\) and scale \(B(n)\).

Assume that
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Positive degree.)} \(0<M(n)\).
\item \textbf{(Positive scale.)} \(0<B(n)\).
\item \textbf{(Split size.)} \(4M(n)^2\le m_1\).
\item \textbf{(Light categories.)} \(p_k\le B(n)\) and \(p_l\le B(n)\).
\end{itemize}
Then, under the iid product law generated by \(P\),
\[
E_{P^{\otimes n}}\!\left[
  \left(\widehat P_k-\bar P_k\right)
  \left(\widehat P_l-\bar P_l\right)
\right]
\le
\frac{8M(n)^2}{m_1}\left\{B(n)6^{M(n)}\right\}^2 .
\]

20d8799e4424b62b83518d5dfd92b98e54ca2260.title: Fixed residual variance
20d8799e4424b62b83518d5dfd92b98e54ca2260.body:
For any finite index set \(I\), write \(m=|I|\), and let \((O_i)_{i\in I}\) be an iid sample from \(P\) on \(\{1,\ldots,d\}\times\{0,1\}^2\). Let \(H\subseteq\{1,\ldots,d\}\) and \(a\in\{0,1\}\). Assume:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Overlap.)} The overlap parameter \(\epsilon\) satisfies \(\epsilon>0\), and every positive-mass category obeys \(\epsilon\le \pi_k\le 1-\epsilon\).
\item \textbf{(Fixed support.)} The set \(H\) is deterministic.
\item \textbf{(Positive cell mass.)} Each category in \(H\) has positive mass: \(p_k>0\) for every \(k\in H\).
\end{itemize}
With counts computed from \((O_i)_{i\in I}\), define
\[
\mathcal R_a(H)
=
\sum_{k\in H}
N_k\frac{\mathbf 1\{N_{ak}>0\}}{N_{ak}}
\{N_{ak1}-\mu_{ak}N_{ak}\}.
\]
Then
\[
\mathbb E_{P^{\otimes I}}\!\left[\mathcal R_a(H)^2\right]
\le
\frac{2m}{\epsilon}\sum_{k\in H}p_k .
\]

fd1b2e33401f1a1bc838d67670ad32a86c53e736.title: Missing-arm envelope
fd1b2e33401f1a1bc838d67670ad32a86c53e736.body:
Let \(P\) be a probability law for \(O=(X,A,Y)\in\{1,\ldots,d\}\times\{0,1\}^2\), and let \(J\) be a finite sample-index set with \(m=|J|\). For an observation array \(z=(O_j)_{j\in J}\), write \(N_k(z)\) for the number of observations with \(X=k\), write \(N_{ak}(z)\) for the number with \(A=a\) and \(X=k\), and set
\[
Z_{ak}(z)=N_k(z)\mathbf 1\{N_{ak}(z)=0\}.
\]
For a deterministic category set \(H\), the fixed missing-arm count is \(\sum_{k\in H}Z_{ak}(z)\). Assume:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Sample size.)} \(m\ge 3\).
\item \textbf{(Overlap.)} \(P\) satisfies overlap at level \(\epsilon\), meaning that every category with \(p_k=P(X=k)>0\) has \(\epsilon\le \pi_k\le 1-\epsilon\), and \(\epsilon>0\).
\item \textbf{(Mass floor.)} \(B>0\), and \(p_k\ge B\) for every \(k\in H\).
\end{itemize}
Then, for any arm \(a\in\{0,1\}\),
\[
\int \left(\sum_{k\in H}Z_{ak}(z)\right)^2\,dP^{\otimes J}(z)
\le
m+m^2\left[
\frac{|H|}{\left(\left(\frac{m-2}{2}\epsilon\right)^2 B\right)}
\right]^2.
\]

b2906bf1eb4a8b06b1d248005a326f6ce622ed27.title: Light-cell polynomial rate
b2906bf1eb4a8b06b1d248005a326f6ce622ed27.body:
Fix an overlap parameter \(\epsilon\) with \(0<\epsilon\le 1/2\). The hybrid estimator admits a real-arithmetic implementation: there is a universal operation-count constant \(K\in\mathbb N\), \(K>0\), such that for every \(n\) and \(d\) the program reads the split-count vector, returns \(\widehat\tau_n^{\mathrm{hyb}}\) exactly, and uses at most \(K\,d\,M(n)^4\) arithmetic and comparison operations.

Moreover, there are constants \(C_\epsilon,c_\epsilon>0\) such that, for every \(n,d\), every single-observation law \(P\in\mathsf{Prob}(\{1,\ldots,d\}\times\{0,1\}^2)\), and every sample law \(P^{\otimes n}\) satisfying \(P^{\otimes n}\in\mathcal E_{n,d,\epsilon}\) as in \(\cref{obj:def:experiment-class}\), if
\[
d\le c_\epsilon n\log n,
\]
then the light-cell contribution \(\widehat T_{\mathcal L}\) satisfies
\[
E_{P^{\otimes n}}\!\left[
\left\{
\widehat T_{\mathcal L}
-
\sum_{k\in\widehat{\mathcal L}_n}\phi(q_k)
\right\}^2
\right]
\le
C_\epsilon
\left\{
\frac{1}{n}
+
\frac{d^2}{n^2(\log n)^2}
\right\}.
\]

5d4551af9805a7516ccffe6abcc18b0927a9f2db.title: Heavy-cell aggregate rate
5d4551af9805a7516ccffe6abcc18b0927a9f2db.body:
For every overlap parameter \(\epsilon\) with \(0<\epsilon<1/2\), there exist constants
\(C_\epsilon>0\) and \(\rho_\epsilon>0\), and a sample-size cutoff
\(N_\epsilon<\infty\), such that the following holds.  For every \(n,d\), every
single-observation law \(P\in\mathsf{Prob}(\{1,\ldots,d\}\times\{0,1\}^2)\), and every
sample law \(\mu_n\) for \(O_1,\ldots,O_n\), suppose that
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Sample size.)} \(n\ge N_\epsilon\).
\item \textbf{(Dimension range.)} \(d\le \rho_\epsilon n\log n\).
\item \textbf{(Experiment class.)} \(\mu_n\in\mathcal E_{n,d,\epsilon}\) for \(P\), as in
\(\cref{obj:def:experiment-class}\).
\end{itemize}
Then the mean squared error, under \(\mu_n\), of the heavy-cell aggregate ratio branch
\(\widehat T_{\mathcal H}=\sum_{k\in\widehat{\mathcal H}_n}\widehat h_k\) around the
pilot-heavy target \(\sum_{k\in\widehat{\mathcal H}_n}\phi(q_k)\) satisfies
\[
\int
\left(
\sum_{k\in\widehat{\mathcal H}_n}\widehat h_k
-
\sum_{k\in\widehat{\mathcal H}_n}\phi(q_k)
\right)^2
\,d\mu_n
\le
C_\epsilon\left\{
\frac{1}{n}
+
\frac{d^2}{n^2(\log n)^2}
\right\}.
\]

358fdae2d86b9b3e78940044b0debeb0295b1c73.title: IID observed-data model
358fdae2d86b9b3e78940044b0debeb0295b1c73.body:
The observed data are \(O_i=(X_i,A_i,Y_i)\), \(i=1,\ldots,n\), with
\[
O_1,\ldots,O_n\stackrel{\mathrm{iid}}{\sim}P.
\]
The covariate \(X\) takes values in \(\{1,\ldots,d\}\), and the treatment \(A\) and observed outcome \(Y\) are binary. For each category \(k\in\{1,\ldots,d\}\), let
\[
p_k=P(X=k)
\]
denote the category mass and let
\[
\pi_k=P(A=1\mid X=k)
\]
denote the treatment probability. For each treatment arm \(a\in\{0,1\}\), let
\[
\mu_{ak}=E_P[Y\mid A=a,X=k]
\]
denote the conditional mean outcome.

86f340883f85ff71672f00f128bbb2ab9ce06726.title: Light-cell polynomial rate
86f340883f85ff71672f00f128bbb2ab9ce06726.body:
Fix an overlap parameter \(\epsilon\). Suppose that
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Positive overlap.)} \(0<\epsilon\).
\item \textbf{(Fixed interior.)} \(\epsilon\le 1/2\).
\item \textbf{(Experiment class.)} \(n,d\in\mathbb N\), \(P\in\mathsf{Prob}(\{1,\ldots,d\}\times\{0,1\}^2)\), and the sample law \(P^{\otimes n}\) belongs to \(\mathcal E_{n,d,\epsilon}\) as in \(\cref{obj:def:experiment-class}\).
\item \textbf{(Dimension range.)} \(d\le c_\epsilon n\log n\).
\end{itemize}
The hybrid estimator admits a real-arithmetic implementation: there is a universal operation-count constant \(K\in\mathbb N\), \(K>0\), such that for every \(n\) and \(d\) the program reads the split-count vector, returns \(\widehat\tau_n^{\mathrm{hyb}}\) exactly, and uses at most \(K\,d\,M(n)^4\) arithmetic and comparison operations.

Moreover, there are constants \(C_\epsilon,c_\epsilon>0\) such that, whenever the four displayed conditions hold, the light-cell contribution \(\widehat T_{\mathcal L}\) satisfies
\[
E_{P^{\otimes n}}\!\left[
\left\{
\widehat T_{\mathcal L}
-
\sum_{k\in\widehat{\mathcal L}_n}\phi(q_k)
\right\}^2
\right]
\le
C_\epsilon
\left\{
\frac{1}{n}
+
\frac{d^2}{n^2(\log n)^2}
\right\}.
\]

5a873217f8a867c03a3f8a3d3458bdd8a187e6e5.title: Consistency of realized outcomes
5a873217f8a867c03a3f8a3d3458bdd8a187e6e5.body:
Let \(Y(0)\) and \(Y(1)\) denote the binary potential outcomes under control and treatment, respectively. For the observed treatment \(A\), write \(Y(A)\) for the realized potential outcome. The observed outcome satisfies
\[
Y=Y(A)\quad\text{almost surely}.
\]

675efb191c69f089ee89621f71a655d42492952f.title: Coefficient sum certificate
675efb191c69f089ee89621f71a655d42492952f.body:
Let \(M\ge 1\) be an integer and let \(z\ge 0\). Define
\[
g_M^+(z)=\sum_{j=0}^{M-2}|g_{M,j}|\,z^j .
\]
Then
\[
g_M^+(z)\le 6^M \max\{1,z^{M-2}\}.
\]

27075fbbf88a34b63f810f891375ca0bf8ae199d.title: Factorial moment variance
27075fbbf88a34b63f810f891375ca0bf8ae199d.body:
Fix \(n,d\in\mathbb N\), a single-observation law \(P\) on \(\{1,\ldots,d\}\times\{0,1\}^2\), and a category \(k\).  Let \(m_1=|I_1|\), \(M=M(n)\), \(B=B(n)\), \(p_k=P(X=k)\), let \(\widehat P_k\) be the factorial-moment polynomial estimate for category \(k\), and let
\[
\bar P_k
\]
denote the sparse factorial-polynomial mean of \(\widehat P_k\) under \(P\) with degree \(M\) and scale \(B\).  Suppose that
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Split size.)} \(m_1>0\).
\item \textbf{(Degree.)} \(M>0\).
\item \textbf{(Scale.)} \(B>0\).
\item \textbf{(Sample size.)} \(4M^2\le m_1\).
\item \textbf{(Shifted mass.)} \(p_k+4M/m_1\le B\).
\item \textbf{(Cell mass.)} \(p_k\le B\).
\end{itemize}
Then, for an iid product sequence generated by \(P\),
\[
\int \bigl(\widehat P_k-\bar P_k\bigr)^2\,dP^{\otimes\infty}
\le
8(\mathrm e+1)\bigl(B\,6^M\bigr)^2 .
\]

491258fce66b6f6bf1471fb6b559a80ece22583d.title: Off-diagonal centered covariance
491258fce66b6f6bf1471fb6b559a80ece22583d.body:
Let \(O_1,O_2,\ldots\) be iid observations with single-observation law \(P\) on
\(\{1,\ldots,d\}\times\{0,1\}^2\).  For each category \(k\), let
\(\widehat P_k\) denote the factorial-moment polynomial estimate based on
\(O_1,\ldots,O_n\), and let
\(\bar P_k\) be its sparse polynomial mean with polynomial degree \(M(n)\) and
light-cell scale \(B(n)\).

Suppose that:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Distinct categories.)} \(k\ne l\).
\item \textbf{(Positive calibration.)} The polynomial degree satisfies \(M(n)\ge 1\), and \(B(n)>0\).
\item \textbf{(Second-split size.)} \(4M(n)^2\le m_1\).
\item \textbf{(Light cells.)} The category masses satisfy \(p_k\le B(n)\) and \(p_l\le B(n)\).
\end{itemize}
Then
\[
\mathbb E\!\left[
  \left(\widehat P_k-\bar P_k\right)
  \left(\widehat P_l-\bar P_l\right)
\right]
\le
\frac{8M(n)^2}{m_1}\left\{B(n)6^{M(n)}\right\}^2 .
\]

0f6001663a9db966ee2dc7fb0fdc80b4c609a198.title: Factorial product moment
0f6001663a9db966ee2dc7fb0fdc80b4c609a198.body:
Fix \(n,d\in\mathbb N\), a probability law \(P\) on \(\{1,\ldots,d\}\times\{0,1\}^2\), a category \(k\in\{1,\ldots,d\}\), and four-cell multi-indices \(r\) and \(s\).  Write \(q_{aky}=P(X=k,A=a,Y=y)\), let \(m_1=|I_1|\), and write \(|t|=\sum_{a,y}t_{ay}\) for a multi-index \(t\).  Define the normalized factorial-moment monomial
\[
\mathfrak m_{k,t}
=
\frac{\prod_{a,y}\bigl(N^{(1)}_{aky}\bigr)_{t_{ay}}}{(m_1)_{|t|}},
\]
where \((z)_\ell\) denotes the falling factorial.  Assume:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Positive split size.)} \(m_1>0\).
\item \textbf{(Degree ordering.)} \(|r|\le |s|\).
\item \textbf{(Split-size calibration.)} \(4|s|^2\le m_1\).
\end{itemize}
Then, under the iid product law generated by \(P\),
\[
