E_{P^{\otimes n}}\!\left[\mathfrak m_{k,r}\mathfrak m_{k,s}\right]
\le
\mathrm e
\prod_{a,y} q_{aky}^{\,r_{ay}}
\prod_{a,y}\left(q_{aky}+\frac{|s|}{m_1}\right)^{s_{ay}} .
\]

acf9dd6caaad1cb0887b36a4bb8f788131f2b222.title: Factorial covariance bound
acf9dd6caaad1cb0887b36a4bb8f788131f2b222.body:
Let \(P\) be a law on the finite observed-data alphabet, let \(k\) and \(l\) be two distinct categories, and let \(\widehat P_k\) denote the factorial-moment polynomial estimate for category \(k\), with sparse factorial-polynomial mean \(\bar P_k\). With \(M(n)=\max\{2,\lfloor\alpha_0L\rfloor\}\), \(B(n)=b_0L/m_1\), and \(m_1=|I_1|\) as in \(\cref{obj:def:sample-splits}\), suppose that
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Distinct categories.)} \(k\ne l\).
\item \textbf{(Positive degree.)} \(M(n)>0\).
\item \textbf{(Positive scale.)} \(B(n)>0\).
\item \textbf{(Split size.)} \(4M(n)^2\le m_1\).
\item \textbf{(Light cells.)} \(p_k\le B(n)\) and \(p_l\le B(n)\).
\end{itemize}
Then
\[
E_{P^{\otimes n}}\left[
  \left(\widehat P_k-\bar P_k\right)
  \left(\widehat P_l-\bar P_l\right)
\right]
\le
\frac{8M(n)^2}{m_1}\left\{B(n)\,6^{M(n)}\right\}^2 .
\]

6d8a006523e36392eeafa6f27873ea9606cba229.title: Factorial variance bound
6d8a006523e36392eeafa6f27873ea9606cba229.body:
Let \(P\) be a probability law on the finite observed-data alphabet, let \(k\) be a category, and let \(\widehat P_k\) denote the factorial-moment polynomial estimate for that category, with sparse factorial-polynomial mean \(\bar P_k\). Suppose that the sample split is as in \(\cref{obj:def:sample-splits}\), and write \(m_1=|I_1|\), \(M=M(n)\), \(B=B(n)\), and \(p_k=P(X=k)\). Assume:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Nonempty split.)} \(m_1>0\).
\item \textbf{(Positive degree and scale.)} \(M>0\) and \(B>0\).
\item \textbf{(Split-size calibration.)} \(4M^2\le m_1\).
\item \textbf{(Shifted light-cell mass.)} \(p_k+4M/m_1\le B\).
\item \textbf{(Light-cell mass.)} \(p_k\le B\).
\end{itemize}
Then, for an iid sequence \(O_1,O_2,\ldots\) with one-observation law \(P\),
\[
\mathbb E\left[\left(\widehat P_k-\bar P_k\right)^2\right]
\le
8(\exp(1)+1)\left(B\,6^M\right)^2 .
\]

cb1236524026cd2696ef5077e5747024c7e91ff7.title: Factorial product moment
cb1236524026cd2696ef5077e5747024c7e91ff7.body:
Let \(n,d\in\mathbb N\), let \(P\) be a probability law on
\(\{1,\ldots,d\}\times\{0,1\}^2\), let \(k\in\{1,\ldots,d\}\), and let \(r\)
and \(s\) be multi-indices over the four treatment--outcome cells.  Use the
deterministic split of \(\cref{obj:def:sample-splits}\), write \(m_1=|I_1|\),
write \(|t|=\sum_{a,y}t_{ay}\), and set
\[
\mathfrak m_{k,t}
=
\frac{\prod_{a,y}\bigl(N^{(1)}_{aky}\bigr)_{t_{ay}}}
     {(m_1)_{|t|}},
\]
where \((z)_u\) denotes the falling factorial.  Write
\(q_{aky}=P(X=k,A=a,Y=y)\).  Assume:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Nonempty estimation split.)} \(m_1>0\).
\item \textbf{(Degree ordering.)} \(|r|\le |s|\).
\item \textbf{(Size calibration.)} \(4|s|^2\le m_1\).
\end{itemize}
Then
\[
E_{P^{\otimes n}}\!\left[\mathfrak m_{k,r}\mathfrak m_{k,s}\right]
\le\ne\,
\prod_{a,y} q_{aky}^{\,r_{ay}}
\prod_{a,y}\left(q_{aky}+\frac{|s|}{m_1}\right)^{s_{ay}} .
\]

1d6544a670867c53617018ed466422d144bd8d55.title: Pilot sandwich tail bound
1d6544a670867c53617018ed466422d144bd8d55.body:
Let \(L=\log(en)\), and let \(m_0=|I_0|\) be the pilot-split size from \(\cref{obj:def:sample-splits}\).  For a threshold \(t>0\), define
\[
\widehat{\mathcal H}=\{k:N_k^{(0)}>tL\},
\qquad
\widehat{\mathcal L}=\widehat{\mathcal H}^{c},
\qquad
B_-=\frac{tL}{2m_0},
\qquad
B_+=\frac{2tL}{m_0}.
\]
The following bounds hold.
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Arbitrary polynomial tail.)} For every \(K>0\) and every \(c>0\), there are constants \(t_0>0\), \(C>0\), and \(N\) such that, for every \(t\ge t_0\), every \(n\ge N\), every dimension \(d\) with \(d\le c n L\), every law \(P\) on \(\{1,\ldots,d\}\times\{0,1\}^2\), and every sample law satisfying \(\cref{obj:ass:iid-sampling}\),
\[
\mathbb P_{\mu_n}\left(
\widehat{\mathcal H}\not\subseteq\{k:p_k\ge B_-\}
\ \text{or}\
\widehat{\mathcal L}\not\subseteq\{k:p_k\le B_+\}
\right)
\le C n^{-K}.
\]
\item \textbf{(Fixed threshold.)} For every \(c>0\), there are constants \(C>0\) and \(N\) such that, for every \(n\ge N\), every dimension \(d\) with \(d\le c n L\), every law \(P\) on \(\{1,\ldots,d\}\times\{0,1\}^2\), and every sample law satisfying \(\cref{obj:ass:iid-sampling}\), the same sandwich event at threshold \(t=256\) obeys
\[
\mathbb P_{\mu_n}\left(
\widehat{\mathcal H}\not\subseteq\left\{k:p_k\ge \frac{256L}{2m_0}\right\}
\ \text{or}\
\widehat{\mathcal L}\not\subseteq\left\{k:p_k\le \frac{2\cdot256L}{m_0}\right\}
\right)
\le C n^{-4}.
\]
\end{itemize}

d0ce473788ea83ccb4dbafb2de37218bdc9189cd.title: Sample splits \(I_0,I_1\) and counts \(N^{(j)}_{aky}\)
d0ce473788ea83ccb4dbafb2de37218bdc9189cd.body:
For a sample \(O_1,\ldots,O_n\) with \(O_i=(X_i,A_i,Y_i)\in\{1,\ldots,d\}\times\{0,1\}\times\{0,1\}\), define
\[
I_0=\{1,\ldots,\lfloor n/2\rfloor\},\qquad
I_1=\{\lfloor n/2\rfloor+1,\ldots,n\},
\]
\[
m_j=|I_j|,\qquad L=\log(en).
\]
For each \(j\in\{0,1\}\), \(a\in\{0,1\}\), \(k\in\{1,\ldots,d\}\), and \(y\in\{0,1\}\), define the split cell count
\[
N^{(j)}_{aky}
=
\#\{i\in I_j:(A_i,X_i,Y_i)=(a,k,y)\}.
\]

e2ccfeba783a99f12752c86330aa1a2565160738.title: Hybrid estimator \(\widehat\tau_n^{\mathrm{hyb}}\)
e2ccfeba783a99f12752c86330aa1a2565160738.body:
Using the deterministic splits \(I_0,I_1\), split sizes \(m_j\), logarithmic scale \(L=\log(en)\), and split counts \(N^{(j)}_{aky}\) from \(\cref{obj:def:sample-splits}\), set
\[
A=6,\qquad \lambda_0=256,\qquad b_0=4096,
\]
\[
D_A=8\log(9A/8)=8\log(27/4),
\]
and
\[
\alpha_0=\min\left\{1,\frac1{32\log A},\frac1{256D_A}\right\}.
\]
For \(n\ge2\), define
\[
M(n)=\max\{2,\lfloor\alpha_0L\rfloor\},\qquad B(n)=b_0L/m_1.
\]
Let \(N_0\) be the least numerical cutoff such that, for every \(n\ge N_0\),
\[
\alpha_0L\ge2,\qquad 4M(n)^2\le m_1,\qquad 4M(n)/m_1\le 3B(n)/4.
\]
For \(n\ge N_0\), abbreviate \(M=M(n)\) and \(B=B(n)\), and define
\[
\widehat{\mathcal H}_n
=
\left\{k:\sum_{a,y}N^{(0)}_{aky}>\lambda_0L\right\},
\qquad
\widehat{\mathcal L}_n=\widehat{\mathcal H}_n^c.
\]
Put
\[
N_k^{(1)}=\sum_{a,y}N^{(1)}_{aky},
\qquad
N_{ak}^{(1)}=\sum_yN^{(1)}_{aky},
\]
and define the heavy-category ratio contribution
\[
\widehat h_k
=
\frac{N_k^{(1)}}{m_1}
\left\{
\frac{N^{(1)}_{1k1}}{N^{(1)}_{1k}}\mathbf1\{N^{(1)}_{1k}>0\}
-
\frac{N^{(1)}_{0k1}}{N^{(1)}_{0k}}\mathbf1\{N^{(1)}_{0k}>0\}
\right\}.
\]
Define
\[
H_M(x)=\frac{1-T_M(1-2x)}{2M^2},
\qquad
E_M(x)=\frac{H_M(x)}{x},
\qquad
G_M(x)=\frac{1-E_M(x)}{x},
\]
where \(E_M\) and \(G_M\) are interpreted by polynomial continuation at zero. For \(u=(u_{00},u_{01},u_{10},u_{11})\), set
\[
s_a(u)=u_{a0}+u_{a1},\qquad s(u)=s_0(u)+s_1(u),
\]
\[
t_1(u)=u_{11},\qquad t_0(u)=u_{01},
\]
and define the light-cell polynomial
\[
P_{M,B}(u)
=
\frac{s(u)t_1(u)}B
G_M\!\left(\frac{s_1(u)}B\right)
-
\frac{s(u)t_0(u)}B
G_M\!\left(\frac{s_0(u)}B\right).
\]
Expand
\[
P_{M,B}(u)=\sum_{|r|\le M}c_ru^r.
\]
For each category \(k\), define
\[
\widehat P_k
=
\sum_{|r|\le M}
c_r
\frac{\prod_{a,y}(N^{(1)}_{aky})_{r_{ay}}}{(m_1)_{|r|}}.
\]
The heavy and light sums are
\[
\widehat T_{\mathcal H}
=
\sum_{k\in\widehat{\mathcal H}_n}\widehat h_k,
\qquad
\widehat T_{\mathcal L}
=
\sum_{k\in\widehat{\mathcal L}_n}\widehat P_k.
\]
The truncated balanced ratio-polynomial hybrid estimator is
\[
\widehat\tau_n^{\mathrm{hyb}}
=
\max\{-1,\min(1,\widehat T_{\mathcal H}+\widehat T_{\mathcal L})\}.
\]
For \(n<N_0\), set \(\widehat{\mathcal L}_n=\varnothing\) and use the ratio branch on every category. The construction is overlap-free and is computable in \(O(dM^4)\) arithmetic operations.

6a7c8c7d3e65bd8871518728a193a249a679703e.title: Consistency of potential outcomes
6a7c8c7d3e65bd8871518728a193a249a679703e.body:
For each \(a\in\{0,1\}\), let \(Y(a)\) denote the potential outcome under treatment \(a\). The pair \(Y(0),Y(1)\) consists of the binary potential outcomes, and the realized potential outcome under the observed treatment is \(Y(A)\).

The observed outcome agrees almost surely with the realized potential outcome:
\[
Y=Y(A)\quad\text{almost surely}.
\]

7f826a8253f3560b936ec9e05460dac89ebd7576.title: Sample splits \(I_0,I_1\), sizes \(m_j\), and counts \(N^{(j)}_{aky}\)
7f826a8253f3560b936ec9e05460dac89ebd7576.body:
For a sample \(O_1,\ldots,O_n\) with observed unit \(O_i=(X_i,A_i,Y_i)\in\{1,\ldots,d\}\times\{0,1\}\times\{0,1\}\), define the deterministic half-sample splits, their sizes, and the logarithmic scale by
\[
I_0=\{1,\ldots,\lfloor n/2\rfloor\},\qquad
I_1=\{\lfloor n/2\rfloor+1,\ldots,n\},\qquad
m_j=|I_j|,\qquad
L=\log(en).
\]
For each split \(j\in\{0,1\}\), treatment arm \(a\in\{0,1\}\), category \(k\in\{1,\ldots,d\}\), and outcome \(y\in\{0,1\}\), define the split cell count by
\[
N^{(j)}_{aky}
=
\#\{i\in I_j:(A_i,X_i,Y_i)=(a,k,y)\}.
\]

b511e3f0cc8241c4a9f5477943bde73053b1e4e5.title: Centered linear MSE bound
b511e3f0cc8241c4a9f5477943bde73053b1e4e5.body:
For any \(n,d\in\mathbb N\), any overlap level \(\epsilon\in\mathbb R\), any single-observation law \(P\), and any sample law \(\mu_n\), suppose that
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Sample size.)} \(n>0\).
\item \textbf{(Experiment class.)} \(\mu_n=P^{\otimes n}\in\mathcal E_{n,d,\epsilon}\) as defined in \(\cref{obj:def:experiment-class}\).
\end{itemize}
Define
\[
\widehat\tau_{\mathrm{ctr}}(O_1,\ldots,O_n)
=
\frac1n\sum_{i=1}^n
2(2A_i-1)\left(Y_i-\frac12\right).
\]
Then, for the average treatment effect functional \(\tau(P)\) in \(\cref{obj:def:ate-functional}\),
\[
\int
\left(\widehat\tau_{\mathrm{ctr}}(o_1,\ldots,o_n)-\tau(P)\right)^2
\,d\mu_n(o_1,\ldots,o_n)
\le
\frac1n+4\left(\frac12-\epsilon\right)^2 .
\]

7c775742f61d6abe248043c3b2a60eb494b896fb.title: Heavy-cell aggregate rate
7c775742f61d6abe248043c3b2a60eb494b896fb.body:
For every overlap parameter \(\epsilon\) with \(0<\epsilon<1/2\), there exist constants
\(C_\epsilon>0\) and \(\rho_\epsilon>0\), and a sample-size cutoff
\(N_\epsilon<\infty\), such that the following holds.  For every \(n,d\), every
single-observation law \(P\in\mathsf{Prob}(\{1,\ldots,d\}\times\{0,1\}^2)\), and every
sample law \(\mu_n\) for \(O_1,\ldots,O_n\), suppose that
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Sample size.)} \(n\ge N_\epsilon\).
\item \textbf{(Dimension range.)} \(d\le \rho_\epsilon n\log n\).
\item \textbf{(Experiment class.)} \(\mu_n=P^{\otimes n}\in\mathcal E_{n,d,\epsilon}\)
for the law \(P\), as in \cref{obj:def:experiment-class}.
\end{itemize}
Then the mean squared error, under \(\mu_n\), of the heavy-cell aggregate ratio branch
\[
\widehat T_{\mathcal H}
=
\sum_{k\in\widehat{\mathcal H}_n}\widehat h_k
\]
around the pilot-heavy target
\[
\sum_{k\in\widehat{\mathcal H}_n}\phi(q_k)
\]
satisfies
\[
\int
\left(
\widehat T_{\mathcal H}
-
\sum_{k\in\widehat{\mathcal H}_n}\phi(q_k)
\right)^2
\,d\mu_n
\le
C_\epsilon\left\{
\frac{1}{n}
+
\frac{d^2}{n^2(\log n)^2}
\right\}.
\]

63085a38e8806caa1e26fbbe61aaae2c04c6b506.title: Light-cell polynomial rate
63085a38e8806caa1e26fbbe61aaae2c04c6b506.body:
Fix the overlap level \(\epsilon\) with the following conditions:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Positive overlap.)} \(0<\epsilon\).
\item \textbf{(Fixed interior.)} \(\epsilon\le 1/2\).
\item \textbf{(Experiment class.)} For every \(n,d\), every single-observation law \(P\in\mathsf{Prob}(\{1,\ldots,d\}\times\{0,1\}^2)\), and every sample law \(\mu_n\) on \(O_1,\ldots,O_n\), the condition \(\mu_n\in\mathcal E_{n,d,\epsilon}\) means exactly that \(\mu_n=P^{\otimes n}\) and the overlap condition in \(\cref{obj:def:experiment-class}\) holds for \(P\).
\item \textbf{(Dimension range.)} The dimension satisfies \(d\le c_\epsilon n\log n\).
\end{itemize}
The hybrid estimator admits a real-arithmetic implementation: there is a universal operation-count constant \(K\in\mathbb N\), \(K>0\), such that for every \(n\) and \(d\) there is a real-arithmetic program which reads the split-count vector, returns \(\widehat\tau_n^{\mathrm{hyb}}\) exactly, and uses at most \(K\,d\,M(n)^4\) arithmetic and comparison operations.

Moreover, there are constants \(C_\epsilon,c_\epsilon>0\) such that, for every \(n,d\), every \(P\in\mathsf{Prob}(\{1,\ldots,d\}\times\{0,1\}^2)\), and every \(\mu_n\in\mathcal E_{n,d,\epsilon}\) in the sense above, if \(d\le c_\epsilon n\log n\), then the light-cell contribution \(\widehat T_{\mathcal L}\) satisfies
\[
\int
\left\{
\widehat T_{\mathcal L}
-
\sum_{k\in\widehat{\mathcal L}_n}\phi(q_k)
\right\}^2
\,d\mu_n
\le
C_\epsilon
\left\{
\frac{1}{n}
+
\frac{d^2}{n^2(\log n)^2}
\right\}.
\]

c6525f5f8b1ae066bf641705cf903c48c3940354.title: Sample splits \(I_0,I_1\)
c6525f5f8b1ae066bf641705cf903c48c3940354.body:
For a sample \(O_1,\ldots,O_n\) with observed unit \(O_i=(X_i,A_i,Y_i)\in\{1,\ldots,d\}\times\{0,1\}\times\{0,1\}\), define
\[
I_0=\{1,\ldots,\lfloor n/2\rfloor\},\qquad
I_1=\{\lfloor n/2\rfloor+1,\ldots,n\},\qquad
m_j=|I_j|,\qquad
L=\log(en).
\]
For each split \(j\in\{0,1\}\), treatment arm \(a\in\{0,1\}\), category \(k\in\{1,\ldots,d\}\), and outcome \(y\in\{0,1\}\), define the split cell count by
\[
N^{(j)}_{aky}
=
\#\{i\in I_j:(A_i,X_i,Y_i)=(a,k,y)\}.
\]

60d04cf610f7457bfd27aae2590f096f13cc65ac.title: Absolute coefficient envelope
60d04cf610f7457bfd27aae2590f096f13cc65ac.body:
With \(P_{M,B}\), \(s(\cdot)\), \(c_r\), and \(u^r\) as in \(\cref{obj:def:hybrid-estimator-handle}\), write
\[
P_{M,B}(u)=\sum_r c_r u^r .
\]
For every nonnegative integer \(M\), every scale \(B>0\), and every nonnegative four-cell vector \(v\),
\[
\sum_{r\in \operatorname{supp}(P_{M,B})}|c_r|\,v^r
\le
B\,6^M
\max\left\{
\left(\frac{s(v)}{B}\right)^2,
\left(\frac{s(v)}{B}\right)^M
\right\}.
\]

744102ec959e6c9197713fd7ecdbcd414ada85d7.title: Exact factorial mean
744102ec959e6c9197713fd7ecdbcd414ada85d7.body:
Let \(d,n\in\mathbb N\), let \(P\) be a single-observation law on \(\{1,\ldots,d\}\times\{0,1\}^2\), and let \(k\) be a category. Suppose that \(n\ge N_0\), where \(N_0\) is the calibration cutoff in \(\cref{obj:def:hybrid-estimator-handle}\). With \(M=M(n)\), \(B=B(n)\), and \(\widehat P_k\) the factorial-moment polynomial estimate defined in \(\cref{obj:def:hybrid-estimator-handle}\), its exact mean under the iid product law generated by \(P\) is
\[
\int \widehat P_k(O_1,\ldots,O_n)\,dP^{\otimes n}
=
P_{M(n),B(n)}(q_k).
\]

5d57a965a3a2e5e94ade24ac643928af23ce2f37.title: Polynomial approximation certificate
5d57a965a3a2e5e94ade24ac643928af23ce2f37.body:
With the notation for \(\mathcal C_\epsilon\), \(s(u)\), \(P_{M,B}\), and \(\phi(u)\) from \cref{obj:def:overlap-cone,obj:def:hybrid-estimator-handle,obj:def:cell-functional}, let \(M\), \(B\), the overlap level \(\epsilon\), and \(u\) satisfy:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Degree.)} \(M\ge 1\).
\item \textbf{(Overlap.)} \(\epsilon>0\).
\item \textbf{(Cone membership.)} \(u\in\mathcal C_\epsilon\).
\item \textbf{(Mass bound.)} \(s(u)\le B\).
\end{itemize}
Then
\[
\left|P_{M,B}(u)-\phi(u)\right|\le \frac{2B}{\epsilon M^2}.
\]

09acc926b574cfcf0762cf1586995365e4d7ae16.title: Calibration consequences
09acc926b574cfcf0762cf1586995365e4d7ae16.body:
Let \(L=\log(en)\), let \(\ell=\log n\), and let \(m_1=|I_1|\) be the second split size from \(\cref{obj:def:sample-splits}\). Let \(M=M(n)\) and \(B=B(n)\) be the polynomial degree and light-cell approximation scale from \(\cref{obj:def:hybrid-estimator-handle}\). Suppose that
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Calibration cutoff.)} \(n\ge N_0\).
\item \textbf{(Large logarithmic scale.)} \(L\ge240\).
\end{itemize}
Then
\[
0<\ell,\qquad
\ell\le L,\qquad
L\le2\ell,\qquad
0<m_1,\qquad
n\le2m_1,\qquad
M\le L,\qquad
B\le\frac{8192L}{n},\qquad
(6^{2M})^2L^6\le n .
\]

865083bf35710e790e456d8492503b4e781fca84.title: Fixed-set residual variance
865083bf35710e790e456d8492503b4e781fca84.body:
Let \(P\) be a law on \(\{1,\ldots,d\}\times\{0,1\}^2\), and let \(O_i=(X_i,A_i,Y_i)\), \(i\in I\), be an iid \(P\)-sample indexed by a finite set \(I\). Put \(m=|I|\), \(p_k=P(X=k)\), and \(\mu_{ak}=E_P[Y\mid A=a,X=k]\). For a deterministic set \(H\subseteq\{1,\ldots,d\}\) and an arm \(a\in\{0,1\}\), define
\[
\mathcal R_a(H)
=
\sum_{k\in H}
N_k\frac{\mathbf 1\{N_{ak}>0\}}{N_{ak}}
\{N_{ak1}-\mu_{ak}N_{ak}\}.
\]
Assume:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Positive overlap.)} The overlap level satisfies \(\epsilon>0\), and every category with positive mass satisfies
\[
\epsilon\le P(A=1\mid X=k)\le 1-\epsilon .
\]
\item \textbf{(Positive mass on \(H\).)} For every \(k\in H\), \(p_k>0\).
\end{itemize}
Then
\[
E_P\!\left[\mathcal R_a(H)^2\right]
\le
\frac{2m}{\epsilon}\sum_{k\in H}p_k .
\]

9b33816fe47d35fd00439de97447544b8800035c.title: Factorial product moment
9b33816fe47d35fd00439de97447544b8800035c.body:
Fix \(n,d\in\mathbb N\), \(P\in\mathsf{Prob}(\{1,\ldots,d\}\times\{0,1\}^2)\), a category \(k\in\{1,\ldots,d\}\), and four-cell multi-indices \(r,s\). Using the split counts and split size in \(\cref{obj:def:sample-splits}\), let
\[
\mathfrak m_{k,r}
=
\frac{\prod_{(a,y)}(N^{(1)}_{aky})_{r_{ay}}}{(m_1)_{|r|}},
\]
where \((z)_t\) denotes the falling factorial and \(|r|=\sum_{(a,y)}r_{ay}\). Let \(q_{aky}\) denote the treatment--outcome cell mass in category \(k\), as in \(\cref{obj:def:ate-functional}\). Assume:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Nonempty estimation split.)} \(m_1>0\).
\item \textbf{(Degree ordering.)} \(|r|\le |s|\).
\item \textbf{(Split-size condition.)} \(4|s|^2\le m_1\).
\end{itemize}
Then, under the iid product law generated by \(P\),
\[
\mathbb E_{P^{\otimes n}}\!\left[\mathfrak m_{k,r}\mathfrak m_{k,s}\right]
\le\ne\prod_{(a,y)}q_{aky}^{\,r_{ay}}
\prod_{(a,y)}
\left(q_{aky}+\frac{|s|}{m_1}\right)^{s_{ay}} .
\]

ab5f5ade83742464538ce58bf0fd71f1ece92027.title: Missing-arm second moment
ab5f5ade83742464538ce58bf0fd71f1ece92027.body:
Let \(P\) be a probability law for one observed unit \(O=(X,A,Y)\), with \(X\in\{1,\ldots,d\}\) and \(A,Y\in\{0,1\}\). Let \(J\) be a finite index set and write \(m=|J|\). For an iid \(P\)-sample \((O_j)_{j\in J}\), a deterministic category set \(H\subseteq\{1,\ldots,d\}\), and an arm \(a\in\{0,1\}\), set
\[
Z_{ak}=N_k\mathbf 1\{N_{ak}=0\},
\qquad
N_k=\sum_{j\in J}\mathbf 1\{X_j=k\},
\qquad
N_{ak}=\sum_{j\in J}\mathbf 1\{X_j=k,A_j=a\}.
\]
Assume:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Sample size.)} \(m\ge 3\).
\item \textbf{(Overlap.)} \(P\) satisfies overlap at level \(\epsilon\), the overlap parameter, and \(\epsilon>0\).
\item \textbf{(Mass floor.)} \(B>0\) and \(p_k=P(X=k)\ge B\) for every \(k\in H\).
\end{itemize}
Then
\[
E_{P^{\otimes J}}\left[\left(\sum_{k\in H}Z_{ak}\right)^2\right]
\le
m
+
m^2
\left[
\frac{|H|}
{\left\{((m-2)/2)\epsilon\right\}^2 B}
\right]^2 .
\]

8a7409d6b86e5b664956032ded8bf94288200356.title: Coefficient sum certificate
8a7409d6b86e5b664956032ded8bf94288200356.body:
Let \(M\) be a positive integer and let \(z\ge 0\). With \(g_{M,j}\) denoting the coefficients of the polynomial continuation \(G_M\) in \cref{obj:def:hybrid-estimator-handle}, define
\[
g_M^+(z):=\sum_{0\le j<M-1}|g_{M,j}|z^j .
\]
Then
\[
g_M^+(z)\le 6^M\max\{1,z^{M-2}\}.
\]

421c0dc922e2964a504eee343832c26503f13361.title: Factorial-polynomial variance bound
421c0dc922e2964a504eee343832c26503f13361.body:
Let \(P\) be a law on the observed-data alphabet and let \(k\) be a category. With the sample splits and the calibration \(M(n)\) and \(B(n)\) defined in \cref{obj:def:sample-splits,obj:def:hybrid-estimator-handle}, write \(\widehat P_k\) for the factorial-moment polynomial estimate in \cref{obj:def:hybrid-estimator-handle} and write \(\bar P_k\) for its sparse factorial-polynomial mean.

Assume that
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Nonempty second split.)} \(m_1>0\).
\item \textbf{(Positive degree and scale.)} \(M(n)>0\) and \(B(n)>0\).
\item \textbf{(Split-size calibration.)} \(4M(n)^2\le m_1\).
\item \textbf{(Light-cell mass bounds.)} The category mass \(p_k=P(X=k)\) satisfies
\[
p_k+\frac{4M(n)}{m_1}\le B(n)
\qquad\text{and}\qquad
p_k\le B(n).
\]
\end{itemize}
Then
\[
E_{P^{\otimes n}}\!\left[\left(\widehat P_k-\bar P_k\right)^2\right]
\le
8(\mathrm e+1)\left\{B(n)6^{M(n)}\right\}^2 .
\]

102acf5fd405dfd9ec9e59ef2ad06063f568277d.title: Cross-cell factorial covariance
102acf5fd405dfd9ec9e59ef2ad06063f568277d.body:
Let \(P\) be a law on the finite observed-data alphabet, and let \(k\) and \(l\) be categories.  Define \(\bar P_k\) and \(\bar P_l\) as the sparse factorial-polynomial means of the light-cell factorial estimates \(\widehat P_k\) and \(\widehat P_l\) from \(\cref{obj:def:hybrid-estimator-handle}\).  Suppose that
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Distinct categories.)} \(k\ne l\).
\item \textbf{(Degree and scale.)} \(M(n)>0\) and \(B(n)>0\), with \(M(n)\), \(B(n)\), and \(m_1\) as in \(\cref{obj:def:sample-splits,obj:def:hybrid-estimator-handle}\).
\item \textbf{(Split size.)} \(4M(n)^2\le m_1\).
\item \textbf{(Light-cell masses.)} \(p_k\le B(n)\) and \(p_l\le B(n)\).
\end{itemize}
Then
\[
E_{P^{\otimes n}}\!\left[
  \left(\widehat P_k-\bar P_k\right)
  \left(\widehat P_l-\bar P_l\right)
\right]
\le
\frac{8M(n)^2}{m_1}\left\{B(n)6^{M(n)}\right\}^2 .
\]

cd4e7a234b00dbf3a62abc14993f5b8ef6739684.title: Coefficients \(c_r\)
cd4e7a234b00dbf3a62abc14993f5b8ef6739684.body:
For nonnegative integer \(M\) and scale \(B>0\), \(c_r\) is the coefficient of \(u^r\) in the monomial expansion of the ratio-polynomial \(P_{M,B}\) from \(\cref{obj:synth_36}\):
\[
P_{M,B}(u)=\sum_{|r|\le M} c_r u^r .
\]

c26ea13fd38332f23bec143746652e788e7a45ba.title: Consistency of potential outcomes
c26ea13fd38332f23bec143746652e788e7a45ba.body:
For each \(a\in\{0,1\}\), let \(Y(a)\) denote the potential outcome under treatment level \(a\). The observed outcome agrees almost surely with the potential outcome realized under the observed treatment:
\[
Y=Y(A)\quad\text{almost surely}.
\]

317eaf49f4288bcf74285973ec5560c2d8d97c6e.title: Factorial-moment contribution \(\widehat P_k\)
317eaf49f4288bcf74285973ec5560c2d8d97c6e.body:
For \(n\ge N_0\), set \(M=M(n)\) and \(B=B(n)\). If the ratio-polynomial has monomial expansion
\[
P_{M,B}(u)=\sum_{|r|\le M}c_ru^r,
\]
then the factorial-moment polynomial contribution for category \(k\) is
\[
\widehat P_k
=
\sum_{|r|\le M}c_r
\frac{\prod_{a,y\in\{0,1\}}(N^{(1)}_{aky})_{r_{ay}}}{(m_1)_{|r|}}.
\]

e1763e712354bc5768688ec81f37fcc5021bd732.title: Degree schedule \(M(n)\)
e1763e712354bc5768688ec81f37fcc5021bd732.body:
For \(n\ge2\), the logarithmic polynomial degree schedule is
\[
M(n)=\max\{2,\lfloor\alpha_0\log(en)\rfloor\},
\]
where
\[
\alpha_0
=
\min\left\{
1,\frac{1}{32\log 6},\frac{1}{256\cdot 8\log(27/4)}
\right\}.
\]

a3ff07559b4184af7a55b7f269e3b2c4d1f6c0be.title: Coefficients \(c_r\)
a3ff07559b4184af7a55b7f269e3b2c4d1f6c0be.body:
For a nonnegative integer \(M\) and scale \(B>0\), \(c_r\) is the coefficient of \(u^r\) in the monomial expansion of the ratio-polynomial \(P_{M,B}\):
\[
P_{M,B}(u)=\sum_{|r|\le M} c_r u^r .
\]

3e4558a5fde6633bb3959c5cd61548db45b1c630.title: Consistency of outcomes
3e4558a5fde6633bb3959c5cd61548db45b1c630.body:
The treated potential outcome is denoted by \(Y(1)\). The observed outcome agrees almost surely with the potential outcome realized under the observed treatment:
\[
Y=Y(A)\quad\text{almost surely}.
\]

aa734ca929c7429b703ebf540972349c7bb743e8.title: Centered estimator MSE bound
aa734ca929c7429b703ebf540972349c7bb743e8.body:
For every \(n,d\in\mathbb N\), every overlap parameter \(\epsilon\in\mathbb R\), every single-observation law \(P\) on the finite observed-data alphabet, and every sample law \(\mu_n\), suppose that
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Sample size.)} \(n>0\).
\item \textbf{(Experiment class.)} \(\mu_n=P^{\otimes n}\in\mathcal E_{n,d,\epsilon}\) in the sense of \cref{obj:def:experiment-class}.
\end{itemize}
Define the centered near-randomization linear estimator by
\[
\widehat\tau_{\mathrm{ctr}}(O_1,\ldots,O_n)
=
\frac1n\sum_{i=1}^n
2(2A_i-1)\left(Y_i-\frac12\right).
\]
Then, for the average treatment effect functional \(\tau(P)\) in \cref{obj:def:ate-functional},
\[
\int
\left(\widehat\tau_{\mathrm{ctr}}(o_1,\ldots,o_n)-\tau(P)\right)^2
\,d\mu_n(o_1,\ldots,o_n)
\le
\frac1n+4\left(\frac12-\epsilon\right)^2 .
\]

a57ca2db0d9e3d43239eb649e5f99d869806ed44.title: Heavy-cell ratio rate
a57ca2db0d9e3d43239eb649e5f99d869806ed44.body:
For every overlap parameter \(\epsilon\) with \(0<\epsilon<1/2\), there exist constants
\(C_\epsilon>0\) and \(\rho_\epsilon>0\), and a sample-size cutoff
\(N_\epsilon<\infty\), such that the following holds.  For every \(n,d\), every
single-observation law \(P\in\mathsf{Prob}(\{1,\ldots,d\}\times\{0,1\}^2)\), and every
sample law \(\mu_n\) for \(O_1,\ldots,O_n\), suppose that
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Sample size.)} \(n\ge N_\epsilon\).
\item \textbf{(Dimension range.)} \(d\le \rho_\epsilon n\log n\).
\item \textbf{(Experiment class.)} \(\mu_n=P^{\otimes n}\in\mathcal E_{n,d,\epsilon}\), as in
\cref{obj:def:experiment-class}.
\end{itemize}
Let
\[
\widehat T_{\mathcal H}
=
\sum_{k\in\widehat{\mathcal H}_n}\widehat h_k,
\qquad
T_{\mathcal H}(P)
=
\sum_{k\in\widehat{\mathcal H}_n}\phi(q_k).
\]
Then
\[
\int
\left(
\widehat T_{\mathcal H}
-
T_{\mathcal H}(P)
\right)^2
\,d\mu_n
\le
C_\epsilon\left\{
\frac{1}{n}
+
\frac{d^2}{n^2(\log n)^2}
\right\}.
\]

0fc84eb8cf5a829a2dbceb38525ac3a9bbfdfc06.title: Light-cell polynomial rate
0fc84eb8cf5a829a2dbceb38525ac3a9bbfdfc06.body:
Fix an overlap level \(\epsilon\) satisfying \(0<\epsilon\le 1/2\). The hybrid estimator admits a real-arithmetic implementation: there is a constant \(K\in\mathbb N\), \(K>0\), such that, for every \(n,d\), a real-arithmetic program reads the split-count vector, returns \(\widehat\tau_n^{\mathrm{hyb}}\) exactly, and uses at most \(K\,d\,M(n)^4\) arithmetic and comparison operations.

Moreover, there are constants \(C_\epsilon,c_\epsilon>0\) such that, whenever
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Sample size and dimension.)} \(n,d\in\mathbb N\).
\item \textbf{(Single-observation law.)} \(P\in\mathsf{Prob}(\{1,\ldots,d\}\times\{0,1\}^2)\).
\item \textbf{(Sample law and experiment membership.)} The sample law \(\mu_n\) is the iid product law generated by \(P\) and satisfies \(\mu_n=P^{\otimes n}\in\mathcal E_{n,d,\epsilon}\), as in \cref{obj:def:experiment-class}.
\item \textbf{(Dimension range.)} \(d\le c_\epsilon n\log n\).
\end{itemize}
the light-cell contribution \(\widehat T_{\mathcal L}\) satisfies
\[
\int
\left\{
\widehat T_{\mathcal L}(O_1,\ldots,O_n)
-
\sum_{k\in\widehat{\mathcal L}_n}\phi(q_k)
\right\}^2
\,d\mu_n
\le
C_\epsilon
\left\{
\frac{1}{n}
+
\frac{d^2}{n^2(\log n)^2}
\right\}.
\]

69ae2c45ee0274a2e6a1e522ece2a7a7f838509b.title: One-category Bernoulli lower bound
69ae2c45ee0274a2e6a1e522ece2a7a7f838509b.body:
For any positive integers \(n\) and \(d\), the minimax mean-squared-error risk \(\mathsf R_{n,d,\epsilon}\) of \cref{obj:def:minimax-risk}, evaluated at randomization \(\epsilon=1/2\), satisfies
\[
\frac{1}{100n}\le \mathsf R_{n,d,1/2}.
\]

8e705a3d885b21c8352e2a3368289e5537e7f619.title: Two-category confounding witness
8e705a3d885b21c8352e2a3368289e5537e7f619.body:
For any overlap level \(\epsilon\) satisfying \(0<\epsilon\le 1/2\), let \(P\) be the full-data law constructed in \cref{obj:def:two-category-witness}. Then \(P\) satisfies \(\cref{obj:ass:consistency,obj:ass:conditional-exchangeability,obj:ass:overlap}\). Its average treatment effect, with \(\tau(P)\) as in \cref{obj:def:ate-functional}, and its naive observed contrast are
\[
\tau(P)=\frac12,
\qquad
E_P[Y\mid A=1]-E_P[Y\mid A=0]=\epsilon .
\]

8207e3faf5ad54403b9eea03f3214d32d175fe61.title: ATE lower-bound transfer
8207e3faf5ad54403b9eea03f3214d32d175fe61.body:
Fix an overlap level \(\epsilon\) with \(0<\epsilon<1/2\). For the minimax risk \(\mathsf R_{n,d,\epsilon}\) in \(\cref{obj:def:minimax-risk}\), there exist constants \(a_\epsilon,b_\epsilon>0\) and an integer \(N_\epsilon\) such that, for every \(n,d\in\mathbb N\), if \(d>0\), \(n\ge N_\epsilon\), and
\[
d\le b_\epsilon n\log n,
\]
then
\[
\mathsf R_{n,d,\epsilon}
\ge
a_\epsilon\left\{\frac1n+\frac{d^2}{n^2(\log n)^2}\right\}.
\]

1a36efea3ecfc11acb0cdaa2355fea19ee3767bc.title: Near-randomization linear bound
1a36efea3ecfc11acb0cdaa2355fea19ee3767bc.body:
For \(n\in\mathbb N\) with \(n>0\), \(d\in\mathbb N\), a law \(P\) on \(\{1,\ldots,d\}\times\{0,1\}^2\), and a sample law \(\mu_n\), suppose that \(\mu_n\in\mathcal E_{n,d,\epsilon}\) in the sense of \(\cref{obj:def:experiment-class}\). Thus \(0<\epsilon\le 1/2\), \(\mu_n=P^{\otimes n}\), and \(P\) satisfies overlap at level \(\epsilon\). Define
\[
\widehat\tau_{\mathrm{ctr}}
=
\frac1n\sum_{i=1}^n
2(2A_i-1)\left(Y_i-\frac12\right).
\]
Then, for \(\tau(P)\) as in \(\cref{obj:def:ate-functional}\),
\[
\int
\left(\widehat\tau_{\mathrm{ctr}}(O_1,\ldots,O_n)-\tau(P)\right)^2
\,d\mu_n
\le
\frac1n+4\left(\frac12-\epsilon\right)^2 .
\]

3e6a8beccfbca4d7a73ec8d42bdf1c626f37803c.title: Randomization endpoint risk
3e6a8beccfbca4d7a73ec8d42bdf1c626f37803c.body:
Let \(n,d\in\mathbb N\) satisfy \(n>0\) and \(d>0\). For the minimax MSE risk \(\mathsf R_{n,d,\epsilon}\) defined in \(\cref{obj:def:minimax-risk}\), exact randomization satisfies
\[
\frac{1}{100n}\le \mathsf R_{n,d,1/2}\le \frac{1}{n}.
\]

a4b3451bda7aa7c816e66af32e58a33aa79950ee.title: Ambient sample marginal law
a4b3451bda7aa7c816e66af32e58a33aa79950ee.body:
Let \(P\) be a probability law on a measurable single-observation space, and let \(n\in\mathbb N\). Write \(P^{\otimes\infty}\) for the infinite product law on sequences \((O_i)_{i\ge 0}\), and write \(P^{\otimes n}\) for the finite product law on \(n\)-tuples. Then the coordinate restriction map
\[
(O_i)_{i\ge 0}\longmapsto (O_i)_{i\in\{0,\ldots,n-1\}}
\]
pushes \(P^{\otimes\infty}\) forward to \(P^{\otimes n}\):
\[
(P^{\otimes\infty})\circ\bigl((O_i)_{i\ge 0}\mapsto (O_i)_{i\in\{0,\ldots,n-1\}}\bigr)^{-1}
=
P^{\otimes n}.
\]
In particular, for the observed-data laws \(P\) used in \(\cref{obj:ass:iid-sampling}\), the initial sample segment has the \(n\)-fold product law \(P^{\otimes n}\) appearing in \(\cref{obj:def:experiment-class}\).

1b7ad0a112fdbf13ba9b1f179254f2b2224d24be.title: Pilot sandwich tail bound
1b7ad0a112fdbf13ba9b1f179254f2b2224d24be.body:
Let \(L=\log(en)\) and let \(m_0=|I_0|\) be the pilot-split size from \(\cref{obj:def:sample-splits}\).  For a threshold \(t\in\mathbb R\), define
\[
\widehat{\mathcal H}(t)=\{k:N_k^{(0)}>tL\},\qquad
\widehat{\mathcal L}(t)=\widehat{\mathcal H}(t)^c,
\]
and
\[
B_-(t)=\frac{tL}{2m_0},\qquad
B_+(t)=\frac{2tL}{m_0}.
\]
The pilot heavy/light sandwich has the following two polynomial tail guarantees.
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Arbitrary polynomial exponent.)} For every \(K>0\) and \(c>0\), there exist constants \(t_0>0\), \(C>0\), and \(N\) such that, for every \(t\ge t_0\), every \(n\ge N\), every dimension \(d\) satisfying \(d\le c\,nL\), every probability law \(P\) on \(\{1,\ldots,d\}\times\{0,1\}^2\), and every sample law \(\mu_n\) satisfying the iid sampling condition in \(\cref{obj:ass:iid-sampling}\),
\[
\mu_n\!\left(
\widehat{\mathcal H}(t)\not\subseteq\{k:p_k\ge B_-(t)\}
\;\text{or}\;
\widehat{\mathcal L}(t)\not\subseteq\{k:p_k\le B_+(t)\}
\right)
\le C n^{-K}.
\]
\item \textbf{(Fixed threshold specialization.)} For every \(c>0\), there exist constants \(C>0\) and \(N\) such that, for every \(n\ge N\), every dimension \(d\) satisfying \(d\le c\,nL\), every probability law \(P\) on \(\{1,\ldots,d\}\times\{0,1\}^2\), and every sample law \(\mu_n\) satisfying the iid sampling condition in \(\cref{obj:ass:iid-sampling}\),
\[
\mu_n\!\left(
\widehat{\mathcal H}(256)\not\subseteq\{k:p_k\ge B_-(256)\}
\;\text{or}\;
\widehat{\mathcal L}(256)\not\subseteq\{k:p_k\le B_+(256)\}
\right)
\le C n^{-4}.
\]
\end{itemize}

1e20febf4cd6be25f5d0c8626aac2c7249cdc40f.title: Combined envelope selector
1e20febf4cd6be25f5d0c8626aac2c7249cdc40f.body:
Fix constants \(\epsilon,C_\epsilon,\rho_\epsilon\in\mathbb R\) and \(N_\epsilon\in\mathbb N\). Assume:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Interior overlap.)} \(0<\epsilon<1/2\).
\item \textbf{(Positive constants.)} \(C_\epsilon>0\) and \(\rho_\epsilon>0\).
\item \textbf{(Hybrid bound.)} For every \(n,d\in\mathbb N\), if \(0<n\), \(N_\epsilon\le n\), and \(d\le \rho_\epsilon n\log n\), then the hybrid estimator \(\widehat\tau_n^{\mathrm{hyb}}\) of \cref{obj:def:hybrid-estimator-handle} satisfies
\[
\sup_{P^{\otimes n}\in\mathcal E_{n,d,\epsilon}}
\mathbb E_{P^{\otimes n}}\!\left[\left(\widehat\tau_n^{\mathrm{hyb}}-\tau(P)\right)^2\right]
\le
C_\epsilon\left\{\frac1n+\frac{d^2}{n^2(\log n)^2}\right\}.
\]
\end{itemize}
Then for every \(n,d\in\mathbb N\) with \(0<n\), \(N_\epsilon\le n\), and \(d\le \rho_\epsilon n\log n\), set
\[
K_\epsilon=\max\{C_\epsilon,4\}.
\]
Define the \(C_\epsilon,\epsilon\)-dependent selected estimator \(\widehat\tau^{\mathrm{sel}}_{C_\epsilon,\epsilon}\) to be \(\widehat\tau_n^{\mathrm{hyb}}\) when
\[
C_\epsilon\left\{\frac1n+\frac{d^2}{n^2(\log n)^2}\right\}
\le
\frac1n+4(1/2-\epsilon)^2
\]
and to be \(\widehat\tau_{\mathrm{ctr}}\) otherwise. This selected estimator satisfies
\[
\mathsf R_{n,d,\epsilon}\le
\sup_{P^{\otimes n}\in\mathcal E_{n,d,\epsilon}}
\mathbb E_{P^{\otimes n}}\!\left[\left(\widehat\tau^{\mathrm{sel}}_{C_\epsilon,\epsilon}-\tau(P)\right)^2\right]
\le
K_\epsilon\left[
\frac1n+
\min\left\{\frac{d^2}{n^2(\log n)^2},(1/2-\epsilon)^2\right\}
\right],
\]
where \(\mathsf R_{n,d,\epsilon}\) is the minimax risk of \cref{obj:def:minimax-risk}.

c895274ee2f4f7e784c6936a885b432e578cab1e.title: Sharp fixed-interior minimax rate
c895274ee2f4f7e784c6936a885b432e578cab1e.body:
Fix an overlap level \(\epsilon\) with \(0<\epsilon<1/2\).  Then there are constants
\(a_\epsilon,\rho_\epsilon,C_\epsilon>0\) and an integer \(N_\epsilon<\infty\) such that, writing
\[
r_{n,d}:=\frac1n+\frac{d^2}{n^2(\log n)^2},
\]
the following statements hold.
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Matched minimax envelope.)} For every \(n,d\), every single-observation law \(P\), and every sample law \(\mu_n\) in the experiment class \(\mathcal E_{n,d,\epsilon}\) of \(\cref{obj:def:experiment-class}\), if
\[
d>0,\qquad n\ge N_\epsilon,\qquad d\le \rho_\epsilon n\log n,
\]
then the minimax risk \(\mathsf R_{n,d,\epsilon}\) of \(\cref{obj:def:minimax-risk}\) and the truncated balanced ratio-polynomial hybrid estimator \(\widehat\tau_n^{\mathrm{hyb}}\) of \(\cref{obj:def:hybrid-estimator-handle}\) satisfy
\[
a_\epsilon r_{n,d}
\le
\mathsf R_{n,d,\epsilon}
\le
\sup_{P^{\otimes n}\in\mathcal E_{n,d,\epsilon}}
E_P\!\left[\left(\widehat\tau_n^{\mathrm{hyb}}-\tau(P)\right)^2\right]
\le
C_\epsilon r_{n,d}.
\]
\item \textbf{(Parametric interior.)} For every \(K>0\) there is a constant \(C_K>0\) such that, for every \(n,d\), every single-observation law \(P\), and every sample law \(\mu_n\) in \(\mathcal E_{n,d,\epsilon}\), if
\[
d>0,\qquad n\ge N_\epsilon,\qquad
d\le K\sqrt n\log n,\qquad
d\le \rho_\epsilon n\log n,
\]
then
\[
\frac{a_\epsilon}{n}
\le
\mathsf R_{n,d,\epsilon}
\le
\frac{C_K}{n}.
\]
\item \textbf{(Consistency threshold.)} For every pair of integer sequences \(n_j,d_j\) with \(n_j\to\infty\), \(d_j>0\) eventually, and
\[
d_j\le \rho_\epsilon n_j\log n_j
\]
eventually, the minimax risk converges to zero exactly along the sequences satisfying the vanishing normalized dimension condition:
\[
\mathsf R_{n_j,d_j,\epsilon}\to 0
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
\frac{d_j}{n_j\log n_j}\to 0.
\]
\end{itemize}

bc652e22d2529bcb32adcbba40da30c8c4e0dd0a.title: Overlap adaptive hybrid envelope
bc652e22d2529bcb32adcbba40da30c8c4e0dd0a.body:
With \(\widehat\tau_n^{\mathrm{hyb}}\) as in \(\cref{obj:def:hybrid-estimator-handle}\) and \(\mathsf R_{n,d,\epsilon}\) as in \(\cref{obj:def:minimax-risk}\), the following assertions hold.
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{Computability.} There is a universal integer \(K>0\) such that, for every \(n,d\in\mathbb N\), a real-arithmetic program based on the hybrid count input has operation count at most
\[
K\,d\,M(n)^4
\]
and, for every sample \(O_1,\ldots,O_n\), evaluates exactly to \(\widehat\tau_n^{\mathrm{hyb}}\).
\item \textbf{Fixed-overlap hybrid calibration.} For every overlap level \(\epsilon\) with \(0<\epsilon<1/2\), there are constants \(C_\epsilon,\rho_\epsilon>0\) and an integer \(N_\epsilon\) such that, for all \(n,d\in\mathbb N\) with \(n>0\), \(d>0\), \(n\ge N_\epsilon\), and
\[
d\le \rho_\epsilon n\log n,
\]
the hybrid estimator satisfies
\[
\sup_{P^{\otimes n}\in\mathcal E_{n,d,\epsilon}}
E_P\!\left[\left(\widehat\tau_n^{\mathrm{hyb}}-\tau(P)\right)^2\right]
\le
C_\epsilon\left\{\frac1n+\frac{d^2}{n^2(\log n)^2}\right\}.
\]
For the deterministic estimator
\[
\widehat\tau_{C_\epsilon,\epsilon}
=
\begin{cases}
\widehat\tau_n^{\mathrm{hyb}},
& \text{if } C_\epsilon\left\{\frac1n+\frac{d^2}{n^2(\log n)^2}\right\}
\le \frac1n+4(1/2-\epsilon)^2,\\
\widehat\tau_{\mathrm{ctr}},
& \text{otherwise,}
\end{cases}
\]
one also has
\[
\mathsf R_{n,d,\epsilon}
\le
\sup_{P^{\otimes n}\in\mathcal E_{n,d,\epsilon}}
E_P\!\left[\left(\widehat\tau_{C_\epsilon,\epsilon}-\tau(P)\right)^2\right]
\le
\max\{C_\epsilon,4\}
\left[
\frac1n+
\min\left\{
\frac{d^2}{n^2(\log n)^2},(1/2-\epsilon)^2
\right\}
\right].
\]
\item \textbf{Centered randomization bound.} For every overlap level \(\epsilon\) with \(0<\epsilon\le 1/2\) and every \(n,d\in\mathbb N\) with \(n>0\) and \(d>0\), the centered estimator
\[
\widehat\tau_{\mathrm{ctr}}
=
\frac1n\sum_{i=1}^n
2(2A_i-1)\left(Y_i-\frac12\right)
\]
satisfies
\[
\sup_{P^{\otimes n}\in\mathcal E_{n,d,\epsilon}}
E_P\!\left[\left(\widehat\tau_{\mathrm{ctr}}-\tau(P)\right)^2\right]
\le
\frac1n+4(1/2-\epsilon)^2.
\]
\item \textbf{Endpoint randomization bracket.} For every \(n,d\in\mathbb N\) with \(n>0\) and \(d>0\),
\[
\frac{1}{100n}\le \mathsf R_{n,d,1/2}\le \frac1n.
\]
\end{itemize}

81813a1dca0845bcd9202f07fa8e786ab2a9a160.title: Sparse arm expansion
81813a1dca0845bcd9202f07fa8e786ab2a9a160.body:
For any sample \(O_1,\ldots,O_n\), with each \(O_i=(X_i,A_i,Y_i)\in\{1,\ldots,d\}\times\{0,1\}^2\), and any category \(k\in\{1,\ldots,d\}\), let \(M=M(n)\) and \(B=B(n)\) be the polynomial degree and light-cell approximation scale of \(\cref{obj:def:hybrid-estimator-handle}\).  For each arm \(a\in\{0,1\}\), define
\[
\widehat A_{a,k}
=
\sum_{j=0}^{M-2}\sum_{t=0}^{j}\sum_{c\in\{0,1\}^2}
B^{-1} g_{M,j} B^{-j}\binom jt\,
\mathfrak m_{k,r^{a,c,j,t}},
\]
where \(g_{M,j}\) are the coefficients of \(G_M\), \(r^{a,c,j,t}\) is the four-cell exponent vector determined by
\(u^{r^{a,c,j,t}}=u_cu_{a1}u_{a0}^{\,t}u_{a1}^{\,j-t}\), and \(\mathfrak m_{k,r^{a,c,j,t}}\) is the corresponding normalized factorial-moment monomial computed from the sample.  Then the factorial-moment polynomial estimate for category \(k\) satisfies
\[
\widehat P_k=\widehat A_{1,k}-\widehat A_{0,k}.
\]

9602a04246ad14e024e44a59fb05d39e7a12cd28.title: Factorial mean identity
9602a04246ad14e024e44a59fb05d39e7a12cd28.body:
Let \(P\) be a probability law for one observation \(O=(X,A,Y)\) with \(X\in\{1,\ldots,d\}\) and \(A,Y\in\{0,1\}\), and let \(k\in\{1,\ldots,d\}\). Let \(P^{\otimes\infty}\) denote the ambient infinite iid product law generated by \(P\). Suppose that \(n\ge N_0\), where \(N_0\) is the calibration cutoff in \(\cref{obj:def:hybrid-estimator-handle}\). For
\[
q_k=\bigl(P(X=k,A=a,Y=y)\bigr)_{a,y\in\{0,1\}},
\]
the factorial-moment polynomial estimate \(\widehat P_k\) from \(\cref{obj:def:hybrid-estimator-handle}\), evaluated on the first \(n\) coordinates under \(P^{\otimes\infty}\), satisfies
\[
\int \widehat P_k(O_1,\ldots,O_n)\,dP^{\otimes\infty}
=
P_{M(n),B(n)}(q_k).
\]

470aab5f2dde56da966671fdd362fea56c6e38b8.title: Absolute coefficient envelope
470aab5f2dde56da966671fdd362fea56c6e38b8.body:
Let \(P_{M,B}\) be the light-cell polynomial approximation in \cref{obj:def:hybrid-estimator-handle}, and write
\[
P_{M,B}(u)=\sum_{r} c_r u^r
\]
in multi-index form over the four treatment--outcome cells. Suppose:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Degree.)} \(M\in\mathbb N\).
\item \textbf{(Scale.)} The approximation scale satisfies \(B>0\).
\item \textbf{(Evaluation vector.)} The four-cell vector \(v\) is nonnegative, so \(v_{ay}\ge 0\) for every cell \((a,y)\).
\end{itemize}
Then, with \(s(v)\) denoting the total four-cell mass from \cref{obj:def:hybrid-estimator-handle},
\[
\sum_{r\in \operatorname{supp}(P_{M,B})}|c_r|\,v^r
\le
B\,6^M\max\left\{\left(\frac{s(v)}{B}\right)^2,\left(\frac{s(v)}{B}\right)^M\right\}.
\]

cf21fdeba17c8cbacae3613485e090aa9d753a99.title: Polynomial approximation certificate
cf21fdeba17c8cbacae3613485e090aa9d753a99.body:
Fix a degree \(M\in\mathbb N\), a real scale \(B\), the overlap level \(\epsilon\), and a four-cell vector \(u\). Assume:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Degree.)} \(M\ge 1\).
\item \textbf{(Overlap level.)} \(\epsilon>0\).
\item \textbf{(Cone membership.)} \(u\in\mathcal C_\epsilon\), where \(\mathcal C_\epsilon\) is the overlap-restricted cone in \(\cref{obj:def:overlap-cone}\).
\item \textbf{(Mass bound.)} \(s(u)\le B\).
\end{itemize}
For the light-cell polynomial \(P_{M,B}\) from \(\cref{obj:def:hybrid-estimator-handle}\) and the homogeneous cell contribution \(\phi\) from \(\cref{obj:def:cell-functional}\),
\[
\left|P_{M,B}(u)-\phi(u)\right|\le \frac{2B}{\epsilon M^2}.
\]

cbb3c0c2e10e4e8eaad418c1bb2cf76401fc8d04.title: Calibration consequences
cbb3c0c2e10e4e8eaad418c1bb2cf76401fc8d04.body:
Let \(L=\log(en)\), let \(\ell=\log n\), and let \(m_1=|I_1|\) be the second split size from \(\cref{obj:def:sample-splits}\). Let \(M=M(n)\) and \(B=B(n)\) be the polynomial degree and light-cell approximation scale from \(\cref{obj:def:hybrid-estimator-handle}\). If \(n\ge N_0\) and \(L\ge240\), then
\[
0<\ell,\qquad
\ell\le L,\qquad
L\le2\ell,\qquad
0<m_1,\qquad
n\le2m_1,\qquad
M\le L,\qquad
B\le\frac{8192L}{n},\qquad
(6^{2M})^2L^6\le n .
\]

cd91f52031136116ff0d63fe45e2bd2a3abe88dd.title: Fixed-set residual variance
cd91f52031136116ff0d63fe45e2bd2a3abe88dd.body:
Let \(P\) be a probability law on the finite observed-data alphabet
\(\{1,\ldots,d\}\times\{0,1\}^2\), let \(I\) be a finite index set, and write
\(m=|I|\).  For observations \(O_i=(X_i,A_i,Y_i)\), \(i\in I\), drawn independently
from \(P\), let \(H\subseteq\{1,\ldots,d\}\) be deterministic and fix
\(a\in\{0,1\}\).

Assume:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Overlap.)} The overlap level \(\epsilon\) satisfies \(\epsilon>0\), and for every category \(k\) with \(p_k=P(X=k)>0\),
\[
\epsilon\le \pi_k\le 1-\epsilon .
\]
\item \textbf{(Positive mass on \(H\).)} For every \(k\in H\), \(p_k>0\).
\end{itemize}

With counts computed from the sample,
\[
\mathcal R_a(H)
=
\sum_{k\in H}
N_k\frac{\mathbf 1\{N_{ak}>0\}}{N_{ak}}
\left\{N_{ak1}-\mu_{ak}N_{ak}\right\}.
\]
Then
\[
E_P\!\left[\mathcal R_a(H)^2\right]
\le
\frac{2m}{\epsilon}\sum_{k\in H}p_k .
\]

0a8fb6487a7552582e30267f5374c790c4838d8e.title: Missing-arm second moment
0a8fb6487a7552582e30267f5374c790c4838d8e.body:
Let \(J\) be a finite sample-index set and write \(m=|J|\). For a probability law \(P\) on \(\{1,\ldots,d\}\times\{0,1\}^2\), a deterministic category set \(H\subseteq\{1,\ldots,d\}\), and an arm \(a\in\{0,1\}\), define
\[
Z_{ak}=N_k\mathbf 1\{N_{ak}=0\},
\]
where \(N_k\) is the number of observations in category \(k\) and \(N_{ak}\) is the number of observations in category \(k\) and arm \(a\) in the \(J\)-indexed iid sample from \(P\).

Assume:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Sample size.)} \(m\ge 3\).
\item \textbf{(Overlap.)} The overlap level \(\epsilon\) satisfies \(\epsilon>0\), and for every category \(k\) with \(p_k=P(X=k)>0\),
\[
\epsilon\le P(A=1\mid X=k)\le 1-\epsilon .
\]
\item \textbf{(Mass floor.)} \(B>0\), and \(p_k\ge B\) for every \(k\in H\).
\end{itemize}
Then
\[
\mathbb E_{P^{\otimes J}}\left[
\left(\sum_{k\in H} Z_{ak}\right)^2
\right]
\le
m+m^2
\left[
\frac{|H|}
{\left\{\left((m-2)/2\right)\epsilon\right\}^2 B}
\right]^2 .
\]

4215e054804a98e50a9057ae3bd0bb40c0a1c52b.title: Coefficient sum certificate
4215e054804a98e50a9057ae3bd0bb40c0a1c52b.body:
Let \(M\) be a positive integer and let \(z\ge 0\). With \(g_{M,j}\) denoting the coefficients of the polynomial continuation \(G_M\) from \(\cref{obj:def:hybrid-estimator-handle}\), define
\[
g_M^+(z)
=
\sum_{j\in\{0,\ldots,M-2\}} |g_{M,j}| z^j,
\]
with the sum interpreted as empty when \(M=1\). Then
\[
g_M^+(z)
\le
6^M \max\{1,z^{M\dotminus 2}\},
\]
where \(M\dotminus 2=\max\{M-2,0\}\).

95978b8c25a9e61dcc818aa7f881d84954699e34.title: Heavy-cell rate bound

0eda0ba2e0c6820edbe0ba22b56a391d779c631e.title: Factorial moment variance bound
0eda0ba2e0c6820edbe0ba22b56a391d779c631e.body:
Use the split notation and hybrid-estimator calibration in \cref{obj:def:sample-splits,obj:def:hybrid-estimator-handle}.  For any sample size \(n\), alphabet size \(d\), probability law \(P\) on the finite observed-data alphabet, and category \(k\), let \(\bar P_k\) denote the sparse factorial-polynomial mean of the light-cell statistic \(\widehat P_k\).  Suppose that
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Split size.)} \(m_1>0\).
\item \textbf{(Degree and scale.)} \(M(n)>0\) and \(B(n)>0\).
\item \textbf{(Sample-size calibration.)} \(4M(n)^2\le m_1\).
\item \textbf{(Mass envelope.)} The category mass \(p_k=P(X=k)\) satisfies
\[
p_k+\frac{4M(n)}{m_1}\le B(n)
\qquad\text{and}\qquad
p_k\le B(n).
\]
\end{itemize}
Then, under the ambient infinite iid product law \(P^{\otimes\infty}\),
\[
\int
\left(\widehat P_k-\bar P_k\right)^2
\,dP^{\otimes\infty}
\le
8(\mathrm e+1)\left(B(n)6^{M(n)}\right)^2 .
\]

7d286a45e52ec7e39428fc6984bfa8350acaae8f.title: Off-diagonal factorial covariance
7d286a45e52ec7e39428fc6984bfa8350acaae8f.body:
Use the split notation and calibration \(m_1\), \(M(n)\), and \(B(n)\) from \(\cref{obj:def:sample-splits,obj:def:hybrid-estimator-handle}\).  For each category \(k\), let \(\widehat P_k\) be the factorial-moment polynomial estimate from \(\cref{obj:def:hybrid-estimator-handle}\), computed from the first \(n\) coordinates of the ambient iid sequence, and let
\[
\bar P_k
=
\bar A_{1,k}\bigl(P,M(n),B(n)\bigr)
-
\bar A_{0,k}\bigl(P,M(n),B(n)\bigr)
\]
denote the corresponding sparse factorial-polynomial mean, written as the treated sparse-arm mean minus the control sparse-arm mean.

For any single-observation law \(P\) on \(\{1,\ldots,d\}\times\{0,1\}^2\) and any two categories \(k,l\in\{1,\ldots,d\}\), suppose that
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{Distinct categories.} \(k\ne l\).
\item \textbf{Positive calibration.} \(M(n)>0\) and \(B(n)>0\).
\item \textbf{Second-split size.} \(4M(n)^2\le m_1\).
\item \textbf{Light masses.} \(p_k\le B(n)\) and \(p_l\le B(n)\).
\end{itemize}
Then, under the ambient infinite iid product law \(P^{\otimes\infty}\),
\[
\mathbb E_{P^{\otimes\infty}}
\!\left[
\bigl(\widehat P_k-\bar P_k\bigr)
\bigl(\widehat P_l-\bar P_l\bigr)
\right]
\le
\frac{8M(n)^2}{m_1}
\left\{B(n)\,6^{M(n)}\right\}^2 .
\]

1ee6c163ae28d3286b6c1a428d86f98eb6afeb8e.title: Light-cell polynomial rate

6f77b97b63f25f1fd5114dbb67098f570f2509dc.title: Fixed overlap
6f77b97b63f25f1fd5114dbb67098f570f2509dc.body:
For the overlap level \(\epsilon\), every category \(k\) with category mass \(p_k>0\) satisfies
\[
\epsilon \le \pi_k \le 1-\epsilon .
\]

3f34c927f0902cada5b4885b30f90a245e5fe538.title: Observed-outcome consistency
3f34c927f0902cada5b4885b30f90a245e5fe538.body:
The observed outcome satisfies
\[
Y=Y(A)
\]
almost surely.

ec68b4447f162517004144731ddd7254d7d5499b.title: Conditional exchangeability
ec68b4447f162517004144731ddd7254d7d5499b.body:
The potential outcomes satisfy
\[
(Y(0),Y(1))\perp A\mid X .
\]

6b6a55be879e342c75b3c312bb686a3779d861fa.title: Experiment class \(\mathcal E_{n,d,\epsilon}\)
6b6a55be879e342c75b3c312bb686a3779d861fa.body:
For \(n,d\in\mathbb N\) and \(0<\epsilon\le 1/2\), the overlap-restricted iid experiment class is
\[
\mathcal E_{n,d,\epsilon}
:=
\left\{
P^{\otimes n}:
P\in\mathsf{Prob}(\{1,\ldots,d\}\times\{0,1\}^2)
\ \text{and } P \text{ satisfies } \cref{obj:ass:overlap}
\right\}.
\]
The law \(P^{\otimes n}\) is formed from the single-observation law in \(\cref{obj:ass:iid-sampling}\).

979ee3cd14f10f599a93bf1a4e7fe634d485dbc6.title: Overlap cone \(\mathcal C_\epsilon\)
979ee3cd14f10f599a93bf1a4e7fe634d485dbc6.body:
The overlap-restricted cone of nonnegative four-cell vectors is
\[
\mathcal C_\epsilon
:=
\left\{
u=(u_{00},u_{01},u_{10},u_{11})\in\mathbb R_+^4:
\epsilon(u_{00}+u_{01}+u_{10}+u_{11})
\le
u_{10}+u_{11}
\le
(1-\epsilon)(u_{00}+u_{01}+u_{10}+u_{11})
\right\}.
\]

bb96fc176e4b2f28e4e06cbc980792664c4fddef.title: Cell functional \(\phi(u)\)
bb96fc176e4b2f28e4e06cbc980792664c4fddef.body:
For \(u=(u_{00},u_{01},u_{10},u_{11})\in\mathcal C_\epsilon\) as in \(\cref{obj:def:overlap-cone}\), define
\[
\phi(u)
:=
\begin{cases}
(u_{00}+u_{01}+u_{10}+u_{11})
\left[
\dfrac{u_{11}}{u_{10}+u_{11}}
-
\dfrac{u_{01}}{u_{00}+u_{01}}
\right],
& u\neq(0,0,0,0),\\[1.2em]
0,
& u=(0,0,0,0).
\end{cases}
\]

2c6041c231543ae64bf9e1c8b0d1931ed4d71a79.title: Minimax risk \(\mathsf R_{n,d,\epsilon}\)

fe56f3acd65431fa6fa4b2068d0a1a246cf6b2a7.title: Coefficient envelope
fe56f3acd65431fa6fa4b2068d0a1a246cf6b2a7.body:
Let \(M\in\mathbb N\), let \(B>0\), and let \(v=(v_{00},v_{01},v_{10},v_{11})\) be a nonnegative four-cell vector. For \(a\in\{0,1\}\), write \(s_a(u)=u_{a0}+u_{a1}\), \(s(u)=s_0(u)+s_1(u)\), \(t_1(u)=u_{11}\), and \(t_0(u)=u_{01}\). Define
\[
P_{M,B}(u)
=
B^{-1}s(u)t_1(u)\sum_{0\le j<M-1} g_{M,j}\bigl(B^{-1}s_1(u)\bigr)^j
-
B^{-1}s(u)t_0(u)\sum_{0\le j<M-1} g_{M,j}\bigl(B^{-1}s_0(u)\bigr)^j .
\]
Writing \(P_{M,B}(u)=\sum_r c_r u^r\) over its finite support,
\[
\sum_r |c_r|v^r
\le
B\,6^M
\max\left\{
\left(\frac{s(v)}{B}\right)^2,
\left(\frac{s(v)}{B}\right)^M
\right\}.
\]

b82fcfd88d5299c2e792b83335d73633ed0260be.title: Sharp fixed-interior minimax rate
b82fcfd88d5299c2e792b83335d73633ed0260be.body:
Fix an overlap level \(\epsilon\), with \(0<\epsilon<1/2\).  Then there are constants \(a_\epsilon,\rho_\epsilon,C_\epsilon>0\) and an integer \(N_\epsilon<\infty\) such that the following three assertions hold.

\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Sharp fixed-interior envelope.)} For every sample size \(n\), alphabet size \(d\), and product-law member \(P^{\otimes n}\in\mathcal E_{n,d,\epsilon}\) of \(\cref{obj:def:experiment-class}\), if \(d>0\), \(n\ge N_\epsilon\), and
\[
d\le \rho_\epsilon n\log n,
\]
then, with \(\mathsf R_{n,d,\epsilon}\) as in \(\cref{obj:def:minimax-risk}\),
\[
a_\epsilon\left\{\frac1n+\frac{d^2}{n^2(\log n)^2}\right\}
\le
\mathsf R_{n,d,\epsilon}
\le
\sup_{P^{\otimes n}\in\mathcal E_{n,d,\epsilon}}
E_P\!\left[\left(\widehat\tau_n^{\mathrm{hyb}}-\tau(P)\right)^2\right]
\le
C_\epsilon\left\{\frac1n+\frac{d^2}{n^2(\log n)^2}\right\}.
\]

\item \textbf{(Parametric subrange.)} For every \(K>0\), there is a constant \(C_K>0\) such that, for every \(n\), \(d\), and product-law member \(P^{\otimes n}\in\mathcal E_{n,d,\epsilon}\), if \(d>0\), \(n\ge N_\epsilon\),
\[
d\le K\sqrt n\log n
\quad\text{and}\quad
d\le \rho_\epsilon n\log n,
\]
then
\[
\frac{a_\epsilon}{n}
\le
\mathsf R_{n,d,\epsilon}
\le
\frac{C_K}{n}.
\]

\item \textbf{(Consistency threshold.)} For any sequences \(n_j\to\infty\) and \(d_j\), if eventually \(d_j>0\) and eventually
\[
d_j\le \rho_\epsilon n_j\log n_j,
\]
then
\[
\mathsf R_{n_j,d_j,\epsilon}\to 0
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
\frac{d_j}{n_j\log n_j}\to 0.
\]
\end{itemize}

81a8ddb57fe665648e542bdbad256e86116992d7.title: Universal hybrid envelope
81a8ddb57fe665648e542bdbad256e86116992d7.body:
The following assertions hold.
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Computable universal hybrid.)} There is a constant \(K\in\mathbb N\), \(K>0\), such that for every \(n,d\in\mathbb N\) there is a real-arithmetic program, with input the split-count vector of a sample \(O_1,\ldots,O_n\), whose operation count is at most \(K\,d\,M(n)^4\) and whose output is exactly the truncated balanced ratio-polynomial hybrid estimator \(\widehat\tau_n^{\mathrm{hyb}}\). The estimator is a single rule indexed by \(n\) and \(d\).
\item \textbf{(Fixed-overlap calibration and deterministic envelope.)} For every overlap level \(\epsilon\) satisfying \(0<\epsilon<1/2\), there are constants \(C_\epsilon,\rho_\epsilon>0\) and \(N_\epsilon\in\mathbb N\) such that, for all \(n,d\in\mathbb N\) with \(n>0\), \(d>0\), \(n\ge N_\epsilon\), and
\[
d\le \rho_\epsilon n\log n,
\]
the hybrid estimator satisfies
\[
\sup_{P^{\otimes n}\in\mathcal E_{n,d,\epsilon}}
E_P\!\left[\bigl(\widehat\tau_n^{\mathrm{hyb}}-\tau(P)\bigr)^2\right]
\le
C_\epsilon\left\{\frac1n+\frac{d^2}{n^2(\log n)^2}\right\}.
\]
For the minimax risk \(\mathsf R_{n,d,\epsilon}\) in \(\cref{obj:def:minimax-risk}\), define the deterministic selector
\[
\widehat\tau_{C_\epsilon,\epsilon}
=
\begin{cases}
\widehat\tau_n^{\mathrm{hyb}},
&
C_\epsilon\left\{\dfrac1n+\dfrac{d^2}{n^2(\log n)^2}\right\}
\le
\dfrac1n+4(1/2-\epsilon)^2,\\[1.2ex]
\widehat\tau_{\mathrm{ctr}},
&
\text{otherwise}.
\end{cases}
\]
Then
\[
\mathsf R_{n,d,\epsilon}
\le
\sup_{P^{\otimes n}\in\mathcal E_{n,d,\epsilon}}
E_P\!\left[\bigl(\widehat\tau_{C_\epsilon,\epsilon}-\tau(P)\bigr)^2\right],
\]
and
\[
\sup_{P^{\otimes n}\in\mathcal E_{n,d,\epsilon}}
E_P\!\left[\bigl(\widehat\tau_{C_\epsilon,\epsilon}-\tau(P)\bigr)^2\right]
\le
\max\{C_\epsilon,4\}
\left[
\frac1n+
\min\left\{
\frac{d^2}{n^2(\log n)^2},
(1/2-\epsilon)^2
\right\}
\right].
\]
\item \textbf{(Centered endpoint bound.)} For every overlap level \(\epsilon\) satisfying \(0<\epsilon\le 1/2\) and all \(n,d\in\mathbb N\) with \(n>0\) and \(d>0\), the centered estimator
\[
\widehat\tau_{\mathrm{ctr}}
=
\frac1n\sum_{i=1}^n
2(2A_i-1)\left(Y_i-\frac12\right)
\]
satisfies
\[
\sup_{P^{\otimes n}\in\mathcal E_{n,d,\epsilon}}
E_P\!\left[\bigl(\widehat\tau_{\mathrm{ctr}}-\tau(P)\bigr)^2\right]
\le
\frac1n+4(1/2-\epsilon)^2.
\]
\item \textbf{(Exact-randomization bracket.)} For all \(n,d\in\mathbb N\) with \(n>0\) and \(d>0\),
\[
\frac{1}{100n}
\le
\mathsf R_{n,d,1/2}
\le
\frac1n.
\]
\end{itemize}

2b21326b0a0c2e1c3d178c79457cf66f517e667e.title: Sparse arm expansion
2b21326b0a0c2e1c3d178c79457cf66f517e667e.body:
For any sample \(O_i=(X_i,A_i,Y_i)\), \(i\in\{1,\ldots,n\}\), with values in \(\{1,\ldots,d\}\times\{0,1\}^2\), and any category \(k\in\{1,\ldots,d\}\), set \(M=M(n)\), the polynomial degree, and \(B=B(n)\), the bandwidth.  For each arm \(a\in\{0,1\}\), define
\[
\widehat A_{a,k}
=
\sum_{j=0}^{M-2}\sum_{t=0}^{j}\sum_{c\in\{0,1\}^2}
B^{-1}g_{M,j}B^{-j}\binom jt\,
\mathfrak m_{k,r^{a,c,j,t}} .
\]
Then the factorial-moment polynomial contribution for category \(k\) satisfies
\[
\widehat P_k=\widehat A_{1,k}-\widehat A_{0,k}.
\]

85bfa9aceb0895f073e23fa184fd4c2477dbd908.title: Exact factorial mean
85bfa9aceb0895f073e23fa184fd4c2477dbd908.body:
Let \(P\in\mathsf{Prob}(\{1,\ldots,d\}\times\{0,1\}^2)\) be a single-observation law, and let \(k\in\{1,\ldots,d\}\).  Let \(N_0\) be the calibration cutoff, i.e. the least numerical cutoff satisfying the three calibration inequalities, and suppose \(n\ge N_0\).  With \(L=\log(en)\) and \(m_1\) as in \(\cref{obj:def:sample-splits}\), set
\[
M(n)=\max\{2,\lfloor\alpha_0 L\rfloor\},
\qquad
B(n)=b_0L/m_1 .
\]
Let \(q_k\) be the four-cell vector with entries
\[
(q_k)_{ay}=P(X=k,A=a,Y=y),
\qquad a,y\in\{0,1\}.
\]
If \(\widehat P_k\) denotes the sparse factorial-polynomial contribution in \(\cref{obj:lem:sparse-arm-expansion}\), evaluated on the first \(n\) coordinates of the ambient iid sequence with law \(P^{\otimes\infty}\), then
\[
\int \widehat P_k(O_1,\ldots,O_n)\,dP^{\otimes\infty}
=
P_{M(n),B(n)}(q_k).
\]

2f307edcc48997617ef612fb21de8e5ff970d0f1.title: Missing-arm second moment
2f307edcc48997617ef612fb21de8e5ff970d0f1.body:
Let \(J\) be a finite sample-index set with \(m=|J|\), and let \(P\) be a single-observation law for \(O=(X,A,Y)\in\{1,\ldots,d\}\times\{0,1\}^2\). Let \(H\subseteq\{1,\ldots,d\}\) be deterministic and let \(a\in\{0,1\}\). Suppose that:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Sample size.)} \(m\ge 3\).
\item \textbf{(Overlap.)} For every category \(k\) with category mass \(p_k=P(X=k)>0\), the treatment probability \(\pi_k=P(A=1\mid X=k)\) satisfies
\[
\epsilon\le \pi_k\le 1-\epsilon .
\]
\item \textbf{(Positive constants.)} \(\epsilon>0\) and \(B>0\).
\item \textbf{(Mass floor.)} For every \(k\in H\), \(p_k\ge B\).
\end{itemize}
For an iid \(P\)-sample indexed by \(J\), write \(N_k\) for the category count and \(N_{ak}\) for the treatment-category count, and define
\[
Z_{ak}=N_k\mathbf 1\{N_{ak}=0\},
\qquad
u=\frac{m-2}{2}\epsilon .
\]
Then
\[
E_{P^{\otimes J}}\left[\left(\sum_{k\in H} Z_{ak}\right)^2\right]
\le
m+m^2\left(\frac{|H|}{u^2B}\right)^2 .
\]

a7cbad1455e65daa58bbcd348c3f3d9be3cb0942.title: Fixed residual variance
a7cbad1455e65daa58bbcd348c3f3d9be3cb0942.body:
Let \(P\) be a law on \(\{1,\ldots,d\}\times\{0,1\}^2\), let \(I\) be a finite index set with \(m=|I|\), and draw the iid sample \(O_i=(X_i,A_i,Y_i)\), \(i\in I\), from \(P\). Suppose that:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Overlap.)} For the overlap level \(\epsilon\), \(0<\epsilon\), and every category \(k\) with \(p_k=P(X=k)>0\),
\[
\epsilon\le \pi_k \le 1-\epsilon .
\]
\item \textbf{(Fixed set.)} \(H\subseteq\{1,\ldots,d\}\) is deterministic and satisfies \(p_k>0\) for every \(k\in H\).
\item \textbf{(Arm.)} \(a\in\{0,1\}\) is fixed.
\end{itemize}
With
\[
\mathcal R_a(H)
=
\sum_{k\in H}
N_k\frac{\mathbf 1\{N_{ak}>0\}}{N_{ak}}
\{N_{ak1}-\mu_{ak}N_{ak}\},
\]
where \(N_k\) is the category count, \(N_{ak}\) is the treatment--category count, \(N_{ak1}\) is the outcome-one treatment--category count, and \(\mu_{ak}=E_P[Y\mid A=a,X=k]\), one has
\[
E_P\!\left[\mathcal R_a(H)^2\right]
\le
\frac{2m}{\epsilon}\sum_{k\in H}p_k .
\]

953a919ba2f09d38cda63be7c576296761f8294e.title: Factorial moment variance
953a919ba2f09d38cda63be7c576296761f8294e.body:
Let \(P\) be a single-observation law on \(\{1,\ldots,d\}\times\{0,1\}^2\), let \(k\in\{1,\ldots,d\}\), and use the deterministic split sizes \(m_j=|I_j|\), polynomial degree \(M(n)\), and bandwidth \(B(n)\) from \(\cref{obj:def:sample-splits}\).  Let \(p_k=P(X=k)\).  Let \(\widehat P_k\) denote the sparse factorial-moment polynomial contribution for category \(k\), and let
\[
\bar P_k
=
\bar P_k(P,M(n),B(n))
\]
be the corresponding sparse factorial-polynomial mean, formed as the treated-arm sparse polynomial mean minus the control-arm sparse polynomial mean.

Assume that:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Nonempty second split.)} \(m_1>0\).
\item \textbf{(Positive degree and bandwidth.)} \(M(n)>0\) and \(B(n)>0\).
\item \textbf{(Split size calibration.)} \(4M(n)^2\le m_1\).
\item \textbf{(Shifted light-cell mass.)} \(p_k+4M(n)/m_1\le B(n)\).
\item \textbf{(Light-cell mass.)} \(p_k\le B(n)\).
\end{itemize}
Then, under the ambient iid product law \(P^{\otimes\infty}\),
\[
\int
\left(\widehat P_k-\bar P_k\right)^2
\,dP^{\otimes\infty}
\le
8(\mathrm e+1)\left\{B(n)6^{M(n)}\right\}^2 .
\]

2bd23440f9baf8e1b0f09933e7568f2352861281.title: Centered cross covariance
2bd23440f9baf8e1b0f09933e7568f2352861281.body:
Let \(P\) be a probability law on the finite observed-data alphabet, and let \(k\) and \(l\) be two distinct categories.  With the split-size notation \(m_1=|I_1|\) from \(\cref{obj:def:sample-splits}\), set
\[
L=\log(en),\qquad M(n)=\max\{2,\lfloor \alpha_0 L\rfloor\},\qquad B(n)=b_0L/m_1 .
\]
Let \(\widehat P_k\) and \(\widehat P_l\) be the sparse factorial-moment polynomial estimates formed from the first \(n\) coordinates of the ambient iid sample, and let \(\bar P_k\) and \(\bar P_l\) be their corresponding sparse factorial-polynomial means.

Assume:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Positive degree.)} \(M(n)>0\).
\item \textbf{(Positive bandwidth.)} \(B(n)>0\).
\item \textbf{(Split size.)} \(4M(n)^2\le m_1\).
\item \textbf{(Light categories.)} \(p_k\le B(n)\) and \(p_l\le B(n)\).
\end{itemize}
Then, under the ambient iid product law \(P^{\otimes\infty}\),
\[
\mathbb E_{P^{\otimes\infty}}
\left[
\left(\widehat P_k-\bar P_k\right)
\left(\widehat P_l-\bar P_l\right)
\right]
\le
\frac{8M(n)^2}{m_1}\left\{B(n)\,6^{M(n)}\right\}^2 .
\]

796bfb9f81c5156dfbd53c077e296c010c71965e.title: Combined upper envelope
796bfb9f81c5156dfbd53c077e296c010c71965e.body:
For the minimax risk in \cref{obj:def:minimax-risk}, fix \(0<\epsilon<1/2\) and constants \(C_\epsilon,\rho_\epsilon,N_\epsilon\) for which the fixed-interior upper bound holds. Let
\[
K_\epsilon=\max\{C_\epsilon,4\}.
\]
Suppose that:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Sample size.)} \(n\ge N_\epsilon\).
\item \textbf{(Dimension range.)} \(d\le\rho_\epsilon n\log n\).
\item \textbf{(Estimator choice.)} Choose the hybrid estimator when
\[
C_\epsilon\left\{\frac1n+\frac{d^2}{n^2\log^2 n}\right\}\le\frac1n+4(1/2-\epsilon)^2,
\]
and otherwise choose \(\widehat\tau_{\mathrm{ctr}}\).
\end{itemize}
Then the selected estimator has worst-case risk at most
\[
K_\epsilon\left[\frac1n+\min\left\{\frac{d^2}{n^2\log^2 n},(1/2-\epsilon)^2\right\}\right].
\]

9acb50f131e1e40466a1b183e161f709123bdac9.title: Chebyshev reciprocal approximation
9acb50f131e1e40466a1b183e161f709123bdac9.body:
For the cell functional \(\phi\) in \cref{obj:def:cell-functional} and the overlap cone \(\mathcal C_\epsilon\) in \cref{obj:def:overlap-cone}, fix a degree \(M\ge1\), a scale \(B\), and \(\epsilon>0\). For every \(u\in\mathcal C_\epsilon\) with \(s(u)\le B\),
\[
\left|P_{M,B}(u)-\phi(u)\right|\le\frac{2B}{\epsilon M^2}.
\]

5490ff290f6056f904bd5a909611b65e27eced48.title: Coefficient sum bound
5490ff290f6056f904bd5a909611b65e27eced48.body:
Let \(M\ge1\) and \(z\ge0\). With \(g_{M,j}\) denoting the coefficients of the polynomial continuation \(G_M\), the one-arm absolute coefficient sum
\[
g_M^+(z)=\sum_{j=0}^{M-2}|g_{M,j}|\,z^j
\]
satisfies
\[
g_M^+(z)\le 6^M\max\{1,z^{M-2}\}.
\]

12bdc144cf670e1b7e14297742fda74d4b49f399.title: Calibration consequences
12bdc144cf670e1b7e14297742fda74d4b49f399.body:
For the sample split in \cref{obj:def:sample-splits}, let \(L=\log(en)\), \(\ell=\log n\), \(M=M(n)\), \(B=B(n)\), and \(m_1=|I_1|\). Suppose that:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Sample size.)} \(n\ge N_0\).
\item \textbf{(Logarithmic scale.)} \(L\ge240\).
\end{itemize}
Then
\[
0<\ell\le L\le2\ell,\qquad 0<m_1,\qquad n\le2m_1,\qquad M\le L,\qquad B\le\frac{8192L}{n},\qquad (6^{2M})^2L^6\le n.
\]
In particular,
\[
\frac1{m_1}\le\frac2n.
\]

N_k^{(0)}.body: For observations \(O_i=(X_i,A_i,Y_i)\) indexed by a finite set \(I\), a category \(k\in\{1,\ldots,d\}\), and an arm \(a\in\{0,1\}\), the category count, the arm-specific category count, and the arm-specific outcome-one count are \[ N_k=\sum_{i\in I}\mathbf 1\{X_i=k\},\qquad N_{ak}=\sum_{i\in I}\mathbf 1\{X_i=k,A_i=a\},\qquad N_{ak1}=\sum_{i\in I}\mathbf 1\{X_i=k,A_i=a,Y_i=1\}. \] For the deterministic pilot split \(I_0\) of \cref{obj:def:sample-splits} we write \(m_0=|I_0|\) for its size and \(N_k^{(0)}=\sum_{a,y\in\{0,1\}}N^{(0)}_{aky}\) for the pilot count of category \(k\).

T_M.title: Chebyshev polynomials, falling factorials, and four-cell monomials
T_M.body: For \(M\in\mathbb N\), \(T_M\) denotes the degree-\(M\) Chebyshev polynomial of the first kind, characterized by \(T_M(\cos\theta)=\cos(M\theta)\) for every \(\theta\in\mathbb R\). For a real number \(z\) and an integer \(t\ge1\), the falling factorial is \((z)_t=z(z-1)\cdots(z-t+1)\), with \((z)_0=1\); it is applied to the split cell counts as \((N^{(1)}_{aky})_{r_{ay}}\) and to the estimation-split size as \((m_1)_{|r|}=\prod_{\ell=0}^{|r|-1}(m_1-\ell)\), the empty product being \(1\). For a four-cell vector \(u=(u_{00},u_{01},u_{10},u_{11})\) and a multi-index \(r=(r_{ay})_{a,y\in\{0,1\}}\in\mathbb N_0^4\) of total degree \(|r|=\sum_{a,y\in\{0,1\}}r_{ay}\), the monomial \(u^r\) is \(\prod_{a,y\in\{0,1\}}u_{ay}^{r_{ay}}\). For a category \(k\) and a multi-index \(r\), the normalized factorial-moment monomial is \[ \mathfrak m_{k,r} = \frac{\prod_{a,y\in\{0,1\}}(N^{(1)}_{aky})_{r_{ay}}}{(m_1)_{|r|}}. \]

A.title: Observed treatment, outcome, and potential outcomes
A.body: We write \(A\in\{0,1\}\) for the observed binary treatment, with \(A=1\) denoting treated status and \(A=0\) untreated status, and \(Y\in\{0,1\}\) for the observed binary outcome. The potential outcomes \(Y(0)\) and \(Y(1)\) are \(\{0,1\}\)-valued random variables on the same probability space as the observed variables, where \(Y(a)\) is the outcome that would be recorded under treatment level \(a\in\{0,1\}\).

\\widehat\\tau_{\\mathrm{ctr}}.title: Centered endpoint estimator $\widehat\tau_{\mathrm{ctr}}$
\\widehat\\tau_{\\mathrm{ctr}}.body: For \(n\in\mathbb N\) with \(n>0\) and observed units \(O_i=(X_i,A_i,Y_i)\in\{1,\ldots,d\}\times\{0,1\}\times\{0,1\}\), define the centered endpoint estimator by \[ \widehat\tau_{\mathrm{ctr}}(O_1,\ldots,O_n)=\frac1n\sum_{i=1}^n 2(2A_i-1)\left(Y_i-\frac12\right). \]

\\mu_n.title: Product sampling laws
\\mu_n.body: For a finite index set \(J\) and a probability law \(P\) for one observed unit \(O=(X,A,Y)\), \(P^{\otimes J}\) denotes the product law on families \((O_j)_{j\in J}\) under which the coordinates are independent and each coordinate has law \(P\). For a sample \(O_1,\ldots,O_n\) with single-observation law \(P\) on \(\{1,\ldots,d\}\times\{0,1\}\times\{0,1\}\), we write \(\mu_n=P^{\otimes n}\) for the \(n\)-fold product law of the observed sample.

g_{M,j}.title: Chebyshev reciprocal coefficients \(g_{M,j}\)
g_{M,j}.body: For an integer \(M\ge2\), we say \(g_{M,j}\), \(0\le j\le M-2\), are the Chebyshev reciprocal coefficients when they are the unique real coefficients satisfying \[\frac{1-\frac{1-T_M(1-2x)}{2M^2x}}{x}=\sum_{j=0}^{M-2}g_{M,j}x^j,\] with the left-hand side interpreted by polynomial continuation at \(x=0\), where \(T_M\) is the degree-\(M\) Chebyshev polynomial of the first kind.

\\bar\u0001P_k.title: Sparse factorial-polynomial means
\\bar\u0001P_k.body: Given a law \(P\), a category \(k\in\{1,\ldots,d\}\), a degree \(M\), and a scale \(B\), write \(q_k=(q_{0k0},q_{0k1},q_{1k0},q_{1k1})\) for the four-cell mass vector of category \(k\) under \(P\). For an arm \(a\in\{0,1\}\), the sparse-arm mean is \[ \bar A_{a,k}(P,M,B) = \frac{s(q_k)\,t_a(q_k)}{B}\,G_M\!\left(\frac{s_a(q_k)}{B}\right), \] with \(s\), \(s_a\), \(t_a\), and \(G_M\) as in \cref{obj:def:hybrid-estimator-handle}. The sparse factorial-polynomial mean of category \(k\) is the difference of the two arm means, \[ \bar P_k = P_{M,B}(q_k) = \bar A_{1,k}(P,M,B) - \bar A_{0,k}(P,M,B). \]
